- **E 正确**，因为 Lake Formation 蓝图可创建简化的自动化工作流，生成用于 ETL 加载和更新数据的 AWS Glue 爬虫、作业和触发器。这些蓝图包括数据库快照、增量数据库和日志文件摄取模式。AWS Glue 是无服务器的，可与 Amazon S3 数据湖集成，支持 ETL/流式工作负载，并且可以将 Parquet 文件写入 S3。这最符合以最少运营开销将批处理和流式源整合到 S3 中的要求。([Lake Formation blueprints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/workflows-about.html), [AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/what-is-glue.html), [Glue Parquet](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-format-parquet-home.html))

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B:** Kinesis Data Analytics 用于处理流式数据，不是稍后对暂存的 S3 数据进行一次性/临时 SQL 查询的最佳选择。Athena 是 AWS 文档中说明的、可直接对 S3 进行临时 SQL 分析的服务。([Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html))
- **C:** 自定义 Lambda 函数将记录移动到 Amazon Redshift 会增加自定义代码和运营工作量，并且会将数据暂存在 Redshift 中，而不是所需的 S3 存储桶中。AWS Glue/Lake Formation 提供托管的无服务器 ETL，可将数据加载到数据湖中。([AWS Glue](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/what-is-glue.html))
- **D:** 将 JSON 数据加载到多个 OpenSearch Service 集群不满足将处理后数据暂存在不同 S3 存储桶中的要求，并且会引入集群管理开销。Glue 将 Parquet 写入 S3 是更好的分析/数据湖模式。([Glue Parquet](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-format-parquet-home.html))

en.question: A company stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. The company must store all the data for 5 years and must delete all the data after 5 years. The company also must indefinitely keep audit logs of actions that are performed within the database. Currently, the company has automated backups configured for Aurora. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Take a manual snapshot of the DB cluster.
options.B: Create a lifecycle policy for the automated backups.
options.C: Configure automated backup retention for 5 years.
options.D: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster.
options.E: Use AWS Backup to take the backups and to keep the backups for 5 years.

en.explanation:
The best choices are **D and E**.

- **D. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster** — Aurora PostgreSQL can publish its PostgreSQL log data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. AWS states that exporting logs publishes events from the cluster's PostgreSQL log to CloudWatch Logs, and that this keeps PostgreSQL log records in highly durable storage; existing exported logs remain available according to CloudWatch Logs retention settings. This addresses the requirement to keep database audit/action logs indefinitely by configuring log export and leaving CloudWatch Logs retention unset/appropriate for indefinite retention. [Publishing Aurora PostgreSQL logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.CloudWatch.html)
- **E. Use AWS Backup to take the backups and to keep the backups for 5 years** — Native RDS/Aurora automated backup retention is not long enough for 5 years. AWS Backup backup plans support lifecycle retention: the total retention period is the number of days AWS Backup stores the resource, and a backup plan can automatically delete backups after a specified number of days (`DeleteAfterDays`). Therefore, a backup plan can retain backups for 5 years and then delete them. [Create a backup plan](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/creating-a-backup-plan.html)

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. Take a manual snapshot of the DB cluster** — A manual snapshot can preserve data, but it does not automatically enforce deletion after 5 years. Aurora documentation also notes that unlike retained automated backups, a final/manual snapshot does not expire, so this would not meet the mandatory deletion requirement without additional controls. [Retaining automated backups - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.Retaining.html)
- **B. Create a lifecycle policy for the automated backups** — Aurora/RDS automated backups use backup retention settings, not an AWS Backup-style lifecycle policy for 5-year retention. Retained automated backups expire according to the source cluster retention period. [Retaining automated backups - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.Retaining.html)
- **C. Configure automated backup retention for 5 years** — RDS automated backup retention can be set only up to **35 days**, not 5 years. [Backup retention period - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupRetention.html)

zh.question: 一家公司将数据存储在 Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster 中。该公司必须将所有数据存储 5 年，并且必须在 5 年后删除所有数据。该公司还必须无限期保留在数据库内执行的操作的审计日志。目前，该公司已为 Aurora 配置 automated backups。solutions architect 应采取哪组步骤组合来满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 对 DB cluster 拍摄 manual snapshot。
options.B: 为 automated backups 创建 lifecycle policy。
options.C: 将 automated backup retention 配置为 5 年。
options.D: 为 DB cluster 配置 Amazon CloudWatch Logs export。
options.E: 使用 AWS Backup 执行 backups，并将 backups 保留 5 年。

zh.explanation:
最佳选择是 **D 和 E**。

- **D. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch Logs export for the DB cluster** — Aurora PostgreSQL 可以将其 PostgreSQL 日志数据发布到 Amazon CloudWatch Logs。AWS 声明，导出日志会将来自 cluster 的 PostgreSQL 日志的事件发布到 CloudWatch Logs，并且这会将 PostgreSQL 日志记录保存在高持久性存储中；现有已导出的日志将根据 CloudWatch Logs retention 设置保持可用。这通过配置日志导出并将 CloudWatch Logs retention 保持未设置/适当设置为无限期保留，满足了无限期保留数据库审计/操作日志的要求。[Publishing Aurora PostgreSQL logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.CloudWatch.html)
- **E. Use AWS Backup to take the backups and to keep the backups for 5 years** — 原生 RDS/Aurora automated backup retention 对于 5 年而言不够长。AWS Backup backup plans 支持 lifecycle retention：总保留期是 AWS Backup 存储资源的天数，并且 backup plan 可以在指定天数后自动删除 backups（`DeleteAfterDays`）。因此，backup plan 可以将 backups 保留 5 年，然后删除它们。[Create a backup plan](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/creating-a-backup-plan.html)

其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. Take a manual snapshot of the DB cluster** — manual snapshot 可以保留数据，但它不会在 5 年后自动强制删除。Aurora 文档还指出，与保留的 automated backups 不同，final/manual snapshot 不会过期，因此在没有额外控制措施的情况下，这将无法满足强制删除要求。[Retaining automated backups - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.Retaining.html)
- **B. Create a lifecycle policy for the automated backups** — Aurora/RDS automated backups 使用 backup retention 设置，而不是用于 5 年保留的 AWS Backup 样式 lifecycle policy。保留的 automated backups 会根据源 cluster 的保留期过期。[Retaining automated backups - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.Retaining.html)
- **C. Configure automated backup retention for 5 years** — RDS automated backup retention 最多只能设置为 **35 days**，而不是 5 年。[Backup retention period - Amazon Relational Database Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupRetention.html)

en.question: A solutions architect is optimizing a website for an upcoming musical event. Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then will be available on demand. The event is expected to attract a global online audience. Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand streaming?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: Amazon Route 53
options.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Amazon CloudFront**

Amazon CloudFront is the best fit because it is designed to improve content delivery performance for global viewers. AWS states that CloudFront routes user requests to edge locations with the lowest latency and improves performance by reducing network hops, giving users lower latency and higher data transfer rates ([CloudFront introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)). For this specific use case, AWS also states that CloudFront supports streaming media to global viewers for both **pre-recorded files** and **live events**, including VOD formats and caching live-stream media fragments at the edge ([CloudFront use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/IntroductionUseCases.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. AWS Global Accelerator**: Global Accelerator improves application availability/performance by routing traffic over the AWS global network to optimal regional endpoints and provides static anycast IP addresses ([Global Accelerator overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)). However, it is not the AWS service specifically documented for video-on-demand and live streaming delivery/caching at edge locations.
- **C. Amazon Route 53**: Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS web service for domain registration, DNS routing, and health checking ([Route 53 overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/Welcome.html)). DNS routing alone does not provide edge caching or streaming optimization.
- **D. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration**: S3 Transfer Acceleration is for faster uploads/transfers to S3, such as customers uploading to a centralized bucket or transferring large data across continents ([S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html)). It does not optimize real-time and on-demand streaming delivery to viewers.

Therefore, **Amazon CloudFront** is the service that improves performance for both live and on-demand video streaming to a global audience.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在为即将举行的音乐活动优化一个网站。演出视频将进行实时流式传输，之后还将按需提供。预计该活动将吸引全球在线观众。哪项服务将提升实时流式传输和按需流式传输的性能？

options.A: Amazon CloudFront
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: Amazon Route 53
options.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. Amazon CloudFront**

Amazon CloudFront 是最合适的选择，因为它旨在提升面向全球观众的内容交付性能。AWS 表示，CloudFront 会将用户请求路由到延迟最低的边缘站点，并通过减少网络跃点来提升性能，为用户提供更低延迟和更高的数据传输速率（[CloudFront introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)）。对于此特定用例，AWS 还表示 CloudFront 支持向全球观众流式传输媒体，既支持**预录文件**，也支持**直播活动**，包括 VOD 格式以及在边缘缓存直播流媒体片段（[CloudFront use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/IntroductionUseCases.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. AWS Global Accelerator**：Global Accelerator 通过 AWS 全球网络将流量路由到最佳区域端点，并提供静态 anycast IP 地址，从而提升应用程序的可用性/性能（[Global Accelerator overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)）。但是，它并不是 AWS 文档中专门用于在边缘站点进行视频点播和直播流交付/缓存的服务。
- **C. Amazon Route 53**：Route 53 是一种高度可用且可扩展的 DNS Web 服务，用于域名注册、DNS 路由和运行状况检查（[Route 53 overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/Welcome.html)）。单纯的 DNS 路由不提供边缘缓存或流式传输优化。
- **D. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration**：S3 Transfer Acceleration 用于更快地上传/传输到 S3，例如客户上传到集中式存储桶或跨大陆传输大量数据（[S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html)）。它不会优化面向观众的实时和按需流式传输交付。因此，**Amazon CloudFront** 是能够为面向全球观众的直播和按需视频流式传输提升性能的服务。

en.question: A company is running a publicly accessible serverless application that uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The application’s traffic recently spiked due to fraudulent requests from botnets. Which steps should a solutions architect take to block requests from unauthorized users? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create a usage plan with an API key that is shared with genuine users only.
options.B: Integrate logic within the Lambda function to ignore the requests from fraudulent IP addresses.
options.C: Implement an AWS WAF rule to target malicious requests and trigger actions to filter them out.
options.D: Convert the existing public API to a private API. Update the DNS records to redirect users to the new API endpoint.
options.E: Create an IAM role for each user attempting to access the API. A user will assume the role when making the API call.

en.explanation:
The best choices are **A and C**.

- **A — Correct.** An API Gateway usage plan can require API keys for selected methods. AWS says a usage plan “specifies who can access” deployed API stages/methods and uses API keys to identify API clients; API keys are distributed to customers to grant access to the API ([API Gateway usage plans and API keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html)). This can stop requests that do not include a valid key. Caveat: AWS also says not to use API keys as the primary authentication/authorization mechanism; for stronger identity-based access, use IAM, Lambda authorizers, or Cognito. But among the given options, requiring a key shared only with genuine users is a valid access-filtering step.
- **C — Correct.** AWS WAF can be associated with an API Gateway stage and can allow or block requests based on rules. AWS specifically notes that AWS WAF can block requests from IP ranges, countries/regions, malicious payloads, specific user agents, bad bots, content scrapers, and can use rate-based rules; WAF rules are evaluated before other API Gateway access controls ([Use AWS WAF to protect REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html)). This directly addresses fraudulent botnet traffic.

Incorrect options:

- **B — Incorrect.** Adding filtering logic inside Lambda does not block the request before it reaches and invokes the backend. AWS WAF is described as the “first line of defense” and is evaluated before API Gateway access controls, making it the appropriate place to filter malicious web requests ([Use AWS WAF to protect REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html)).
- **D — Incorrect.** A private API is only callable from within an Amazon VPC through an interface VPC endpoint, and traffic is isolated from the public internet ([Private REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html)). Converting a publicly accessible application to a private API would prevent normal public users from accessing it via public DNS.
- **E — Incorrect.** IAM authorization can control invocation only when the API method is configured for `AWS_IAM` and callers submit signed AWS credentials; policies are attached to users, roles, or groups ([Control access to a REST API with IAM permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/permissions.html)). Creating a separate IAM role for every user attempting to access a public API is not a practical bot-blocking step and does not itself filter fraudulent requests.

zh.question: 一家公司正在运行一个可公开访问的无服务器应用程序，该应用程序使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 AWS Lambda。该应用程序的流量最近因来自僵尸网络的欺诈性请求而激增。解决方案架构师应采取哪些步骤来阻止来自未授权用户的请求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 创建一个使用计划，并配置一个仅与真实用户共享的 API 密钥。
options.B: 在 Lambda 函数中集成逻辑，以忽略来自欺诈性 IP 地址的请求。
options.C: 实施 AWS WAF 规则以针对恶意请求，并触发操作将其过滤掉。
options.D: 将现有公共 API 转换为私有 API。更新 DNS 记录，将用户重定向到新的 API 端点。
options.E: 为每个尝试访问该 API 的用户创建一个 IAM 角色。用户在发起 API 调用时将代入该角色。

zh.explanation:
最佳选择是 **A 和 C**。

- **A — 正确。** API Gateway 使用计划可以要求选定方法使用 API keys。AWS 表示，使用计划“specifies who can access”已部署的 API 阶段/方法，并使用 API keys 来识别 API 客户端；API keys 会分发给客户以授予对 API 的访问权限（[API Gateway usage plans and API keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html)）。这可以阻止不包含有效密钥的请求。注意：AWS 也表示不要将 API keys 用作主要的身份验证/授权机制；对于更强的基于身份的访问，请使用 IAM、Lambda authorizers 或 Cognito。但在给定选项中，要求使用仅与真实用户共享的密钥是一个有效的访问过滤步骤。
- **C — 正确。** AWS WAF 可以与 API Gateway 阶段关联，并且可以根据规则允许或阻止请求。AWS 特别指出，AWS WAF 可以阻止来自 IP 范围、国家/地区、恶意负载、特定用户代理、恶意机器人、内容抓取工具的请求，并且可以使用基于速率的规则；WAF 规则会在其他 API Gateway 访问控制之前进行评估（[Use AWS WAF to protect REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html)）。这直接解决了欺诈性僵尸网络流量问题。错误选项：

- **B — 错误。** 在 Lambda 内部添加过滤逻辑并不能在请求到达并调用后端之前阻止该请求。AWS WAF 被描述为“first line of defense”，并且会在 API Gateway 访问控制之前进行评估，因此它是过滤恶意 Web 请求的适当位置（[Use AWS WAF to protect REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-control-access-aws-waf.html)）。
- **D — 错误。** 私有 API 只能从 Amazon VPC 内部通过 interface VPC endpoint 调用，并且流量与公共互联网隔离（[Private REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html)）。将可公开访问的应用程序转换为私有 API 会阻止普通公共用户通过公共 DNS 访问它。
- **E — 错误。** 只有当 API 方法配置为 `AWS_IAM` 且调用者提交已签名的 AWS 凭证时，IAM 授权才能控制调用；策略附加到用户、角色或组（[Control access to a REST API with IAM permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/permissions.html)）。为每个尝试访问公共 API 的用户创建单独的 IAM role 不是一个实际可行的阻止机器人的步骤，并且它本身也不会过滤欺诈性请求。

en.question: An ecommerce company hosts its analytics application in the AWS Cloud. The application generates about 300 MB of data each month. The data is stored in JSON format. The company is evaluating a disaster recovery solution to back up the data. The data must be accessible in milliseconds if it is needed, and the data must be kept for 30 days. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
options.B: Amazon S3 Glacier
options.C: Amazon S3 Standard
options.D: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Amazon S3 Standard**

Amazon S3 Standard is the best fit because the workload is a small monthly backup dataset (about 300 MB), stored as objects such as JSON files, that must be available with **millisecond access** and retained for only **30 days**. AWS documents S3 Standard as designed for frequently accessed data with **millisecond access**, with **no minimum storage duration** and no minimum billable object size, making it simple and cost-effective for this small DR backup requirement ([S3 storage class comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)).

**Why the other options are wrong:**

- **A. Amazon OpenSearch Service** — OpenSearch is for search/analytics clusters, not the most cost-effective simple backup store. AWS notes that OpenSearch Service charges for each hour of EC2 instance use plus attached EBS storage, which is unnecessary overhead for 300 MB of backup JSON data ([OpenSearch pricing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/what-is.html)).
- **B. Amazon S3 Glacier** — S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive are archival classes; AWS states Glacier Flexible Retrieval has retrieval times of **minutes to hours**, and Deep Archive has retrieval times of **hours**. They are not available for real-time access and also have longer minimum storage durations than 30 days ([S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)).
- **D. Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL** — RDS is a managed relational database service with DB instances and database storage, which is unnecessarily complex and costly for storing a small JSON backup dataset for DR ([Creating an RDS DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CreateDBInstance.html)).

zh.question: 一家电子商务公司在 AWS Cloud 中托管其分析应用程序。该应用程序每月生成约 300 MB 的数据。数据以 JSON 格式存储。该公司正在评估一种灾难恢复解决方案来备份数据。如果需要，数据必须能在毫秒内访问，并且数据必须保留 30 天。哪种解决方案能够以最高性价比满足这些要求？

options.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
options.B: Amazon S3 Glacier
options.C: Amazon S3 Standard
options.D: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. Amazon S3 Standard**

Amazon S3 Standard 是最佳选择，因为该工作负载是一个小型月度备份数据集（约 300 MB），以 JSON 文件等对象形式存储，必须能够以 **毫秒级访问** 获取，并且仅保留 **30 天**。AWS 文档说明，S3 Standard 专为频繁访问的数据而设计，提供 **毫秒级访问**，且 **没有最短存储时长**，也没有最低计费对象大小，因此对于这个小型 DR 备份需求来说简单且具有成本效益（[S3 storage class comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。

**为什么其他选项是错误的：**

- **A. Amazon OpenSearch Service** — OpenSearch 用于搜索/分析集群，并不是最具成本效益的简单备份存储。AWS 指出，OpenSearch Service 会按每小时 EC2 实例使用量以及附加的 EBS 存储收费，对于 300 MB 的备份 JSON 数据来说是不必要的开销（[OpenSearch pricing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/what-is.html)）。
- **B. Amazon S3 Glacier** — S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 和 Deep Archive 是归档类别；AWS 表示 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 的检索时间为 **数分钟到数小时**，Deep Archive 的检索时间为 **数小时**。它们不适用于实时访问，并且最短存储时长也超过 30 天（[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。
- **D. Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL** — RDS 是一种托管关系数据库服务，包含 DB 实例和数据库存储；对于存储用于 DR 的小型 JSON 备份数据集来说，它过于复杂且成本较高（[Creating an RDS DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CreateDBInstance.html)）。

en.question: A company has a small Python application that processes JSON documents and outputs the results to an on-premises SQL database. The application runs thousands of times each day. The company wants to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a highly available solution that maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the Python code on multiple Amazon EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
options.B: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs the Python code to process the documents as they arrive in the S3 bucket. Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
options.C: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use the EBS Multi-Attach feature to attach the volume to multiple Amazon EC2 instances. Run the Python code on the EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.
options.D: Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as messages. Deploy the Python code as a container on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that is configured with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Use the container to process the SQS messages. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.** S3 can publish event notifications for **new object created** events and can send those notifications directly to an **AWS Lambda function**. Lambda is appropriate for the small Python/JSON processing workload because AWS says Lambda runs code on high-availability infrastructure and manages server/OS maintenance, capacity provisioning, automatic scaling, and logging; Lambda also automatically scales execution environments as requests increase. The results can be stored in Amazon Aurora, whose cluster storage is replicated across multiple Availability Zones and can fail over automatically with Aurora Replicas, providing high availability. Therefore, S3 + Lambda + Aurora best maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead. ([S3 Event Notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html), [AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html), [Lambda scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html), [Aurora high availability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html))

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** S3 and Aurora are suitable, but running the Python code on multiple EC2 instances requires provisioning, scaling, patching, and maintaining compute instances. Lambda better matches the requirement to minimize operational overhead because Lambda manages the compute infrastructure and automatic scaling for you. ([AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html))
- **C:** EBS volumes and EC2 instances add unnecessary infrastructure management and are not the natural scalable ingestion mechanism for object-style JSON documents. This option also uses a single Amazon RDS DB instance rather than the more highly available Aurora DB cluster architecture described in the correct option.
- **D:** SQS and ECS can be scalable, but the option specifies the **EC2 launch type**, which means tasks run on EC2-backed infrastructure. AWS documentation distinguishes this from serverless Fargate and describes EC2 Auto Scaling group capacity as self-managed EC2 instances, so this has more operational overhead than an S3-triggered Lambda function. ([Amazon ECS launch types and capacity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-launch-type-comparison.html))

zh.question: 一家公司有一个小型 Python 应用程序，用于处理 JSON 文档并将结果输出到本地 SQL 数据库。该应用程序每天运行数千次。公司希望将该应用程序迁移到 AWS Cloud。公司需要一个高可用的解决方案，以最大化可扩展性并最小化运营开销。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 JSON 文档放入 Amazon S3 bucket。在多个 Amazon EC2 实例上运行 Python 代码以处理这些文档。将结果存储在 Amazon Aurora DB cluster 中。
options.B: 将 JSON 文档放入 Amazon S3 bucket。创建一个 AWS Lambda function，在文档到达 S3 bucket 时运行 Python 代码来处理这些文档。将结果存储在 Amazon Aurora DB cluster 中。
options.C: 将 JSON 文档放入 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume。使用 EBS Multi-Attach 功能将该 volume 附加到多个 Amazon EC2 实例。在 EC2 实例上运行 Python 代码以处理这些文档。将结果存储在 Amazon RDS DB instance 上。
options.D: 将 JSON 文档作为消息放入 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue。将 Python 代码作为容器部署到配置为 Amazon EC2 launch type 的 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster 上。使用该容器处理 SQS 消息。将结果存储在 Amazon RDS DB instance 上。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。** S3 可以为 **new object created** 事件发布事件通知，并可以将这些通知直接发送到 **AWS Lambda function**。Lambda 适合小型 Python/JSON 处理工作负载，因为 AWS 表示 Lambda 在高可用性基础设施上运行代码，并管理服务器/OS 维护、容量预置、自动扩展和日志记录；随着请求增加，Lambda 还会自动扩展执行环境。结果可以存储在 Amazon Aurora 中，其 cluster storage 会跨多个 Availability Zones 复制，并且可以通过 Aurora Replicas 自动故障转移，从而提供高可用性。因此，S3 + Lambda + Aurora 最能最大化可扩展性并最小化运营开销。([S3 Event Notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html), [AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html), [Lambda scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html), [Aurora high availability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html))

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A:** S3 和 Aurora 是合适的，但在多个 EC2 实例上运行 Python 代码需要预置、扩展、修补和维护计算实例。Lambda 更符合最小化运营开销的要求，因为 Lambda 会为你管理计算基础设施和自动扩展。([AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html))
- **C:** EBS volumes 和 EC2 instances 增加了不必要的基础设施管理，并且对于对象式 JSON 文档而言，并不是天然可扩展的摄取机制。此选项还使用单个 Amazon RDS DB instance，而不是正确选项中描述的更高可用性的 Aurora DB cluster 架构。
- **D:** SQS 和 ECS 可以具备可扩展性，但该选项指定了 **EC2 launch type**，这意味着任务运行在 EC2 支撑的基础设施上。AWS 文档将其与 serverless Fargate 区分开来，并将 EC2 Auto Scaling group 容量描述为自管理的 EC2 实例，因此它比由 S3 触发的 Lambda function 具有更多运营开销。([Amazon ECS launch types and capacity providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-launch-type-comparison.html))

en.question: A company wants to use high performance computing (HPC) infrastructure on AWS for financial risk modeling. The company’s HPC workloads run on Linux. Each HPC workflow runs on hundreds of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances, is short-lived, and generates thousands of output files that are ultimately stored in persistent storage for analytics and long-term future use. The company seeks a cloud storage solution that permits the copying of on-premises data to long-term persistent storage to make data available for processing by all EC2 instances. The solution should also be a high performance file system that is integrated with persistent storage to read and write datasets and output files. Which combination of AWS services meets these requirements?

options.A: Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3
options.B: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server integrated with Amazon S3
options.C: Amazon S3 Glacier integrated with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
options.D: Amazon S3 bucket with a VPC endpoint integrated with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume

en.explanation:
The correct answer is **A. Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3**.

Amazon FSx for Lustre is designed for exactly this pattern: AWS states that it provides **high-performance file systems optimized for fast workload processing** and supports workloads including **HPC** and **financial modeling**. The same documentation says these workloads often use long-term repositories in **Amazon S3**, and that FSx for Lustre is **natively integrated with Amazon S3** for processing datasets with Lustre ([Using data repositories with Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fsx-data-repositories.html)). FSx for Lustre can link to S3 so S3 objects are presented as files, import S3 file listings, and write file system data back to S3; data repository tasks transfer data and metadata between the file system and durable S3 storage ([What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)). It is also compatible with Linux AMIs and can be mounted by EC2 instances using the Lustre client, fitting the Linux EC2 Spot fleet requirement ([What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

* **B. FSx for Windows File Server integrated with S3** — FSx for Windows File Server provides Windows file shares accessed with the **SMB** protocol and is made up of Windows file servers; it is not the Lustre high-performance parallel file system for Linux HPC, and this option does not match the native S3 data repository integration described for FSx for Lustre ([What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html)).
* **C. S3 Glacier integrated with EBS** — S3 Glacier classes are archival/long-term storage. For example, Glacier Flexible Retrieval is for archive data that does not require immediate access, and archived objects are not available for real-time access until restored; this is not a high-performance shared file system for active HPC processing ([Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)).
* **D. S3 bucket with VPC endpoint integrated with EBS gp2** — S3 plus EBS gp2 does not provide a shared high-performance POSIX file system for hundreds of EC2 instances. EBS Multi-Attach is supported only on Provisioned IOPS SSD `io1`/`io2` volumes, not gp2, and standard file systems such as XFS/EXT4 are not designed for simultaneous access by multiple EC2 instances ([Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司希望在 AWS 上使用高性能计算 (HPC) 基础设施进行金融风险建模。该公司的 HPC 工作负载运行在 Linux 上。每个 HPC 工作流都运行在数百个 Amazon EC2 Spot Instances 上，生命周期很短，并生成数千个输出文件，这些文件最终存储在持久性存储中，用于分析和长期未来使用。该公司正在寻找一种云存储解决方案，允许将本地数据复制到长期持久性存储中，以便所有 EC2 实例都可以处理这些数据。该解决方案还应是一个与持久性存储集成的高性能文件系统，用于读取和写入数据集及输出文件。哪种 AWS 服务组合满足这些要求？

options.A: 与 Amazon S3 集成的 Amazon FSx for Lustre
options.B: 与 Amazon S3 集成的 Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
options.C: 与 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 集成的 Amazon S3 Glacier
options.D: 带有 VPC 端点并与 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp2) 卷集成的 Amazon S3 存储桶

zh.explanation:
正确答案是 **A. Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3**。

Amazon FSx for Lustre 正是为这种模式而设计的：AWS 表示，它提供**针对快速工作负载处理而优化的高性能文件系统**，并支持包括 **HPC** 和**金融建模**在内的工作负载。同一文档还说明，这些工作负载通常使用 **Amazon S3** 中的长期存储库，并且 FSx for Lustre **与 Amazon S3 原生集成**，可使用 Lustre 处理数据集（[Using data repositories with Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fsx-data-repositories.html)）。FSx for Lustre 可以链接到 S3，使 S3 对象以文件形式呈现，导入 S3 文件列表，并将文件系统数据写回 S3；数据存储库任务会在文件系统和持久的 S3 存储之间传输数据和元数据（[What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)）。它还兼容 Linux AMIs，并且 EC2 实例可以使用 Lustre 客户端挂载它，符合 Linux EC2 Spot 队列的要求（[What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)）。为什么其他选项不正确：

* **B. FSx for Windows File Server integrated with S3** — FSx for Windows File Server 提供使用 **SMB** 协议访问的 Windows 文件共享，并由 Windows 文件服务器组成；它不是面向 Linux HPC 的 Lustre 高性能并行文件系统，而且该选项也不符合为 FSx for Lustre 描述的原生 S3 数据存储库集成（[What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html)）。
* **C. S3 Glacier integrated with EBS** — S3 Glacier 存储类是归档/长期存储。例如，Glacier Flexible Retrieval 用于不需要立即访问的归档数据，并且归档对象在恢复之前无法进行实时访问；这不是用于主动 HPC 处理的高性能共享文件系统（[Understanding S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。
* **D. S3 bucket with VPC endpoint integrated with EBS gp2** — S3 加 EBS gp2 无法为数百个 EC2 实例提供共享的高性能 POSIX 文件系统。EBS Multi-Attach 仅支持 Provisioned IOPS SSD `io1`/`io2` 卷，不支持 gp2，并且 XFS/EXT4 等标准文件系统并非为多个 EC2 实例同时访问而设计（[Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html)）。

en.question: A company is building a containerized application on premises and decides to move the application to AWS. The application will have thousands of users soon after it is deployed. The company is unsure how to manage the deployment of containers at scale. The company needs to deploy the containerized application in a highly available architecture that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
options.B: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Amazon EC2 launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
options.C: Store container images in a repository that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Run the containers on EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Monitor the average CPU utilization in Amazon CloudWatch. Launch new EC2 instances as needed.
options.D: Create an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that contains the container image. Launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale out EC2 instances when the average CPU utilization threshold is breached.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** Amazon ECR is the managed AWS service intended to store container images: AWS states that “Amazon ECR stores Docker images, Open Container Initiative (OCI) images, and OCI compatible artifacts in private repositories” and supports pushing/pulling images from those repositories ([Amazon ECR private images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/images.html)). For compute, Amazon ECS with **AWS Fargate** best matches the need to run containers at scale with minimal operational overhead because Fargate runs containers “without having to manage servers or clusters of Amazon EC2 instances” and removes the need to provision, configure, or scale VM clusters ([AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)). ECS Service Auto Scaling can automatically increase or decrease the desired number of ECS tasks, including with target tracking, to handle demand ([ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)); target tracking specifically increases or decreases the desired task count automatically based on a target metric value ([target tracking scaling policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/target-tracking-create-policy.html)).

**Why the other options are wrong:**

- **B:** ECS with the EC2 launch type can run containers, but it requires managing EC2 cluster capacity. This does not minimize operational overhead compared with Fargate, which avoids managing EC2 instances and VM cluster scaling ([AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)).
- **C:** Running a container repository on an EC2 instance and manually launching EC2 instances adds significant operational burden and is less managed than ECR plus ECS/Fargate.
- **D:** Baking container images into AMIs and scaling EC2 instances is not the best container deployment pattern here and still requires EC2/AMI management. It also scales instances rather than directly using ECS service task auto scaling with target tracking.

zh.question: 一家公司正在本地构建一个容器化应用程序，并决定将该应用程序迁移到 AWS。该应用程序在部署后不久将拥有数千名用户。公司不确定如何大规模管理容器部署。公司需要以一种高可用架构部署该容器化应用程序，并最大限度地减少运营开销。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 将容器镜像存储在 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 存储库中。使用采用 AWS Fargate 启动类型的 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 集群来运行容器。使用目标跟踪根据需求自动扩展。
options.B: 将容器镜像存储在 Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) 存储库中。使用采用 Amazon EC2 启动类型的 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 集群来运行容器。使用目标跟踪根据需求自动扩展。
options.C: 将容器镜像存储在运行于 Amazon EC2 实例上的存储库中。在分布于多个 Availability Zones 的 EC2 实例上运行容器。监控 Amazon CloudWatch 中的平均 CPU 利用率。根据需要启动新的 EC2 实例。
options.D: 创建一个包含容器镜像的 Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI)。在跨多个 Availability Zones 的 Auto Scaling 组中启动 EC2 实例。当平均 CPU 利用率阈值被突破时，使用 Amazon CloudWatch 警报扩展 EC2 实例。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.** Amazon ECR 是用于存储容器镜像的托管 AWS 服务：AWS 表示“Amazon ECR 将 Docker images、Open Container Initiative (OCI) images 和 OCI compatible artifacts 存储在私有存储库中”，并支持从这些存储库推送/拉取镜像（[Amazon ECR private images](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/images.html)）。对于计算，采用 **AWS Fargate** 的 Amazon ECS 最符合以最少运营开销大规模运行容器的需求，因为 Fargate 可以“无需管理服务器或 Amazon EC2 实例集群”即可运行容器，并消除了预置、配置或扩展 VM 集群的需要（[AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)）。ECS Service Auto Scaling 可以自动增加或减少 ECS 任务的期望数量，包括使用目标跟踪来处理需求（[ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)）；目标跟踪会专门根据目标指标值自动增加或减少期望任务数（[target tracking scaling policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/target-tracking-create-policy.html)）。

**为什么其他选项错误：**

- **B:** 采用 EC2 启动类型的 ECS 可以运行容器，但需要管理 EC2 集群容量。与 Fargate 相比，这并不能最大限度地减少运营开销；Fargate 避免了管理 EC2 实例和 VM 集群扩展（[AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)）。
- **C:** 在 EC2 实例上运行容器存储库并手动启动 EC2 实例会增加显著的运营负担，并且托管程度低于 ECR 加 ECS/Fargate。
- **D:** 将容器镜像烘焙到 AMI 中并扩展 EC2 实例并不是这里最佳的容器部署模式，并且仍然需要 EC2/AMI 管理。它还扩展实例，而不是直接使用带目标跟踪的 ECS 服务任务自动扩展。

en.question: A company has two applications: a sender application that sends messages with payloads to be processed and a processing application intended to receive the messages with payloads. The company wants to implement an AWS service to handle messages between the two applications. The sender application can send about 1,000 messages each hour. The messages may take up to 2 days to be processed: If the messages fail to process, they must be retained so that they do not impact the processing of any remaining messages. Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

options.A: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance running a Redis database. Configure both applications to use the instance. Store, process, and delete the messages, respectively.
options.B: Use an Amazon Kinesis data stream to receive the messages from the sender application. Integrate the processing application with the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).
options.C: Integrate the sender and processor applications with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure a dead-letter queue to collect the messages that failed to process.
options.D: Subscribe the processing application to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive notifications to process. Integrate the sender application to write to the SNS topic.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **C**.

Amazon SQS is the most operationally efficient fit for decoupling a sender from a processing application. SQS standard queues support a nearly unlimited number of `SendMessage`, `ReceiveMessage`, and `DeleteMessage` API calls, store messages redundantly across multiple AZs, and are explicitly suited for decoupling requests from background work and batching messages for future processing ([Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)). For failed processing, SQS supports dead-letter queues: source queues can target a DLQ for messages that are not processed successfully, and a redrive policy moves a message to the DLQ after it is received too many times without successful deletion ([Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html)). A DLQ isolates failed/unconsumed messages so they do not block or affect processing of remaining messages.

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A**: Running Redis on an EC2 instance requires the company to manage the instance, Redis installation, scaling, durability, backups, patching, and failure recovery. That is not as operationally efficient as a managed queue service.
- **B**: Kinesis Data Streams is intended for collecting and processing large streams of data records in real time; AWS notes that Kinesis processing is typically lightweight and real time ([What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html)). This is unnecessary complexity for a low-volume work queue with failed-message isolation.
- **D**: SNS is a fully managed publisher/subscriber notification service where publishers send messages to a topic for delivery to subscribers, often multiple subscribers across endpoints ([What is Amazon SNS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)). By itself, SNS is not the best work-queue mechanism for retaining and isolating messages that repeatedly fail processing; SQS with a DLQ directly addresses that requirement.

zh.question: 一家公司有两个应用程序：一个发送方应用程序，用于发送带有负载的消息以供处理；以及一个处理应用程序，用于接收这些带有负载的消息。该公司希望实施一项 AWS 服务来处理这两个应用程序之间的消息。发送方应用程序每小时可以发送大约 1,000 条消息。这些消息最多可能需要 2 天才能处理完成。如果消息处理失败，必须保留这些消息，以便它们不会影响任何剩余消息的处理。哪种解决方案满足这些要求并且在运营效率上最高？

options.A: 设置一个运行 Redis 数据库的 Amazon EC2 实例。配置两个应用程序都使用该实例。分别存储、处理和删除消息。
options.B: 使用 Amazon Kinesis data stream 从发送方应用程序接收消息。将处理应用程序与 Kinesis Client Library (KCL) 集成。
options.C: 将发送方应用程序和处理方应用程序与 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列集成。配置一个死信队列来收集处理失败的消息。
options.D: 将处理应用程序订阅到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题，以接收要处理的通知。将发送方应用程序集成到 SNS 主题中写入消息。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **C**。

Amazon SQS 是将发送方与处理应用程序解耦时在运营效率上最合适的选择。SQS standard queues 支持几乎无限数量的 `SendMessage`、`ReceiveMessage` 和 `DeleteMessage` API 调用，可在多个 AZs 中冗余存储消息，并且明确适用于将请求与后台工作解耦，以及对消息进行批处理以供将来处理（[Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)）。对于处理失败的情况，SQS 支持死信队列：源队列可以将未成功处理的消息发送到 DLQ，并且 redrive policy 会在一条消息被接收过多次但未成功删除后，将该消息移动到 DLQ（[Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html)）。DLQ 会隔离失败/未消费的消息，使它们不会阻塞或影响剩余消息的处理。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A**：在 EC2 实例上运行 Redis 要求公司管理该实例、Redis 安装、扩展、持久性、备份、补丁和故障恢复。这不如托管队列服务在运营效率上高。
- **B**：Kinesis Data Streams 旨在实时收集和处理大量数据记录流；AWS 指出，Kinesis 处理通常是轻量级且实时的（[What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html)）。对于具有失败消息隔离需求的低容量工作队列来说，这是不必要的复杂性。
- **D**：SNS 是一种完全托管的发布者/订阅者通知服务，发布者将消息发送到 topic 以传递给订阅者，通常是跨多个端点的多个订阅者（[What is Amazon SNS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)）。仅凭 SNS 本身，并不是用于保留和隔离反复处理失败消息的最佳工作队列机制；带有 DLQ 的 SQS 可直接满足该要求。

en.question: A solutions architect must design a solution that uses Amazon CloudFront with an Amazon S3 origin to store a static website. The company’s security policy requires that all website traffic be inspected by AWS WAF. How should the solutions architect comply with these requirements?

options.A: Configure an S3 bucket policy to accept requests coming from the AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) only.
options.B: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward all incoming requests to AWS WAF before requesting content from the S3 origin.
options.C: Configure a security group that allows Amazon CloudFront IP addresses to access Amazon S3 only. Associate AWS WAF to CloudFront.
options.D: Configure Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the S3 bucket. Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D.**

To ensure all website traffic is inspected by AWS WAF, users must be forced to access the content through CloudFront, and AWS WAF must be enabled/associated with the CloudFront distribution. AWS documentation states that AWS WAF can protect CloudFront distributions by attaching a web ACL to the distribution, and AWS WAF blocks requests before they reach the servers/origin ([CloudFront: Use AWS WAF protections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html)). For the S3 origin, CloudFront OAI can be used so the OAI accesses files on behalf of viewers and viewers cannot use Amazon S3 URLs to access files outside CloudFront ([CloudFront: Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)). Therefore, restricting S3 access to CloudFront using OAI and enabling AWS WAF on the distribution satisfies the requirement.

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A:** AWS WAF is not an identity that should be granted direct S3 bucket access. AWS WAF protects supported resources by associating a web ACL with them; for CloudFront, the web ACL is associated with the CloudFront distribution ([AWS WAF: Resources that you can protect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)).
- **B:** CloudFront is not configured to “forward requests to AWS WAF” as an origin-like hop. The supported model is to attach/associate a web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. This option also does not prevent direct access to the S3 bucket, which could bypass WAF.
- **C:** Amazon S3 buckets do not use security groups. Security groups are for resources such as EC2 network interfaces, not S3 bucket access control. Although associating AWS WAF with CloudFront is correct, this option’s S3 restriction method is invalid.

Note: AWS now recommends Origin Access Control (OAC) over OAI for new designs, but among the provided choices, **D** is the only option that both restricts direct S3 access and enables AWS WAF inspection at CloudFront.

zh.question: 解决方案架构师必须设计一个解决方案，使用 Amazon CloudFront 搭配 Amazon S3 源来存储静态网站。公司的安全策略要求所有网站流量都必须由 AWS WAF 检查。解决方案架构师应如何满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置 S3 存储桶策略，使其仅接受来自 AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) 的请求。
options.B: 配置 Amazon CloudFront，在从 S3 源请求内容之前，将所有传入请求转发到 AWS WAF。
options.C: 配置一个安全组，仅允许 Amazon CloudFront IP 地址访问 Amazon S3。将 AWS WAF 关联到 CloudFront。
options.D: 配置 Amazon CloudFront 和 Amazon S3 使用 origin access identity (OAI) 来限制对 S3 存储桶的访问。在分配上启用 AWS WAF。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D.**

为了确保所有网站流量都由 AWS WAF 检查，必须强制用户通过 CloudFront 访问内容，并且必须在 CloudFront 分配上启用/关联 AWS WAF。AWS 文档说明，AWS WAF 可以通过将 web ACL 附加到分配来保护 CloudFront 分配，并且 AWS WAF 会在请求到达服务器/源之前阻止请求（[CloudFront: Use AWS WAF protections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html)）。对于 S3 源，可以使用 CloudFront OAI，使 OAI 代表查看器访问文件，并且查看器无法使用 Amazon S3 URL 在 CloudFront 之外访问文件（[CloudFront: Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)）。因此，使用 OAI 将 S3 访问限制为 CloudFront，并在分配上启用 AWS WAF，可以满足该要求。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A:** AWS WAF 不是应被授予直接 S3 存储桶访问权限的身份。AWS WAF 通过将 web ACL 与受支持的资源关联来保护这些资源；对于 CloudFront，web ACL 与 CloudFront 分配关联（[AWS WAF: Resources that you can protect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)）。
- **B:** CloudFront 并不是以类似源的跳点方式配置为“将请求转发到 AWS WAF”。受支持的模型是将 web ACL 附加/关联到 CloudFront 分配。此选项也没有防止对 S3 存储桶的直接访问，而直接访问可能会绕过 WAF。
- **C:** Amazon S3 存储桶不使用安全组。安全组用于 EC2 网络接口等资源，而不是用于 S3 存储桶访问控制。尽管将 AWS WAF 与 CloudFront 关联是正确的，但此选项的 S3 限制方法无效。注意：AWS 现在建议在新设计中使用 Origin Access Control (OAC) 而不是 OAI，但在给定选项中，**D** 是唯一既限制直接 S3 访问又在 CloudFront 启用 AWS WAF 检查的选项。

en.question: Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution. Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?

options.A: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
options.B: Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
options.C: Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
options.D: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D. Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.**

CloudFront is the appropriate service for serving static HTML reports to millions of global users. AWS documentation states that CloudFront uses edge servers close to viewers to deliver content quickly, and that an origin server can be an **Amazon S3 bucket**. It also caches copies of files in geographically dispersed edge locations/POPs around the world, which matches the requirement for efficient global delivery of static pages at high scale ([CloudFront: how to deliver content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)). AWS also provides getting-started guidance for delivering content with CloudFront using an authenticated S3 origin and for secure static websites with an S3 origin ([Get started with CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/GettingStarted.html)).

Why the other options are wrong:

- **A. Generate presigned URLs for the files** — Presigned URLs grant **time-limited access** to S3 objects and are mainly for controlled temporary download/upload access; they do not provide global caching or CDN acceleration for millions of viewers ([S3 presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html)).
- **B. Use cross-Region replication to all Regions** — S3 Cross-Region Replication copies objects between buckets in different Regions and can help with compliance or latency for specific geographic locations, but replicating to all Regions is operationally excessive and does not provide CloudFront’s edge caching/CDN behavior ([S3 replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)).
- **C. Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53** — Route 53 geoproximity routing routes DNS traffic to resources based on the geographic location of users and resources; it does not cache or accelerate static content delivery by itself ([Route 53 geoproximity routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geoproximity.html)).

zh.question: 一个全球性活动的组织者希望将每日报告作为静态 HTML 页面发布到网上。预计这些页面会吸引来自世界各地用户的数百万次浏览。这些文件存储在一个 Amazon S3 存储桶中。一名解决方案架构师被要求设计一个高效且有效的解决方案。该解决方案架构师应采取哪项操作来实现这一目标？

options.A: 为这些文件生成预签名 URL。
options.B: 使用跨区域复制到所有区域。
options.C: 使用 Amazon Route 53 的地理邻近性功能。
options.D: 使用 Amazon CloudFront，并将 S3 存储桶作为其源站。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D. Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.**

CloudFront 是向数百万全球用户提供静态 HTML 报告的合适服务。AWS 文档指出，CloudFront 使用靠近查看者的边缘服务器来快速交付内容，并且源服务器可以是一个 **Amazon S3 bucket**。它还会在全球分散的边缘站点/POP 中缓存文件副本，这符合在高规模下高效进行全球静态页面交付的要求（[CloudFront: how to deliver content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)）。AWS 还提供了使用经过身份验证的 S3 源站通过 CloudFront 交付内容的入门指导，以及使用 S3 源站构建安全静态网站的指导（[Get started with CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/GettingStarted.html)）。其他选项错误的原因：

- **A. Generate presigned URLs for the files** — 预签名 URL 授予对 S3 对象的**限时访问**，主要用于受控的临时下载/上传访问；它们不会为数百万查看者提供全球缓存或 CDN 加速（[S3 presigned URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-presigned-url.html)）。
- **B. Use cross-Region replication to all Regions** — S3 Cross-Region Replication 会在不同区域的存储桶之间复制对象，并且可以帮助满足合规性要求或改善特定地理位置的延迟，但复制到所有区域在运维上过度复杂，并且不提供 CloudFront 的边缘缓存/CDN 行为（[S3 replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)）。
- **C. Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53** — Route 53 地理邻近性路由会根据用户和资源的地理位置将 DNS 流量路由到资源；它本身不会缓存或加速静态内容交付（[Route 53 geoproximity routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geoproximity.html)）。

en.question: A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent traffic. This application should continually process messages without any downtime. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
options.B: Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
options.C: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
options.D: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D. Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.**

The workload has a steady baseline plus unpredictable, intermittent spikes, and it **cannot be interrupted** because messages must be processed continually without downtime. Reserved Instances are appropriate for the predictable baseline because they provide significant savings compared with On-Demand pricing for matching EC2 usage ([Reserved Instances overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-reserved-instances.html)). For the unpredictable extra capacity, AWS recommends On-Demand Instances for “short-term, irregular workloads that cannot be interrupted” ([On-Demand Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-on-demand-instances.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. Spot Instances exclusively** — Spot can be cheaper, but AWS says Spot Instances are suitable only if applications can be interrupted; EC2 can interrupt Spot Instances when it needs capacity back ([Spot Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html), [Spot Instance interruptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-interruptions.html)). This conflicts with the no-downtime requirement.
- **B. Reserved Instances exclusively for maximum capacity** — This would meet availability better than Spot, but it is not cost-effective for unpredictable intermittent peaks because Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment and are billed/committed regardless of actual use ([Reserved Instances overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-reserved-instances.html)).
- **C. Reserved baseline + Spot for additional capacity** — This is cheaper than On-Demand for bursts, but Spot capacity runs only when capacity is available and can be interrupted by Amazon EC2 ([Spot Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html)). Therefore it does not best satisfy “continually process messages without any downtime.”

zh.question: 一家公司在一组 Amazon EC2 实例上运行生产应用程序。该应用程序从 Amazon SQS 队列读取数据，并并行处理消息。消息量不可预测，并且经常出现间歇性流量。该应用程序应持续处理消息，不能有任何停机时间。哪种解决方案能以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 仅使用 Spot Instances 来处理所需的最大容量。
options.B: 仅使用 Reserved Instances 来处理所需的最大容量。
options.C: 使用 Reserved Instances 处理基准容量，并使用 Spot Instances 处理额外容量。
options.D: 使用 Reserved Instances 处理基准容量，并使用 On-Demand Instances 处理额外容量。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D. Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.**

该工作负载具有稳定的基准容量，以及不可预测的间歇性峰值，并且它**不能被中断**，因为消息必须持续处理且不能停机。Reserved Instances 适用于可预测的基准容量，因为对于匹配的 EC2 使用量，与 On-Demand 定价相比，它们可提供显著节省（[Reserved Instances overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-reserved-instances.html)）。对于不可预测的额外容量，AWS 建议将 On-Demand Instances 用于“不能被中断的短期、不规则工作负载”（[On-Demand Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-on-demand-instances.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. Spot Instances exclusively** — Spot 可能更便宜，但 AWS 表示 Spot Instances 仅适用于应用程序可以被中断的情况；当 EC2 需要收回容量时，可以中断 Spot Instances（[Spot Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html)，[Spot Instance interruptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-interruptions.html)）。这与无停机时间要求相冲突。
- **B. Reserved Instances exclusively for maximum capacity** — 这会比 Spot 更好地满足可用性，但对于不可预测的间歇性峰值而言并不具成本效益，因为 Reserved Instances 需要 1 年或 3 年承诺，并且无论实际使用量如何都会计费/承诺（[Reserved Instances overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-reserved-instances.html)）。
- **C. Reserved baseline + Spot for additional capacity** — 对于突发流量，这比 On-Demand 更便宜，但 Spot 容量只有在容量可用时才运行，并且可能被 Amazon EC2 中断（[Spot Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html)）。因此，它不能最好地满足“持续处理消息且没有任何停机时间”的要求。

en.question: A security team wants to limit access to specific services or actions in all of the team’s AWS accounts. All accounts belong to a large organization in AWS Organizations. The solution must be scalable and there must be a single point where permissions can be maintained. What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

options.A: Create an ACL to provide access to the services or actions.
options.B: Create a security group to allow accounts and attach it to user groups.
options.C: Create cross-account roles in each account to deny access to the services or actions.
options.D: Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **D**. In AWS Organizations, **service control policies (SCPs)** are organization policies used to manage permissions centrally. AWS states that SCPs “offer central control over the maximum available permissions” for IAM users and roles in the organization, and that they define permission guardrails or limits on what actions those principals can perform ([AWS Organizations SCPs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)). AWS also states that if a permission is explicitly denied by an applicable SCP, users or roles in affected member accounts cannot use that permission even if an administrator grants broad IAM permissions ([SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)). Attaching a deny-based SCP at the root applies the guardrail through the organization hierarchy to member accounts, giving the security team a scalable single point of control.

Why the other options are incorrect:
- **A**: ACLs are not the AWS Organizations mechanism for centrally limiting services/actions across all accounts. SCPs are the documented organization-level permission guardrail.
- **B**: Security groups control network traffic for resources such as EC2 instances; they do not attach to user groups or centrally deny AWS service actions across accounts.
- **C**: Cross-account roles are used to grant assumable access between accounts, not to provide a scalable, centralized denial mechanism across an AWS Organization. Managing roles in every account would also not meet the single-point-of-maintenance requirement.

zh.question: 安全团队希望在该团队的所有 AWS 账户中限制对特定服务或操作的访问。所有账户都属于 AWS Organizations 中的一个大型组织。该解决方案必须具有可扩展性，并且必须有一个可以维护权限的单一位置。解决方案架构师应如何实现这一目标？

options.A: 创建 ACL 以提供对这些服务或操作的访问权限。
options.B: 创建安全组以允许账户访问，并将其附加到用户组。
options.C: 在每个账户中创建跨账户角色，以拒绝对这些服务或操作的访问。
options.D: 在根组织单元中创建服务控制策略，以拒绝对这些服务或操作的访问。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **D**。在 AWS Organizations 中，**service control policies (SCPs)** 是用于集中管理权限的组织策略。AWS 表示，SCPs 为组织中的 IAM users 和 roles “offer central control over the maximum available permissions”，并且它们定义权限防护栏或限制，以限定这些主体可以执行哪些操作（[AWS Organizations SCPs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)）。AWS 还表示，如果某项权限被适用的 SCP 明确拒绝，则受影响成员账户中的用户或角色即使由管理员授予了宽泛的 IAM 权限，也无法使用该权限（[SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)）。在根位置附加基于拒绝的 SCP 会通过组织层级结构将防护栏应用到成员账户，从而为安全团队提供可扩展的单一控制点。其他选项不正确的原因：
- **A**：ACLs 不是 AWS Organizations 中用于跨所有账户集中限制服务/操作的机制。SCPs 才是文档中说明的组织级权限防护栏。
- **B**：安全组控制 EC2 实例等资源的网络流量；它们不会附加到用户组，也不能跨账户集中拒绝 AWS 服务操作。
- **C**：跨账户角色用于在账户之间授予可代入的访问权限，而不是在 AWS Organization 中提供可扩展的集中式拒绝机制。在每个账户中管理角色也不满足单点维护的要求。

en.question: A company is concerned about the security of its public web application due to recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect must reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the application. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.
options.B: Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.
options.C: Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
options.D: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.**

AWS documentation states that AWS Shield Standard and AWS Shield Advanced provide protection against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks for AWS resources at layers 3, 4, and 7, and that customers can subscribe to Shield Advanced for higher levels of protection ([How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-overview.html)). Shield Advanced specifically provides expanded DDoS protection for Elastic Load Balancing load balancers, which includes the company’s Application Load Balancer ([What is AWS Shield Advanced?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-waf.html)).

- **A is incorrect** because Amazon Inspector is for automated vulnerability scanning of workloads such as EC2, container images, and Lambda functions, not for attaching an agent to an ALB or mitigating DDoS attacks ([What is Amazon Inspector?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html)).
- **B is incorrect** because Amazon Macie focuses on discovering and protecting sensitive data, especially in Amazon S3, not preventing DDoS attacks against a web application ([What is Amazon Macie?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)).
- **D is incorrect** because Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that generates findings for threats and anomalous activity; it is not the primary AWS service for DDoS mitigation for an ALB ([What is Amazon GuardDuty?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司因近期发生的 Web 攻击而担心其公共 Web 应用程序的安全性。该应用程序使用 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。解决方案架构师必须降低针对该应用程序的 DDoS 攻击风险。解决方案架构师应如何满足此要求？

options.A: 向 ALB 添加 Amazon Inspector 代理。
options.B: 配置 Amazon Macie 以防止攻击。
options.C: 启用 AWS Shield Advanced 以防止攻击。
options.D: 配置 Amazon GuardDuty 以监控 ALB。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. 启用 AWS Shield Advanced 以防止攻击。**

AWS 文档指出，AWS Shield Standard 和 AWS Shield Advanced 为第 3、4 和 7 层的 AWS 资源提供针对 Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) 攻击的保护，并且客户可以订阅 Shield Advanced 以获得更高级别的保护（[How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-overview.html)）。Shield Advanced 专门为 Elastic Load Balancing 负载均衡器提供扩展的 DDoS 防护，其中包括该公司的 Application Load Balancer（[What is AWS Shield Advanced?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-waf.html)）。

- **A 不正确**，因为 Amazon Inspector 用于对 EC2、容器镜像和 Lambda 函数等工作负载进行自动漏洞扫描，而不是将代理附加到 ALB 或缓解 DDoS 攻击（[What is Amazon Inspector?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html)）。
- **B 不正确**，因为 Amazon Macie 侧重于发现和保护敏感数据，尤其是 Amazon S3 中的数据，而不是防止针对 Web 应用程序的 DDoS 攻击（[What is Amazon Macie?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)）。
- **D 不正确**，因为 Amazon GuardDuty 是一项威胁检测服务，可针对威胁和异常活动生成发现结果；它不是用于 ALB DDoS 缓解的主要 AWS 服务（[What is Amazon GuardDuty?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/what-is-guardduty.html)）。

en.question: A company’s web application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company recently changed its policy, which now requires the application to be accessed from one specific country only. Which configuration will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances.
options.B: Configure the security group on the Application Load Balancer.
options.C: Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.
options.D: Configure the network ACL for the subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.**

AWS WAF supports geographic match statements to manage web requests based on the request's country of origin; AWS states that a geo match rule can be used to manage requests based solely on country of origin and matches against country codes ([AWS WAF geo match](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-geo-match.html)). AWS also documents that AWS WAF integrates with Application Load Balancers so web ACL rules can allow or block requests before they reach the application ([AWS WAF and ALB integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-integrations.html)). Therefore, attaching an AWS WAF web ACL to the ALB and allowing only the required country, or blocking all others, meets the requirement with the least application change.

**Why the other options are wrong:**

- **A. EC2 instance security group** - Security groups are IP/port/protocol firewall rules for instances; they do not provide country/geolocation matching. Also, traffic reaches the application through the ALB, so enforcing a country policy should be done at the HTTP request layer in front of the application.
- **B. ALB security group** - An ALB security group can restrict traffic by source IP ranges and ports, but it does not natively evaluate a client's country of origin. AWS WAF is the ALB-integrated service for rule-based allow/block decisions.
- **D. Network ACL** - Network ACLs are subnet-level network controls based on CIDR ranges, ports, and protocols, not country/geolocation. They are not the appropriate mechanism for restricting access to one country.

zh.question: 一家公司的 Web 应用程序运行在 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例上。该公司最近更改了其策略，现在要求该应用程序只能从一个特定国家/地区访问。哪种配置可以满足此要求？

options.A: 配置 EC2 实例的安全组。
options.B: 配置 Application Load Balancer 上的安全组。
options.C: 在 VPC 中的 Application Load Balancer 上配置 AWS WAF。
options.D: 为包含 EC2 实例的子网配置网络 ACL。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. 在 VPC 中的 Application Load Balancer 上配置 AWS WAF。**

AWS WAF 支持地理匹配语句，可根据请求的来源国家/地区管理 Web 请求；AWS 声明，地理匹配规则可用于仅基于来源国家/地区管理请求，并根据国家/地区代码进行匹配（[AWS WAF geo match](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-geo-match.html)）。AWS 还记录了 AWS WAF 与 Application Load Balancers 集成，因此 web ACL 规则可以在请求到达应用程序之前允许或阻止请求（[AWS WAF and ALB integration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-integrations.html)）。因此，将 AWS WAF web ACL 附加到 ALB，并仅允许所需国家/地区，或阻止所有其他国家/地区，可以在对应用程序改动最少的情况下满足要求。

**为什么其他选项是错误的：**

- **A. EC2 实例安全组** - 安全组是针对实例的 IP/端口/协议防火墙规则；它们不提供国家/地区或地理位置匹配。此外，流量通过 ALB 到达应用程序，因此应在应用程序前面的 HTTP 请求层强制执行国家/地区策略。
- **B. ALB 安全组** - ALB 安全组可以按源 IP 范围和端口限制流量，但它不会原生评估客户端的来源国家/地区。AWS WAF 是与 ALB 集成的服务，用于基于规则的允许/阻止决策。
- **D. Network ACL** - Network ACL 是基于 CIDR 范围、端口和协议的子网级网络控制，而不是基于国家/地区或地理位置。它们不是将访问限制到一个国家/地区的适当机制。

en.question: A company provides an API to its users that automates inquiries for tax computations based on item prices. The company experiences a larger number of inquiries during the holiday season only that cause slower response times. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that is scalable and elastic. What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

options.A: Provide an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance performs the required computations when the API request is made.
options.B: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that accepts the item names. API Gateway passes item names to AWS Lambda for tax computations.
options.C: Create an Application Load Balancer that has two Amazon EC2 instances behind it. The EC2 instances will compute the tax on the received item names.
options.D: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that connects with an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. API Gateway accepts and passes the item names to the EC2 instance for tax computations.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.** A REST API in Amazon API Gateway integrated with AWS Lambda is the most scalable and elastic design for seasonal bursts. API Gateway is designed to handle the tasks involved in accepting and processing “up to hundreds of thousands of concurrent API calls” and can act as the front door to backend logic, including Lambda functions. AWS also describes API Gateway and Lambda together as part of AWS serverless infrastructure, where Lambda functions can be exposed through API Gateway methods. Lambda then automatically scales execution environments as request volume increases, up to concurrency quotas, making it well suited for holiday-only spikes in API traffic ([API Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html), [Lambda scaling behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html)). AWS documentation also states that API Gateway supports REST APIs that invoke Lambda functions and that a Lambda integration maps an API path and HTTP method to a Lambda function ([API Gateway endpoint for Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-apigateway.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** A single EC2 instance hosting the API and performing computations is not inherently elastic and creates a capacity bottleneck during seasonal spikes.
- **C:** An Application Load Balancer with two EC2 instances provides more capacity than a single instance, but the option specifies a fixed fleet of two instances and does not describe automatic scaling. It is less elastic than serverless API Gateway + Lambda for variable, seasonal demand.
- **D:** API Gateway can front an EC2-backed API, but the computation still depends on an EC2 instance. This does not provide the automatic compute scaling that Lambda provides when request volume increases.

zh.question: 一家公司向其用户提供一个 API，该 API 会根据商品价格自动处理税费计算查询。该公司仅在假日季期间会遇到大量查询，导致响应时间变慢。解决方案架构师需要设计一个可扩展且有弹性的解决方案。解决方案架构师应如何实现这一目标？

options.A: 提供一个托管在 Amazon EC2 实例上的 API。当发出 API 请求时，EC2 实例执行所需的计算。
options.B: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 设计一个 REST API，用于接受商品名称。API Gateway 将商品名称传递给 AWS Lambda 进行税费计算。
options.C: 创建一个 Application Load Balancer，其后端有两个 Amazon EC2 实例。EC2 实例将根据收到的商品名称计算税费。
options.D: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 设计一个 REST API，该 API 连接到托管在 Amazon EC2 实例上的 API。API Gateway 接受商品名称并将其传递给 EC2 实例进行税费计算。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。** 在 Amazon API Gateway 中构建并与 AWS Lambda 集成的 REST API，是应对季节性突发流量的最具可扩展性和弹性的设计。API Gateway 旨在处理接受和处理“多达数十万并发 API 调用”所涉及的任务，并且可以作为后端逻辑（包括 Lambda 函数）的前门。AWS 还将 API Gateway 和 Lambda 一起描述为 AWS 无服务器基础设施的一部分，其中 Lambda 函数可以通过 API Gateway 方法公开。随后，Lambda 会随着请求量增加而自动扩展执行环境，直至达到并发配额，因此非常适合仅在假日出现的 API 流量峰值（[API Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html), [Lambda scaling behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/scaling-behavior.html)）。AWS 文档还说明，API Gateway 支持调用 Lambda 函数的 REST APIs，并且 Lambda 集成会将 API 路径和 HTTP 方法映射到 Lambda 函数（[API Gateway endpoint for Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-apigateway.html)）。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A:** 单个 EC2 实例托管 API 并执行计算并不具备内在弹性，并且会在季节性峰值期间形成容量瓶颈。
- **C:** 带有两个 EC2 实例的 Application Load Balancer 比单个实例提供更多容量，但该选项指定的是固定的两个实例集群，并未描述自动扩展。对于可变的季节性需求，它不如无服务器 API Gateway + Lambda 具有弹性。
- **D:** API Gateway 可以作为 EC2 支撑的 API 的前端，但计算仍依赖于 EC2 实例。这无法提供 Lambda 在请求量增加时所提供的自动计算扩展能力。

en.question: A solutions architect is creating a new Amazon CloudFront distribution for an application. Some of the information submitted by users is sensitive. The application uses HTTPS but needs another layer of security. The sensitive information should.be protected throughout the entire application stack, and access to the information should be restricted to certain applications. Which action should the solutions architect take?

options.A: Configure a CloudFront signed URL.
options.B: Configure a CloudFront signed cookie.
options.C: Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.
options.D: Configure CloudFront and set the Origin Protocol Policy setting to HTTPS Only for the Viewer Protocol Policy.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.**

CloudFront field-level encryption is designed for exactly this requirement: it adds security beyond HTTPS by encrypting specific sensitive fields at the CloudFront edge, keeping them encrypted throughout the application stack, and allowing only applications with the proper private key to decrypt them. AWS states that field-level encryption “adds an additional layer of security” so “only certain applications can see” the data, and that sensitive information “remains encrypted throughout your entire application stack” until components with the appropriate private key decrypt it ([AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)). The setup includes creating a **field-level encryption profile**, which defines the fields to encrypt ([AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. CloudFront signed URL** — Signed URLs restrict access to private content for authorized users, but they do not encrypt sensitive user-submitted fields throughout the application stack ([AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/PrivateContent.html)).
- **B. CloudFront signed cookie** — Signed cookies also restrict access to private content, but like signed URLs, they are for access control to content, not field-level protection of submitted sensitive data through backend systems ([AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/PrivateContent.html)).
- **D. HTTPS Only origin/viewer protocol policy** — HTTPS protects data in transit between viewers, CloudFront, and origins. However, the question already states the application uses HTTPS and needs an additional layer that restricts data visibility to certain applications. Origin Protocol Policy **HTTPS Only** only makes CloudFront use HTTPS to communicate with the origin; it does not keep selected fields encrypted inside the application stack ([AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/using-https-cloudfront-to-custom-origin.html)).

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在为一个应用程序创建新的 Amazon CloudFront 分配。用户提交的某些信息是敏感的。该应用程序使用 HTTPS，但需要另一层安全保护。敏感信息应在整个应用程序堆栈中受到保护，并且对该信息的访问应限制为某些应用程序。解决方案架构师应采取哪项操作？

options.A: 配置 CloudFront 签名 URL。
options.B: 配置 CloudFront 签名 Cookie。
options.C: 配置 CloudFront 字段级加密配置文件。
options.D: 配置 CloudFront，并将 Viewer Protocol Policy 的 Origin Protocol Policy 设置为 HTTPS Only。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.**

CloudFront 字段级加密正是为此类要求而设计的：它通过在 CloudFront 边缘加密特定敏感字段，在 HTTPS 之外增加安全性，使这些字段在整个应用程序堆栈中保持加密状态，并且只允许拥有正确私钥的应用程序解密它们。AWS 表示，字段级加密“adds an additional layer of security”，因此“only certain applications can see”这些数据，并且敏感信息会“remains encrypted throughout your entire application stack”，直到拥有相应私钥的组件对其解密（[AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)）。该设置包括创建一个**字段级加密配置文件**，用于定义要加密的字段（[AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. CloudFront signed URL** — 签名 URL 限制授权用户对私有内容的访问，但它们不会在整个应用程序堆栈中加密用户提交的敏感字段（[AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/PrivateContent.html)）。
- **B. CloudFront signed cookie** — 签名 Cookie 也会限制对私有内容的访问，但与签名 URL 一样，它们用于内容访问控制，而不是在后端系统中对提交的敏感数据进行字段级保护（[AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/PrivateContent.html)）。
- **D. HTTPS Only origin/viewer protocol policy** — HTTPS 保护查看器、CloudFront 和源站之间传输中的数据。但是，题目已经说明该应用程序使用 HTTPS，并且需要一个额外层来将数据可见性限制为某些应用程序。Origin Protocol Policy **HTTPS Only** 只会使 CloudFront 使用 HTTPS 与源站通信；它不会使选定字段在应用程序堆栈内部保持加密（[AWS CloudFront Developer Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/using-https-cloudfront-to-custom-origin.html)）。

en.question: A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3. This content is the same for all users. The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide accessing these media files. The company wants to provide the files to the users while reducing the load on the origin. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
options.B: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
options.C: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.**

CloudFront is designed for this exact scenario: globally delivering HTTP content such as images and media files from origins like Amazon S3. AWS states that CloudFront distributions can use an **Amazon S3 bucket** as an origin, and that CloudFront sends the distribution configuration to worldwide edge locations/POPs where it **caches copies of your files**. This reduces repeated requests to the S3 origin and improves delivery latency for millions of global users. CloudFront also notes that data transfer from AWS origins such as S3 to CloudFront is free; customers are billed for CloudFront-to-viewer transfer, supporting the cost-effective requirement for static shared content delivery ([CloudFront introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)). CloudFront origin settings explicitly support an **Amazon S3 bucket** as an origin domain ([CloudFront origin settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesOrigin.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**
