options.C: 为 Amazon EC2 创建接口端点。
options.D: 在 VPC 的每个子网中为该端点创建一个弹性网络接口。
options.E: 在端点的安全组中创建一个安全组条目以提供访问权限。

zh.explanation:
正确选项是 **A and B**。

- **B is correct**：可以使用 **gateway VPC endpoint** 从 VPC 访问 DynamoDB。AWS 表明，gateway endpoints 可为 **Amazon S3 and DynamoDB** 提供连接，而无需 internet gateway 或 NAT device，这满足流量不经过互联网的要求。AWS 还特别针对 DynamoDB 说明，使用网关端点可以从 VPC 访问 DynamoDB，而无需 internet gateway 或 NAT device（[Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html), [Gateway endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html)）。
- **A is correct**：流量必须被路由到网关端点。AWS 文档说明，创建 DynamoDB 网关端点后，可以在路由表中将其添加为目标，用于发往 DynamoDB 的流量。文档还说明，每个子网路由表都必须有一条路由，使用服务前缀列表将该服务的流量发送到网关端点（[Gateway endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html), [Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **C is incorrect**：用于 **Amazon EC2** 的接口端点用于私有访问 EC2 API，而不是 DynamoDB。本题讨论的是 DynamoDB API 调用。
- **D is incorrect**：端点网络接口是为 **interface** VPC endpoints 创建的。AWS 表明，对于为接口端点指定的每个子网，AWS 都会创建一个端点网络接口。DynamoDB 网关端点不要求你在子网中创建弹性网络接口（[Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-interface-endpoint.html)）。
- **E is incorrect**：**endpoint network interfaces** 的安全组适用于接口端点。对于 DynamoDB 网关端点，AWS 指的是访问 DynamoDB 的 **instances** 上的安全组规则，而不是端点安全组。网关端点通过路由表路由流量，而不是使用带有端点安全组的端点 ENI（[Gateway endpoints for Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-ddb.html), [Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)）。

en.question: A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on-premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
options.B: Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
options.C: Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
options.D: Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B. Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.**

Amazon EKS Connector is designed for exactly this requirement: AWS says you can use it to “register and connect any conformant Kubernetes cluster to AWS and visualize it in the Amazon EKS console.” After connection, “you can see the status, configuration, and workloads” for the connected cluster in the Amazon EKS console, and supported cluster types include **on-premises Kubernetes clusters** ([Amazon EKS Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html)). This provides a central viewing location with minimal operational overhead compared with building a custom monitoring or management layer.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. CloudWatch Container Insights** collects, aggregates, and summarizes **metrics and logs** from containerized applications, and creates metrics at cluster, node, pod, task, and service levels ([Container Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights.html)). It is an observability/metrics solution, not the purpose-built way to register external Kubernetes clusters and view their status, configuration, and workloads centrally in the EKS console.
- **C. AWS Systems Manager** is not the central Kubernetes cluster/workload visualization feature. Although EKS Connector uses Systems Manager endpoints as part of its connectivity requirements, the documented feature for registering and viewing external Kubernetes clusters is **Amazon EKS Connector**, not Systems Manager directly ([Amazon EKS Connector considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html)).
- **D. Amazon EKS Anywhere** is for running and managing Kubernetes clusters in on-premises or edge environments. AWS describes it as a **customer-managed** product where customers are responsible for cluster lifecycle operations and maintenance, which adds operational overhead and does not make it the native central viewer for other clusters ([Amazon EKS deployment options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-deployment-options.html)). The same EKS deployment-options page identifies **Amazon EKS Connector** as the tooling to register any conformant Kubernetes cluster and view its status, configuration, and workloads in the EKS console.

zh.question: 一家公司在 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 集群和本地 Kubernetes 集群上运行其应用程序。该公司希望从一个中心位置查看所有集群和工作负载。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights 来收集并分组集群信息。
options.B: 使用 Amazon EKS Connector 注册并连接所有 Kubernetes 集群。
options.C: 使用 AWS Systems Manager 收集并查看集群信息。
options.D: 使用 Amazon EKS Anywhere 作为主集群，通过原生 Kubernetes 命令查看其他集群。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B. 使用 Amazon EKS Connector 注册并连接所有 Kubernetes 集群。**

Amazon EKS Connector 正是为这一需求而设计的：AWS 表示，你可以使用它“register and connect any conformant Kubernetes cluster to AWS and visualize it in the Amazon EKS console”。连接后，你可以在 Amazon EKS 控制台中查看已连接集群的“status, configuration, and workloads”，并且受支持的集群类型包括 **on-premises Kubernetes clusters**（[Amazon EKS Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html)）。与构建自定义监控或管理层相比，这提供了一个中心查看位置，并且运营开销最小。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. CloudWatch Container Insights** 从容器化应用程序收集、聚合并汇总 **metrics and logs**，并在集群、节点、pod、任务和服务级别创建指标（[Container Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights.html)）。它是可观测性/指标解决方案，而不是用于注册外部 Kubernetes 集群并在 EKS 控制台中集中查看其状态、配置和工作负载的专用方式。
- **C. AWS Systems Manager** 不是集中式 Kubernetes 集群/工作负载可视化功能。虽然 EKS Connector 使用 Systems Manager 端点作为其连接要求的一部分，但用于注册和查看外部 Kubernetes 集群的文档化功能是 **Amazon EKS Connector**，而不是直接使用 Systems Manager（[Amazon EKS Connector considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-connector.html)）。
- **D. Amazon EKS Anywhere** 用于在本地或边缘环境中运行和管理 Kubernetes 集群。AWS 将其描述为 **customer-managed** 产品，客户负责集群生命周期操作和维护，这会增加运营开销，而且它也不是用于查看其他集群的原生中心查看器（[Amazon EKS deployment options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-deployment-options.html)）。同一个 EKS deployment-options 页面指出，**Amazon EKS Connector** 才是用于注册任何符合标准的 Kubernetes 集群，并在 EKS 控制台中查看其状态、配置和工作负载的工具。

en.question: A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
options.B: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
options.C: Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
options.D: Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.** Amazon RDS is the best fit for ecommerce purchase transactions because it is a managed relational database service, supports familiar engines including **MySQL**, and AWS shows a typical dynamic website architecture in which application servers interact with RDS DB instances for database storage ([Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)). To protect sensitive fields even from database administrators, the application should use **client-side encryption** before writing the data to the database. AWS documentation describes client-side encryption as encrypting data before sending it to the database, while server-side encryption transparently decrypts data when it is accessed ([AWS Database Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/database-encryption-sdk/latest/devguide/client-server-side.html)). The AWS Encryption SDK is a client-side encryption library that can use AWS KMS keys/keyrings to protect data keys and encrypted data ([AWS Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html)). Therefore, the database stores ciphertext, so database administrators cannot read the sensitive values without decrypt permissions in the application/KMS path.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A:** EBS encryption protects EBS resources at the infrastructure layer; AWS states encryption operations occur on the servers that host EC2 instances and protect data at rest and in transit between the instance and EBS storage ([Amazon EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html)). It does not provide application-level/client-side encryption of customer fields, and EBS block storage is not the right managed transactional database layer for ecommerce purchase transactions.
* **C:** S3 with SSE-KMS is **server-side** encryption. Amazon S3 encrypts objects before saving them to disk and decrypts them when downloaded ([S3 bucket encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)). That protects objects at rest but does not inherently prevent authorized storage administrators or application paths from receiving plaintext, and S3 object storage is not the best transactional relational store for purchase transactions.
* **D:** FSx for Windows File Server with Windows permissions is file storage access control, not a transactional database design and not client-side encryption of sensitive fields. File permissions do not meet the requirement to keep sensitive data protected from database administrators in the way application-side encryption does.

zh.question: 一家公司正在构建一个电子商务应用程序，需要存储敏感的客户信息。该公司需要让客户能够在网站上完成购买交易。该公司还需要确保敏感客户数据受到保护，即使是数据库管理员也无法访问。哪种解决方案满足这些要求？

options.A: 将敏感数据存储在 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷中。使用 EBS 加密来加密数据。使用 IAM 实例角色来限制访问。
options.B: 将敏感数据存储在 Amazon RDS for MySQL 中。使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 客户端加密来加密数据。
options.C: 将敏感数据存储在 Amazon S3 中。使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 服务器端加密来加密数据。使用 S3 存储桶策略来限制访问。
options.D: 将敏感数据存储在 Amazon FSx for Windows Server 中。在应用程序服务器上挂载文件共享。使用 Windows 文件权限来限制访问。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。** Amazon RDS 最适合电子商务购买交易，因为它是一项托管式关系数据库服务，支持包括 **MySQL** 在内的常用引擎，并且 AWS 展示了一种典型的动态网站架构，其中应用程序服务器与 RDS DB 实例交互以进行数据库存储（[Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)）。为了保护敏感字段，即使是数据库管理员也无法访问，应用程序应在将数据写入数据库之前使用 **客户端加密**。AWS 文档将客户端加密描述为在将数据发送到数据库之前对其进行加密，而服务器端加密会在访问数据时透明地解密数据（[AWS Database Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/database-encryption-sdk/latest/devguide/client-server-side.html)）。AWS Encryption SDK 是一个客户端加密库，可以使用 AWS KMS keys/keyrings 来保护数据密钥和加密数据（[AWS Encryption SDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html)）。因此，数据库存储的是密文，所以数据库管理员如果没有应用程序/KMS 路径中的解密权限，就无法读取敏感值。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A:** EBS 加密在基础设施层保护 EBS 资源；AWS 表示，加密操作发生在托管 EC2 实例的服务器上，并保护静态数据以及实例与 EBS 存储之间传输中的数据（[Amazon EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html)）。它不提供客户字段的应用程序级/客户端加密，而且 EBS 块存储也不是电子商务购买交易所需的合适托管事务型数据库层。
* **C:** 使用 SSE-KMS 的 S3 是 **服务器端** 加密。Amazon S3 在将对象保存到磁盘之前对其进行加密，并在下载时对其进行解密（[S3 bucket encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。这可以保护静态对象，但并不会从本质上阻止已授权的存储管理员或应用程序路径接收明文，而且 S3 对象存储也不是购买交易的最佳事务型关系存储。
* **D:** FSx for Windows File Server 结合 Windows 权限是文件存储访问控制，而不是事务型数据库设计，也不是对敏感字段进行客户端加密。文件权限无法像应用程序端加密那样满足将敏感数据与数据库管理员隔离保护的要求。

en.question: A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud. The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand. Which migration solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.
options.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
options.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.
options.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.** Amazon Aurora is the best fit because it is a fully managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL; AWS states that existing MySQL code, tools, and applications can be used with Aurora, helping maintain application compatibility after migration ([Amazon Aurora overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)). AWS DMS supports self-managed MySQL-compatible databases as sources and MySQL-compatible databases as targets, so it can migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL ([DMS MySQL source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MySQL.html), [DMS MySQL target](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.MySQL.html)). Aurora Auto Scaling dynamically adjusts the number of Aurora Replicas to handle sudden increases in connectivity or workload ([Aurora Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** Amazon RDS for MySQL preserves MySQL compatibility, but the option only configures **storage** autoscaling. RDS storage autoscaling automatically increases storage when free space is low; it does not automatically scale database compute/read capacity during demand spikes ([RDS storage autoscaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html)).
- **B:** Amazon Redshift is a fully managed petabyte-scale **data warehouse** for analytics/BI workloads, not the appropriate transactional MySQL-compatible relational database target ([Amazon Redshift overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/welcome.html)).
- **D:** DynamoDB is a NoSQL database with a different data design model from relational databases; migrating MySQL transactional applications to DynamoDB would not maintain MySQL application compatibility without redesign ([DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司有一个本地 MySQL 数据库，用于处理事务数据。该公司正在将该数据库迁移到 AWS Cloud。迁移后的数据库必须保持与公司使用该数据库的应用程序的兼容性。迁移后的数据库还必须在需求增加期间自动扩展。哪种迁移解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用原生 MySQL 工具将数据库迁移到 Amazon RDS for MySQL。配置弹性存储扩展。
options.B: 使用 mysqldump 实用程序将数据库迁移到 Amazon Redshift。为 Amazon Redshift 集群开启 Auto Scaling。
options.C: 使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 将数据库迁移到 Amazon Aurora。开启 Aurora Auto Scaling。
options.D: 使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 将数据库迁移到 Amazon DynamoDB。配置 Auto Scaling 策略。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C。** Amazon Aurora 是最佳选择，因为它是一个与 MySQL 兼容的完全托管关系数据库引擎；AWS 表示，现有的 MySQL 代码、工具和应用程序可以与 Aurora 一起使用，有助于在迁移后保持应用程序兼容性（[Amazon Aurora overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)）。AWS DMS 支持自管理的 MySQL 兼容数据库作为源，并支持 MySQL 兼容数据库作为目标，因此它可以将本地 MySQL 数据库迁移到 Aurora MySQL（[DMS MySQL source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MySQL.html)，[DMS MySQL target](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.MySQL.html)）。Aurora Auto Scaling 会动态调整 Aurora Replicas 的数量，以处理连接数或工作负载的突然增加（[Aurora Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html)）。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A:** Amazon RDS for MySQL 保留了 MySQL 兼容性，但该选项只配置了**存储**自动扩展。RDS 存储自动扩展会在可用空间不足时自动增加存储；它不会在需求高峰期间自动扩展数据库计算/读取容量（[RDS storage autoscaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html)）。
- **B:** Amazon Redshift 是一个完全托管的 PB 级**数据仓库**，用于分析/BI 工作负载，并不是适合的事务型 MySQL 兼容关系数据库目标（[Amazon Redshift overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/welcome.html)）。
- **D:** DynamoDB 是 NoSQL 数据库，其数据设计模型不同于关系数据库；将 MySQL 事务型应用程序迁移到 DynamoDB，如果不重新设计，就无法保持 MySQL 应用程序兼容性（[DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)）。

en.question: A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure. The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.
options.C: Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.
options.D: Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.** Amazon EFS is the appropriate shared file storage service for Linux EC2 instances that need a hierarchical file system and concurrent access. AWS states that EFS provides elastic **file storage so that you can share file data**, supports **NFSv4**, is accessible from Amazon EC2, and Regional EFS stores data redundantly across **multiple Availability Zones**. EFS also provides throughput, IOPS, low latency, and **massively parallel access** from compute instances, with file-system semantics such as consistency and file locking ([EFS overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/whatisefs.html)). AWS also documents mounting EFS file systems to **multiple Amazon EC2 instances** ([mounting EFS to multiple EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mount-multiple-ec2-instances.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Amazon S3** is object storage, not a normal shared POSIX/NFS file system for applications expecting hierarchical directories. AWS notes that S3 general purpose buckets have a **flat structure instead of a hierarchy like a file system**; console “folders” are implemented with key prefixes ([S3 folders](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-folders.html)).
- **C. Single io2 EBS volume attached to all instances** is not suitable across two AZs. EBS Multi-Attach volumes can attach only to instances in the **same Availability Zone**, and standard file systems such as XFS and EXT4 are not designed for simultaneous access by multiple servers without a clustered file system ([EBS Multi-Attach limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html)).
- **D. Separate EBS volumes synchronized across instances** does not provide a single shared file system with rapid concurrent reads/writes. It introduces synchronization complexity and does not meet the requirement for concurrent shared storage as directly as EFS.

zh.question: 一家公司在跨两个可用区的 VPC 中运行多个 Amazon EC2 Linux 实例。这些实例托管使用分层目录结构的应用程序。这些应用程序需要对共享存储进行快速且并发的读写。解决方案架构师应如何满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。允许 VPC 中的所有 EC2 实例访问该存储桶。
options.B: 创建一个 Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) 文件系统。从每个 EC2 实例挂载该 EFS 文件系统。
options.C: 在一个 Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷上创建文件系统。将该 EBS 卷附加到所有 EC2 实例。
options.D: 在附加到每个 EC2 实例的 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷上创建文件系统。在不同的 EC2 实例之间同步这些 EBS 卷。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。** Amazon EFS 是适用于需要分层文件系统和并发访问的 Linux EC2 实例的合适共享文件存储服务。AWS 表示，EFS 提供弹性**文件存储，以便你可以共享文件数据**，支持 **NFSv4**，可从 Amazon EC2 访问，并且 Regional EFS 会跨**多个可用区**冗余存储数据。EFS 还为计算实例提供吞吐量、IOPS、低延迟和**大规模并行访问**，并具备一致性和文件锁定等文件系统语义（[EFS overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/whatisefs.html)）。AWS 还记录了将 EFS 文件系统挂载到**多个 Amazon EC2 实例**的方法（[mounting EFS to multiple EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mount-multiple-ec2-instances.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. Amazon S3** 是对象存储，而不是面向期望分层目录的应用程序的普通共享 POSIX/NFS 文件系统。AWS 指出，S3 通用存储桶具有**扁平结构，而不是像文件系统那样的层次结构**；控制台中的“文件夹”是通过键前缀实现的（[S3 folders](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-folders.html)）。
- **C. 附加到所有实例的单个 io2 EBS 卷** 不适合跨两个 AZ。EBS Multi-Attach 卷只能附加到**同一可用区**中的实例，并且 XFS 和 EXT4 等标准文件系统并非设计用于在没有集群文件系统的情况下由多个服务器同时访问（[EBS Multi-Attach limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html)）。
- **D. 在实例之间同步的独立 EBS 卷** 无法提供具有快速并发读/写能力的单一共享文件系统。它会引入同步复杂性，并且不像 EFS 那样直接满足并发共享存储的要求。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
options.B: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
options.C: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.
options.D: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.**

A serverless ingestion and processing path provides the least operational overhead. Amazon API Gateway supports stateless **HTTP** and REST APIs and, together with Lambda, is part of AWS serverless infrastructure; API Gateway can expose Lambda functions through API methods and supports streamlined Lambda proxy integrations ([API Gateway documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html)). AWS Lambda runs code **without the need to manage servers**, automatically scales, and is suitable for processing API requests and IoT/API backends; AWS manages server and OS maintenance, capacity provisioning, automatic scaling, and logging ([Lambda documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html)). DynamoDB is appropriate for IoT-style, web-scale workloads, scales seamlessly, and as a managed service insulates applications from implementation details so builders can focus on application design ([DynamoDB documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/SQLtoNoSQL.WhyDynamoDB.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B** uses an ELB and Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances, which requires managing compute instances and application runtime. S3 is object storage, not a database for incrementing and querying per-tenant hourly usage.
- **C** uses API Gateway and Lambda, but stores data in SQL Server Express on an EC2 instance. That introduces EC2 and database administration overhead and is less managed than DynamoDB.
- **D** also requires EC2 instances behind a load balancer and uses EFS file storage rather than a database designed for scalable per-tenant usage records. This has more operational overhead than the serverless API Gateway/Lambda/DynamoDB design.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在设计一个工作负载，用于存储一栋建筑中各业务租户的每小时能源消耗。传感器将通过 HTTP 请求向数据库馈送数据，这些请求会累加每个租户的使用量。解决方案架构师必须在可能的情况下使用托管服务。随着解决方案架构师添加独立组件，该工作负载将来会获得更多功能。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 AWS Lambda 函数接收来自传感器的数据、处理数据，并将数据存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。
options.B: 使用由 Amazon EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组支持的 Elastic Load Balancer 来接收和处理来自传感器的数据。使用 Amazon S3 存储桶存储处理后的数据。
options.C: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 AWS Lambda 函数接收来自传感器的数据、处理数据，并将数据存储在 Amazon EC2 实例上的 Microsoft SQL Server Express 数据库中。
options.D: 使用由 Amazon EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组支持的 Elastic Load Balancer 来接收和处理来自传感器的数据。使用 Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) 共享文件系统存储处理后的数据。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.**

无服务器的摄取和处理路径可提供最少的运营开销。Amazon API Gateway 支持无状态 **HTTP** 和 REST API，并且与 Lambda 一起属于 AWS 无服务器基础设施的一部分；API Gateway 可以通过 API 方法公开 Lambda 函数，并支持简化的 Lambda 代理集成（[API Gateway documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html)）。AWS Lambda 运行代码时**无需管理服务器**，可自动扩展，并且适合处理 API 请求以及 IoT/API 后端；AWS 管理服务器和 OS 维护、容量预置、自动扩展和日志记录（[Lambda documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html)）。DynamoDB 适用于 IoT 风格的 Web 规模工作负载，可无缝扩展，并且作为托管服务可使应用程序免受实现细节影响，从而让构建者专注于应用程序设计（[DynamoDB documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/SQLtoNoSQL.WhyDynamoDB.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B** 使用 ELB 和 EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组，这需要管理计算实例和应用程序运行时。S3 是对象存储，并不是用于按租户递增和查询每小时使用量的数据库。
- **C** 使用 API Gateway 和 Lambda，但将数据存储在 EC2 实例上的 SQL Server Express 中。这会引入 EC2 和数据库管理开销，并且其托管程度低于 DynamoDB。
- **D** 同样需要负载均衡器后面的 EC2 实例，并使用 EFS 文件存储，而不是使用专为可扩展的按租户使用量记录而设计的数据库。与无服务器的 API Gateway/Lambda/DynamoDB 设计相比，这会带来更多运营开销。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application used for storing and viewing engineering drawings. All application components will be deployed on the AWS infrastructure. The application design must support caching to minimize the amount of time that users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must be able to store petabytes of data. Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?

options.A: Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront
options.B: Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache
options.C: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront
options.D: AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront**

Amazon S3 is the best storage layer because it is object storage with “industry-leading scalability” and can “store and protect any amount of data,” which fits a web application that must store petabytes of engineering drawings ([Amazon S3 overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html)). Amazon CloudFront is the right caching layer because it speeds up distribution of static and dynamic web content through global edge locations, delivers cached content immediately when present at the edge, and can use an Amazon S3 bucket as an origin ([CloudFront overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache** — S3 Glacier storage classes are for archive/rarely accessed data; S3 documentation distinguishes frequent-access, millisecond-access storage from archive tiers designed for asynchronous access ([S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)). ElastiCache is not the appropriate cache for serving large static drawing files to web users globally; CloudFront is built for content delivery and edge caching.
- **C. Amazon EBS volumes with Amazon CloudFront** — EBS is block storage for compute workloads, not the best fit for storing and serving petabytes of web objects. CloudFront origins are services such as an S3 bucket or HTTP server; S3 is the native scalable object-store origin for this use case ([CloudFront overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)).
- **D. AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache** — Storage Gateway, specifically S3 File Gateway, is primarily for providing NFS/SMB file interfaces and local caching for existing/on-premises-style file access patterns; the documentation describes deploying the gateway into an on-premises environment or similar appliance/VM model ([S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html)). The question states all components are on AWS infrastructure and needs web content caching, making S3 plus CloudFront the better architecture.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在为一个新的 Web 应用程序设计存储架构，该应用程序用于存储和查看工程图纸。所有应用程序组件都将部署在 AWS 基础设施上。应用程序设计必须支持缓存，以最大限度减少用户等待工程图纸加载的时间。该应用程序必须能够存储 PB 级数据。解决方案架构师应使用哪种存储和缓存组合？

options.A: Amazon S3 搭配 Amazon CloudFront
options.B: Amazon S3 Glacier 搭配 Amazon ElastiCache
options.C: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷搭配 Amazon CloudFront
options.D: AWS Storage Gateway 搭配 Amazon ElastiCache

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront**

Amazon S3 是最佳存储层，因为它是对象存储，具有“行业领先的可扩展性”，并且可以“存储和保护任意数量的数据”，这适合必须存储 PB 级工程图纸的 Web 应用程序（[Amazon S3 overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html)）。Amazon CloudFront 是正确的缓存层，因为它通过全球边缘站点加速静态和动态 Web 内容的分发，当内容存在于边缘时可立即交付缓存内容，并且可以使用 Amazon S3 存储桶作为源站（[CloudFront overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache** — S3 Glacier 存储类适用于归档/很少访问的数据；S3 文档将频繁访问、毫秒级访问的存储与为异步访问而设计的归档层区分开来（[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。ElastiCache 并不适合向全球 Web 用户提供大型静态图纸文件的缓存；CloudFront 专为内容分发和边缘缓存而构建。
- **C. Amazon EBS volumes with Amazon CloudFront** — EBS 是用于计算工作负载的块存储，并不是存储和提供 PB 级 Web 对象的最佳选择。CloudFront 源站可以是 S3 存储桶或 HTTP 服务器等服务；对于此用例，S3 是原生可扩展的对象存储源站（[CloudFront overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)）。
- **D. AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache** — Storage Gateway，特别是 S3 File Gateway，主要用于为现有/本地风格的文件访问模式提供 NFS/SMB 文件接口和本地缓存；文档描述了将网关部署到本地环境或类似设备/VM 模型中（[S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html)）。题目说明所有组件都在 AWS 基础设施上，并且需要 Web 内容缓存，因此 S3 加 CloudFront 是更好的架构。

en.question: An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming traffic. A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and if the rule's target is being invoked. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.
options.B: Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.
options.C: Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
options.D: Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** EventBridge publishes operational metrics to CloudWatch in the **`AWS/Events`** namespace. The documented metrics directly answer both parts of the question: **`MatchedEvents`** shows the number of events that matched a rule, and **`Invocations`** shows the number of times a target was invoked by a rule in response to an event. EventBridge also provides dimensions such as **`RuleName`** and **`EventBusName`** to filter metrics for the specific rule or bus. Therefore, checking CloudWatch metrics for `AWS/Events` is the appropriate way to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and whether the third-party API target is being invoked ([Monitoring Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. SQS dead-letter queue:** A DLQ is useful only if one is configured and events fail delivery or are moved to the DLQ. It does not generally show whether rule conditions are being matched or whether target invocation is occurring. CloudWatch metrics such as `InvocationsSentToDlq`, `FailedInvocations`, `Invocations`, and `MatchedEvents` are the monitoring mechanism for this requirement ([Monitoring Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring.html)).
- **C. CloudWatch Logs:** EventBridge does not automatically log every event or rule evaluation to CloudWatch Logs for troubleshooting. CloudWatch Logs can be a target, but the question asks how to determine matching and target invocation; the documented EventBridge metrics provide that information.
- **D. CloudTrail:** CloudTrail records AWS account API activity, which is useful for auditing calls made to AWS APIs, but it is not the right tool to determine whether an EventBridge rule matched events and invoked its target. Those are EventBridge CloudWatch metrics, not CloudTrail trail records ([What Is AWS CloudTrail?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html)).

zh.question: 一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则以第三方 API 为目标。该第三方 API 没有收到任何传入流量。解决方案架构师需要确定规则条件是否得到满足，以及规则的目标是否被调用。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Amazon CloudWatch 中检查 AWS/Events 命名空间下的指标。
options.B: 查看 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 死信队列中的事件。
options.C: 在 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 中检查这些事件。
options.D: 在 AWS CloudTrail 中检查 EventBridge 事件的跟踪记录。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.** EventBridge 会将操作指标发布到 CloudWatch 的 **`AWS/Events`** 命名空间。文档中的指标直接回答了问题的两个部分：**`MatchedEvents`** 显示匹配规则的事件数量，**`Invocations`** 显示规则响应事件调用目标的次数。EventBridge 还提供 **`RuleName`** 和 **`EventBusName`** 等维度，用于筛选特定规则或总线的指标。因此，检查 `AWS/Events` 的 CloudWatch 指标，是确定规则条件是否得到满足以及第三方 API 目标是否被调用的适当方式（[Monitoring Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. SQS 死信队列：** DLQ 只有在已配置且事件投递失败或被移至 DLQ 时才有用。它通常不能显示规则条件是否正在匹配，或目标调用是否正在发生。`InvocationsSentToDlq`、`FailedInvocations`、`Invocations` 和 `MatchedEvents` 等 CloudWatch 指标才是满足此需求的监控机制（[Monitoring Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-monitoring.html)）。
- **C. CloudWatch Logs：** EventBridge 不会自动将每个事件或规则评估记录到 CloudWatch Logs 以供故障排查。CloudWatch Logs 可以作为目标，但题目询问的是如何确定匹配和目标调用；文档中的 EventBridge 指标提供了这些信息。
- **D. CloudTrail：** CloudTrail 记录 AWS 账户 API 活动，这对于审计对 AWS API 发起的调用很有用，但它不是确定 EventBridge 规则是否匹配事件并调用其目标的正确工具。这些是 EventBridge CloudWatch 指标，而不是 CloudTrail 跟踪记录（[What Is AWS CloudTrail?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html)）。

en.question: A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly repeating increased workload. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
options.B: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
options.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
options.D: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B. Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.**

The workload increase is **predictable and recurring every Friday evening**. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling is designed for this: AWS says scheduled scaling lets you set up automatic scaling based on predictable load changes and create scheduled actions that increase or decrease an Auto Scaling group's desired capacity at specific times. Scheduled actions can also run on a recurring schedule and set the desired, minimum, and maximum capacity at the specified time ([Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html)). Therefore, the company can keep capacity at 2 normally and use scheduled actions to scale to 6 each Friday, with minimal ongoing operations.

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. EventBridge reminder**: A reminder still requires someone or another process to perform the scaling. The requirement asks for the least operational overhead; scheduled scaling performs the action automatically as a function of date and time.
- **C. Manual scaling**: AWS describes manual scaling as updating the desired capacity or terminating instances manually ([Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)). This would require weekly operational work.
- **D. Automatic/dynamic scaling**: Dynamic scaling resizes the group to meet changes in demand and is useful when you **don't know when traffic will change** ([Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)). Here, the increase is known in advance, so scheduled scaling is the more direct, lower-overhead solution.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个大型工作负载，每周五晚上运行。该工作负载运行在 us-east-1 Region 中两个 Availability Zones 内的 Amazon EC2 实例上。通常情况下，公司必须始终运行不超过两个实例。但是，公司希望每周五扩展到六个实例，以处理定期重复增加的工作负载。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Amazon EventBridge 中创建提醒以扩展实例。
options.B: 创建一个具有计划操作的 Auto Scaling group。
options.C: 创建一个使用手动扩展的 Auto Scaling group。
options.D: 创建一个使用自动扩展的 Auto Scaling group。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B. 创建一个具有计划操作的 Auto Scaling group。**

工作负载的增加是**可预测的，并且每周五晚上重复发生**。Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 计划扩展正是为此而设计的：AWS 表示，计划扩展允许你基于可预测的负载变化设置自动扩展，并创建计划操作，在特定时间增加或减少 Auto Scaling group 的所需容量。计划操作还可以按重复计划运行，并在指定时间设置所需容量、最小容量和最大容量（[Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html)）。因此，公司可以在平时将容量保持为 2，并使用计划操作在每周五扩展到 6，且持续运营工作量最小。为什么其他选项不正确：

- **A. EventBridge reminder**：提醒仍然需要某个人或另一个流程来执行扩展。题目要求最少的运营开销；计划扩展会根据日期和时间自动执行该操作。
- **C. Manual scaling**：AWS 将手动扩展描述为手动更新所需容量或终止实例（[Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)）。这将需要每周进行运营工作。
- **D. Automatic/dynamic scaling**：动态扩展会调整组的大小以满足需求变化，并且在你**不知道流量何时会变化**时很有用（[Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)）。在这里，增加的负载是提前已知的，因此计划扩展是更直接、开销更低的解决方案。

en.question: A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS. The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CImport the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
options.B: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
options.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
options.D: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.**

Use a certificate that is obtained outside AWS and signed by the required third-party public CA, then **import** it into ACM and attach it to an API Gateway custom domain. AWS documents that ACM supports importing certificates obtained outside AWS, including cases where you already have a certificate from a **third-party certificate authority (CA)** or have requirements not met by ACM-issued certificates ([ACM import certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/import-certificate.html)). API Gateway HTTP API custom domains support TLSv1.3 under the `TLS_1_2` security policy; the supported protocol table lists **TLSv1.3 = Yes** ([API Gateway HTTP API security policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-ciphers.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **B** is incorrect because ACM public certificates are ACM-issued certificates; ACM does not let you create a public certificate in ACM and choose a specific external third-party public CA to sign it. If the certificate must be signed by a specific third-party CA, AWS says to obtain it outside AWS and import it into ACM ([ACM import certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/import-certificate.html); [ACM public certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/gs-acm-request-public.html)).
- **C** is incorrect for two reasons: it describes creating a certificate in ACM signed by a third-party CA and then importing it, which is not the supported third-party-CA workflow; also Lambda function URL creation/configuration supports settings such as auth type and CORS, not attaching a custom TLS certificate ([Lambda function URL configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)).
- **D** is incorrect for the same reasons as B and C: ACM cannot issue a public certificate signed by a chosen third-party CA, and Lambda function URLs do not provide a custom certificate configuration option in the documented function URL setup ([Lambda function URL configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司正在创建 REST API。该公司对 TLS 的使用有严格要求。该公司要求 API 端点使用 TLSv1.3。该公司还要求由特定的公共第三方证书颁发机构 (CA) 对 TLS 证书进行签名。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用本地计算机创建一个由第三方 C 签名的证书。将该证书导入 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)。在 Amazon API Gateway 中创建带有自定义域名的 HTTP API。配置自定义域名以使用该证书。
options.B: 在 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 中创建一个由第三方 CA 签名的证书。在 Amazon API Gateway 中创建带有自定义域名的 HTTP API。配置自定义域名以使用该证书。
options.C: 使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 创建一个由第三方 CA 签名的证书。将该证书导入 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)。创建一个带有 Lambda 函数 URL 的 AWS Lambda 函数。配置 Lambda 函数 URL 以使用该证书。
options.D: 在 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 中创建一个由第三方 CA 签名的证书。创建一个带有 Lambda 函数 URL 的 AWS Lambda 函数。配置 Lambda 函数 URL 以使用该证书。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.**

使用在 AWS 之外获取并由所需第三方公共 CA 签名的证书，然后将其**导入** ACM，并将其附加到 API Gateway 自定义域名。AWS 文档说明，ACM 支持导入在 AWS 之外获取的证书，包括你已经拥有来自**第三方证书颁发机构 (CA)** 的证书，或有 ACM 颁发证书无法满足的要求的情况（[ACM import certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/import-certificate.html)）。API Gateway HTTP API 自定义域名在 `TLS_1_2` 安全策略下支持 TLSv1.3；支持的协议表列出了 **TLSv1.3 = Yes**（[API Gateway HTTP API security policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-ciphers.html)）。为什么其他选项不正确：

- **B** 不正确，因为 ACM 公共证书是 ACM 颁发的证书；ACM 不允许你在 ACM 中创建公共证书并选择特定的外部第三方公共 CA 对其签名。如果证书必须由特定的第三方 CA 签名，AWS 表示应在 AWS 之外获取该证书并将其导入 ACM（[ACM import certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/import-certificate.html)；[ACM public certificates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/gs-acm-request-public.html)）。
- **C** 不正确，原因有两个：它描述了在 ACM 中创建由第三方 CA 签名的证书，然后再导入，这不是受支持的第三方 CA 工作流；此外，Lambda 函数 URL 的创建/配置支持诸如身份验证类型和 CORS 等设置，而不是附加自定义 TLS 证书（[Lambda function URL configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)）。
- **D** 不正确，原因与 B 和 C 相同：ACM 不能颁发由所选第三方 CA 签名的公共证书，并且 Lambda 函数 URLs 在文档化的函数 URL 设置中不提供自定义证书配置选项（[Lambda function URL configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/urls-configuration.html)）。

en.question: A company runs an application on AWS. The application receives inconsistent amounts of usage. The application uses AWS Direct Connect to connect to an on-premises MySQL-compatible database. The on- premises database consistently uses a minimum of 2 GiB of memory. The company wants to migrate the on-premises database to a managed AWS service. The company wants to use auto scaling capabilities to manage unexpected workload increases. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Provision an Amazon DynamoDB database with default read and write capacity settings.
options.B: Provision an Amazon Aurora database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
options.C: Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
options.D: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 2 GiB of memory.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 ACU.**

Aurora is a managed relational database engine that is compatible with MySQL, so it fits the migration target for an on-premises MySQL-compatible database ([Amazon Aurora overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)). Aurora Serverless is designed for variable or “spiky” workloads: AWS states that it automatically scales capacity to meet peak load and scales back down after the surge, avoiding the need to provision for peak or average capacity ([Aurora Serverless use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)). Each Aurora capacity unit (ACU) is approximately **2 GiB of memory** plus corresponding CPU and networking, so a **minimum of 1 ACU** matches the database’s consistent minimum 2 GiB memory requirement ([Aurora Serverless capacity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)). Aurora Serverless also continuously tracks CPU, memory, and network load and scales up or down as needed, with scaling in increments as small as 0.5 ACUs and no disruption to active operations ([Aurora Serverless scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. DynamoDB** is not a MySQL-compatible relational database. AWS distinguishes DynamoDB as a NoSQL database with a different design model from RDBMS systems ([NoSQL design for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)).
- **B. Provisioned Amazon Aurora with 1 ACU** is not the best fit. Aurora Serverless capacity is measured in ACUs; provisioned Aurora uses DB instance classes. AWS notes that, for a provisioned cluster, scaling up requires adding a whole DB instance, whereas Aurora Serverless can scale granularly by ACUs ([Aurora Serverless use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)).
- **D. Amazon RDS for MySQL with 2 GiB of memory** is MySQL-compatible, but it does not provide the same automatic compute and memory scaling for unpredictable workloads. RDS storage autoscaling addresses storage capacity, not automatic compute/memory scaling for unexpected workload increases ([RDS storage autoscaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS 上运行一个应用程序。该应用程序接收的使用量不一致。该应用程序使用 AWS Direct Connect 连接到本地 MySQL 兼容数据库。本地数据库始终至少使用 2 GiB 内存。公司希望将本地数据库迁移到托管 AWS 服务。公司希望使用自动扩展功能来管理意外的工作负载增加。哪种解决方案能够以最少的管理开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 预置一个使用默认读写容量设置的 Amazon DynamoDB 数据库。
options.B: 预置一个最小容量为 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU) 的 Amazon Aurora 数据库。
options.C: 预置一个最小容量为 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU) 的 Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 数据库。
options.D: 预置一个具有 2 GiB 内存的 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. 预置一个最小容量为 1 ACU 的 Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 数据库。**

Aurora 是一种托管关系数据库引擎，兼容 MySQL，因此适合作为本地 MySQL 兼容数据库的迁移目标（[Amazon Aurora overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)）。Aurora Serverless 专为可变或“突发型”工作负载而设计：AWS 表示，它会自动扩展容量以满足峰值负载，并在激增后缩减容量，从而避免需要按峰值或平均容量进行预置（[Aurora Serverless use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)）。每个 Aurora capacity unit (ACU) 约等于 **2 GiB 内存** 加上相应的 CPU 和网络，因此 **最小 1 ACU** 符合该数据库始终至少 2 GiB 内存的要求（[Aurora Serverless capacity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)）。Aurora Serverless 还会持续跟踪 CPU、内存和网络负载，并根据需要向上或向下扩展，扩展增量可小至 0.5 ACUs，并且不会中断活动操作（[Aurora Serverless scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. DynamoDB** 不是 MySQL 兼容的关系数据库。AWS 将 DynamoDB 区分为一种 NoSQL 数据库，其设计模型不同于 RDBMS 系统（[NoSQL design for DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)）。
- **B. Provisioned Amazon Aurora with 1 ACU** 不是最佳选择。Aurora Serverless 容量以 ACUs 衡量；预置的 Aurora 使用 DB instance classes。AWS 指出，对于预置集群，向上扩展需要添加整个 DB instance，而 Aurora Serverless 可以按 ACUs 进行精细扩展（[Aurora Serverless use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)）。
- **D. Amazon RDS for MySQL with 2 GiB of memory** 兼容 MySQL，但它无法为不可预测的工作负载提供相同的自动计算和内存扩展。RDS storage autoscaling 解决的是存储容量，而不是针对意外工作负载增加的自动计算/内存扩展（[RDS storage autoscaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html)）。

en.question: A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda functions that run on Java 11. The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.
options.B: Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.
options.C: Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.
options.D: Configure Lambda SnapStart.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D. Configure Lambda SnapStart.**

Lambda SnapStart is specifically intended to reduce cold-start latency caused by one-time initialization work. AWS says to use SnapStart to reduce initialization latency from seconds to as low as sub-second, and that it helps reduce outlier function initialization latency. It is supported for **Java 11 and later** managed runtimes. For Java managed runtimes, AWS states there is **no additional cost for SnapStart**, making it the most cost-effective fit for a Java 11 workload without strict latency requirements ([Lambda SnapStart](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/snapstart.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency** — Provisioned concurrency can reduce cold starts by keeping environments pre-initialized, but AWS recommends it when an application has **strict cold start latency requirements** that SnapStart cannot meet. It also runs continually and incurs separate billing, so it is not the most cost-effective option here ([Provisioned concurrency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html)).
- **B. Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions** — Timeout controls how long a function is allowed to run before timing out. It addresses long-running invocations or slow downstream services, not Java startup/cold-start latency ([Lambda timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html)).
- **C. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions** — Increasing memory also increases CPU and can improve performance for CPU-, network-, or memory-bound functions, but it is not the targeted, most cost-effective solution for reducing Java cold starts and scale-up outlier initialization latency ([Lambda memory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-memory.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司希望将事件驱动编程模型与 AWS Lambda 结合使用。该公司希望降低在 Java 11 上运行的 Lambda 函数的启动延迟。该公司对应用程序没有严格的延迟要求。该公司希望在函数扩展时减少冷启动和异常延迟。哪种解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置 Lambda provisioned concurrency。
options.B: 增加 Lambda 函数的超时时间。
options.C: 增加 Lambda 函数的内存。
options.D: 配置 Lambda SnapStart。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D. Configure Lambda SnapStart.**

Lambda SnapStart 专门用于减少由一次性初始化工作导致的冷启动延迟。AWS 表示，可使用 SnapStart 将初始化延迟从数秒降低到最低亚秒级，并且它有助于减少函数初始化延迟异常值。它支持 **Java 11 and later** 托管运行时。对于 Java 托管运行时，AWS 声明 **SnapStart 没有额外成本**，因此对于没有严格延迟要求的 Java 11 工作负载来说，它是最具成本效益的选择 ([Lambda SnapStart](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/snapstart.html))。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency** — Provisioned concurrency 可以通过保持环境预初始化来减少冷启动，但 AWS 建议在应用程序具有 **严格冷启动延迟要求** 且 SnapStart 无法满足时使用它。它还会持续运行并产生单独计费，因此在这里不是最具成本效益的选项 ([Provisioned concurrency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/provisioned-concurrency.html))。
- **B. Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions** — Timeout 控制函数在超时前允许运行的时长。它解决的是长时间运行的调用或缓慢的下游服务，而不是 Java 启动/冷启动延迟 ([Lambda timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html))。
- **C. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions** — 增加内存也会增加 CPU，并且可以改善 CPU、网络或内存受限函数的性能，但它不是用于减少 Java 冷启动和扩展时异常初始化延迟的、有针对性的最具成本效益的解决方案 ([Lambda memory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-memory.html))。

en.question: A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends. The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.
options.B: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.
options.C: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.
options.D: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Migrate to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.**

The workload runs for only about 2 hours per week, so the database should minimize compute cost during long idle periods. AWS documentation states that Aurora Serverless is intended for variable or spiky workloads, automatically scales capacity up and down, and is **cost-effective during periods of low activity** because you pay only for the database resources consumed and usage is measured on a per-second basis ([Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)). Aurora Serverless capacity can scale between configured ACU limits; supported Aurora MySQL versions can use a minimum of **0 ACUs**, allowing the cluster to scale to zero when no workload is running ([How Aurora serverless works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)). This best matches a database needed only briefly each week.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Aurora MySQL database cluster**: A standard/provisioned Aurora cluster uses fixed DB instances rather than serverless ACU scaling, so it does not provide the same granular scale-down and per-second consumed-capacity benefit described for Aurora Serverless ([Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)).
- **C. EC2 instance running MySQL with a reservation**: This adds self-managed database administration and a long-term cost commitment. AWS documentation says EC2 Reserved Instances reduce cost by committing to a specific instance configuration for **1 or 3 years**, which is not cost-effective for a database used only 2 hours per week ([Amazon EC2 pricing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/concepts.html)).
- **D. ECS tasks running MySQL containers**: This would require running and managing MySQL yourself on container infrastructure, rather than using a managed relational database service, and it does not provide the Aurora Serverless database capacity scaling and low-activity cost benefits documented for this use case ([Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)).

zh.question: 一家金融服务公司发布了一个使用 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库的新应用程序。该公司使用该应用程序跟踪股票市场趋势。公司只需要在每周结束时运行该应用程序 2 小时。公司需要优化运行数据库的成本。哪种解决方案将以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 将现有的 RDS for MySQL 数据库迁移到 Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL 数据库集群。
options.B: 将现有的 RDS for MySQL 数据库迁移到 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群。
options.C: 将现有的 RDS for MySQL 数据库迁移到运行 MySQL 的 Amazon EC2 实例。为该 EC2 实例购买实例预留。
options.D: 将现有的 RDS for MySQL 数据库迁移到 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 集群，该集群使用 MySQL 容器镜像来运行任务。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 迁移到 Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL 数据库集群。**

该工作负载每周只运行约 2 小时，因此数据库应在长时间空闲期间最大限度地降低计算成本。AWS 文档指出，Aurora Serverless 旨在用于可变或突发型工作负载，会自动向上和向下扩展容量，并且由于你只需为消耗的数据库资源付费且使用量按秒计量，因此在**低活动期间具有成本效益**（[Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)）。Aurora Serverless 容量可以在配置的 ACU 限制之间扩展；受支持的 Aurora MySQL 版本可以使用最低 **0 ACUs**，从而允许集群在没有工作负载运行时扩展到零（[How Aurora serverless works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)）。这最符合每周仅短时间需要数据库的情况。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. Aurora MySQL 数据库集群**：标准/预置 Aurora 集群使用固定的 DB 实例，而不是无服务器 ACU 扩展，因此它无法提供 Aurora Serverless 所描述的同样精细的缩减能力和按秒计量的已消耗容量优势（[Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)）。
- **C. 运行 MySQL 并带有预留的 EC2 实例**：这会增加自管理数据库管理工作以及长期成本承诺。AWS 文档说明，EC2 Reserved Instances 通过承诺使用特定实例配置 **1 或 3 年** 来降低成本，这对于每周只使用 2 小时的数据库并不具备成本效益（[Amazon EC2 pricing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/concepts.html)）。
- **D. 运行 MySQL 容器的 ECS 任务**：这将需要你在容器基础设施上自行运行和管理 MySQL，而不是使用托管关系数据库服务，并且它不提供文档中针对该用例所说明的 Aurora Serverless 数据库容量扩展和低活动成本优势（[Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)）。

en.question: A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
options.B: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
options.C: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
options.D: Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **C. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.**

An Amazon RDS **Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment** is designed for this exact combination of requirements: it is a semisynchronous, high availability deployment with a writer and **two readable replica DB instances** across three Availability Zones in the same Region. AWS states that Multi-AZ DB clusters provide **high availability** and **increased capacity for read workloads** compared with Multi-AZ DB instance deployments. The reader DB instances can serve read traffic and also act as automatic failover targets, which gives the most operationally efficient managed solution for a PostgreSQL database workload in one Region ([RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. DynamoDB global tables**: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service, not a PostgreSQL database engine. This does not meet the stated PostgreSQL requirement ([DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)).
- **B. RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment**: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance deployment provides failover support, but AWS explicitly says its single standby DB instance **doesn't serve read traffic**. Therefore, it does not satisfy the requirement for increased read capacity as efficiently as a Multi-AZ DB cluster ([RDS Multi-AZ deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)).
- **D. RDS cross-Region read replicas**: RDS read replicas can scale read-heavy workloads, but they use asynchronous replication and must be created/managed separately. Cross-Region read replicas are primarily useful when the replica must be in another Region; the question describes an application in a single Region and asks for high availability plus read scaling with the most operational efficiency ([RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司在某个 AWS Region 中，将其应用程序部署在 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 上。该应用程序需要将数据存储在 PostgreSQL 数据库引擎中。公司希望数据库中的数据具有高可用性。公司还需要提高读取工作负载的容量。哪种解决方案能够以最高的运维效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个配置了 global tables 的 Amazon DynamoDB 数据库表。
options.B: 创建一个采用 Multi-AZ deployments 的 Amazon RDS 数据库。
options.C: 创建一个采用 Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment 的 Amazon RDS 数据库。
options.D: 创建一个配置了 cross-Region read replicas 的 Amazon RDS 数据库。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **C. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.**

Amazon RDS **Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment** 正是为这种需求组合而设计的：它是一种半同步的高可用性部署，在同一 Region 的三个 Availability Zones 中包含一个写入器和 **两个可读取的副本 DB instances**。AWS 说明，与 Multi-AZ DB instance deployments 相比，Multi-AZ DB clusters 提供 **高可用性** 和 **提高的读取工作负载容量**。读取器 DB instances 可以处理读取流量，也可以作为自动故障转移目标，这为单个 Region 中的 PostgreSQL 数据库工作负载提供了运维效率最高的托管解决方案（[RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/multi-az-db-clusters-concepts.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. DynamoDB global tables**：DynamoDB 是一种 NoSQL 数据库服务，不是 PostgreSQL 数据库引擎。这不满足题目所述的 PostgreSQL 要求（[DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)）。
- **B. RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment**：传统的 Multi-AZ DB instance deployment 提供故障转移支持，但 AWS 明确表示其单个备用 DB instance **doesn't serve read traffic**。因此，它不能像 Multi-AZ DB cluster 那样高效地满足提高读取容量的要求（[RDS Multi-AZ deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)）。
- **D. RDS cross-Region read replicas**：RDS read replicas 可以扩展读取密集型工作负载，但它们使用异步复制，并且必须单独创建和管理。Cross-Region read replicas 主要在副本必须位于另一个 Region 时有用；题目描述的是单个 Region 中的应用程序，并要求以最高运维效率实现高可用性和读取扩展（[RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。

en.question: A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users. Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.A: Private endpoint
options.B: Regional endpoint
options.C: Interface VPC endpoint
options.D: Edge-optimized endpoint

en.explanation:
The best answer is **D. Edge-optimized endpoint**.

AWS documentation states that an **edge-optimized API endpoint** for API Gateway REST APIs “typically routes requests to the nearest CloudFront Point of Presence (POP),” which can help when clients are **geographically distributed**. That directly matches the requirement to reduce API request latency for globally distributed users ([AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. Private endpoint** — A private API endpoint is accessible only from an Amazon VPC through an interface VPC endpoint, so it is not intended for public, geographically distributed web users ([AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)).
- **B. Regional endpoint** — A Regional API endpoint is intended for clients in the same AWS Region, not primarily for globally distributed users ([AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)).
- **C. Interface VPC endpoint** — This is the VPC endpoint mechanism used to access private API endpoints from within a VPC, not the API Gateway endpoint type that optimizes latency for global clients ([AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS 上使用 Amazon API Gateway 和 AWS Lambda 构建一个 RESTful 无服务器 Web 应用程序。该 Web 应用程序的用户将在地理位置上分散分布，公司希望降低这些用户的 API 请求延迟。解决方案架构师应使用哪种类型的端点来满足这些要求？

options.A: 私有端点
options.B: 区域端点
options.C: 接口 VPC 端点
options.D: 边缘优化端点

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **D. 边缘优化端点**。

AWS 文档指出，API Gateway REST API 的 **边缘优化 API 端点** “通常会将请求路由到最近的 CloudFront 接入点（POP）”，这在客户端 **地理位置分散** 时会有所帮助。这直接符合为全球分布用户降低 API 请求延迟的要求（[AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. 私有端点** — 私有 API 端点只能通过接口 VPC 端点从 Amazon VPC 访问，因此它并不适用于公共的、地理位置分散的 Web 用户（[AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)）。
- **B. 区域端点** — 区域 API 端点适用于同一 AWS Region 中的客户端，而不是主要用于全球分布的用户（[AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)）。
- **C. 接口 VPC 端点** — 这是用于从 VPC 内访问私有 API 端点的 VPC 端点机制，并不是为全球客户端优化延迟的 API Gateway 端点类型（[AWS API Gateway endpoint types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)）。

en.question: A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content pages for its website. The company needs to ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website. The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.
options.B: Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.
options.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.
options.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.**

Use **AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)** to request the public TLS certificate for the CloudFront website and use **DNS validation**. CloudFront documentation recommends using a public certificate issued by ACM and states that, for viewer HTTPS with CloudFront, the ACM certificate must be requested/imported in **US East (N. Virginia) (`us-east-1`)**. It also states that if you use ACM-provided certificates, **ACM manages certificate renewals** for you ([CloudFront certificate requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html)). ACM documentation further states that ACM renews certificates automatically when using **DNS validation**, and DNS CNAME records allow both initial domain ownership validation and ongoing automated certificate renewal ([ACM managed renewal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/managed-renewal.html), [ACM DNS validation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/dns-validation.html)). This is the most operationally efficient option.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. CloudFront security policy**: A CloudFront security policy is not a certificate creation mechanism. CloudFront requires an SSL/TLS certificate from ACM or another supported CA; the docs recommend ACM for CloudFront certificates ([CloudFront certificate requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html)).
- **B. CloudFront origin access control (OAC)**: OAC is used to secure access from CloudFront to an S3 origin by signing origin requests and granting CloudFront permission to access the bucket. It does not create viewer TLS certificates ([CloudFront OAC for S3 origins](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)).
- **D. ACM with email validation**: ACM can issue certificates with email validation, but ACM documentation contrasts DNS validation with email notices: automatic renewal is provided when using DNS validation, while email validation involves email notices as expiration approaches. Therefore, DNS validation is more operationally efficient for automated renewal ([ACM managed renewal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/managed-renewal.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 Amazon CloudFront 分配为其网站提供内容页面。公司需要确保客户端在访问公司网站时使用 TLS 证书。公司希望自动创建和续订 TLS 证书。哪种解决方案能够以最高运营效率满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 CloudFront 安全策略创建证书。
options.B: 使用 CloudFront origin access control (OAC) 创建证书。
options.C: 使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 创建证书。对域名使用 DNS 验证。
options.D: 使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 创建证书。对域名使用电子邮件验证。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C。**

使用 **AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)** 为 CloudFront 网站请求公有 TLS 证书，并使用 **DNS validation**。CloudFront 文档建议使用由 ACM 颁发的公有证书，并说明对于使用 CloudFront 的查看器 HTTPS，ACM 证书必须在 **US East (N. Virginia) (`us-east-1`)** 中请求/导入。它还说明，如果你使用 ACM 提供的证书，**ACM 会为你管理证书续订**（[CloudFront certificate requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html)）。ACM 文档进一步说明，在使用 **DNS validation** 时，ACM 会自动续订证书，并且 DNS CNAME 记录既允许初始域名所有权验证，也允许持续的自动证书续订（[ACM managed renewal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/managed-renewal.html)，[ACM DNS validation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/dns-validation.html)）。这是运营效率最高的选项。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. CloudFront 安全策略**：CloudFront 安全策略不是证书创建机制。CloudFront 需要来自 ACM 或其他受支持 CA 的 SSL/TLS 证书；文档建议将 ACM 用于 CloudFront 证书（[CloudFront certificate requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html)）。
- **B. CloudFront origin access control (OAC)**：OAC 用于通过签署源请求并授予 CloudFront 访问存储桶的权限，来保护从 CloudFront 到 S3 源的访问。它不会创建查看器 TLS 证书（[CloudFront OAC for S3 origins](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)）。
- **D. 使用电子邮件验证的 ACM**：ACM 可以通过电子邮件验证颁发证书，但 ACM 文档将 DNS 验证与电子邮件通知进行了对比：使用 DNS 验证时会提供自动续订，而电子邮件验证会在临近过期时涉及电子邮件通知。因此，对于自动续订，DNS 验证在运营上更高效（[ACM managed renewal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/managed-renewal.html)）。

en.question: A company deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a database layer. The application has experienced a large increase in users. The company wants to improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds and to cache requests to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
options.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.
options.C: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.
options.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).**

DAX is purpose-built for this exact DynamoDB use case. AWS describes DAX as a **DynamoDB-compatible caching service** that provides fast in-memory performance. It reduces eventually consistent read response times from **single-digit milliseconds to microseconds**, and it reduces operational/application complexity because it is a **managed service** and is API-compatible with DynamoDB, requiring only minimal application changes. AWS also notes that DAX is suitable for read-heavy or bursty workloads and repeated reads, which matches the need to cache database requests during increased user traffic ([AWS DynamoDB DAX documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift** — Redshift is a petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse for analytics/query workloads, not a low-latency cache for an existing DynamoDB application ([Amazon Redshift documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/welcome.html)). Migrating would add significant operational and application overhead and does not directly meet the DynamoDB caching requirement.
- **C. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS** — RDS is a relational database service, not a DynamoDB-compatible microsecond-latency cache. Migrating from DynamoDB to RDS would require schema/application changes and would not be the least operational overhead.
- **D. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis** — ElastiCache can be used as a cache, but it is not DynamoDB-compatible in the same way DAX is. DAX is specifically designed to cache DynamoDB reads with minimal functional changes and microsecond latency, making it the lower-overhead and more targeted solution ([AWS DynamoDB DAX documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司部署了一个使用 Amazon DynamoDB 作为数据库层的无服务器应用程序。该应用程序的用户数量大幅增加。公司希望将数据库响应时间从毫秒级提升到微秒级，并缓存对数据库的请求。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)。
options.B: 将数据库迁移到 Amazon Redshift。
options.C: 将数据库迁移到 Amazon RDS。
options.D: 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 使用 DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)。**

DAX 正是为这种 DynamoDB 使用场景专门构建的。AWS 将 DAX 描述为一种**与 DynamoDB 兼容的缓存服务**，可提供快速的内存性能。它将最终一致性读取响应时间从**个位数毫秒降低到微秒级**，并且由于它是一项**托管服务**且与 DynamoDB API 兼容，只需对应用程序进行最少更改，因此可降低运营/应用程序复杂性。AWS 还指出，DAX 适用于读取密集型或突发型工作负载以及重复读取，这与在用户流量增加期间缓存数据库请求的需求相匹配（[AWS DynamoDB DAX documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. 将数据库迁移到 Amazon Redshift** — Redshift 是用于分析/查询工作负载的 PB 级云数据仓库，而不是用于现有 DynamoDB 应用程序的低延迟缓存（[Amazon Redshift documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/welcome.html)）。迁移会增加大量运营和应用程序开销，并且不能直接满足 DynamoDB 缓存需求。
- **C. 将数据库迁移到 Amazon RDS** — RDS 是一种关系型数据库服务，而不是与 DynamoDB 兼容的微秒级延迟缓存。从 DynamoDB 迁移到 RDS 需要架构/应用程序变更，并且不会是运营开销最少的方案。
- **D. 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis** — ElastiCache 可以用作缓存，但它不像 DAX 那样与 DynamoDB 兼容。DAX 专门设计用于以最少的功能更改和微秒级延迟缓存 DynamoDB 读取，因此它是开销更低且更有针对性的解决方案（[AWS DynamoDB DAX documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)）。

en.question: A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives traffic only on weekdays during business hours. The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.
options.B: Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.
options.C: Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.
options.D: Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** The workload has a predictable schedule: weekdays during business hours. AWS documentation for Instance Scheduler on AWS states that it can automatically start and stop **Amazon RDS** instances, and its sample schedule specifically shows a weekday 9-to-5 pattern that starts instances at 9 AM and stops them at 5 PM Monday–Friday. This directly reduces operational overhead because the scheduling is automated, and it reduces cost because Amazon RDS documentation states that while a DB instance is stopped, you are **not charged for DB instance hours** (though storage/backup charges still apply). [Instance Scheduler sample schedules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/instance-scheduler-on-aws/sample-schedules.html), [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html)

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Turn off automatic backups and create weekly manual snapshots** — This is primarily a backup-retention change, not a compute cost optimization for predictable idle hours. Manual snapshots still contribute to backup storage, and replacing automated backups with weekly manual snapshots increases operational overhead and reduces recovery granularity. AWS states that RDS backup storage includes both automated backups and manual DB snapshots. [Introduction to backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html)
- **C. Create a custom Lambda function based on minimum CPU utilization** — A custom function increases operational overhead compared with the AWS-provided Instance Scheduler solution. Also, CPU utilization is not the right trigger when the usage pattern is already known by business hours; a time-based schedule is simpler and more reliable.
- **D. Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances** — Reserved DB instances can reduce hourly rates, but they are a term commitment. AWS documentation states that All Upfront requires full payment at the start of the term with no other costs for the remainder of the term **regardless of the number of hours used**, and that upfront costs are billed regardless of resource usage. That does not take advantage of stopping the database during nights and weekends. [Reserved DB instances for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithReservedDBInstances.html)

zh.question: 一家公司运行一个使用 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 的应用程序。该应用程序仅在工作日的业务时间接收流量。公司希望根据这种使用情况优化成本并减少运营开销。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Instance Scheduler on AWS 配置启动和停止计划。
options.B: 关闭自动备份。每周创建数据库的手动快照。
options.C: 创建自定义 AWS Lambda 函数，根据最低 CPU 利用率启动和停止数据库。
options.D: 购买 All Upfront reserved DB instances。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.** 该工作负载具有可预测的计划：工作日的业务时间。Instance Scheduler on AWS 的 AWS 文档说明，它可以自动启动和停止 **Amazon RDS** 实例，其示例计划专门展示了工作日 9-to-5 模式：周一至周五上午 9 点启动实例，下午 5 点停止实例。这直接减少了运营开销，因为调度是自动化的；同时也降低了成本，因为 Amazon RDS 文档说明，当 DB instance 处于停止状态时，你**不会被收取 DB instance hours 费用**（但仍会产生存储/备份费用）。[Instance Scheduler sample schedules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/instance-scheduler-on-aws/sample-schedules.html), [Stopping an Amazon RDS DB instance temporarily](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_StopInstance.html)

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. Turn off automatic backups and create weekly manual snapshots** — 这主要是备份保留方面的更改，而不是针对可预测空闲时段的计算成本优化。手动快照仍会产生备份存储，使用每周手动快照替代自动备份会增加运营开销，并降低恢复粒度。AWS 说明，RDS 备份存储包括自动备份和手动 DB 快照。[Introduction to backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html)
- **C. Create a custom Lambda function based on minimum CPU utilization** — 与 AWS 提供的 Instance Scheduler 解决方案相比，自定义函数会增加运营开销。此外，当使用模式已经由业务时间确定时，CPU 利用率并不是合适的触发条件；基于时间的计划更简单且更可靠。
- **D.
