Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances** — Reserved DB instances 可以降低小时费率，但它们是期限承诺。AWS 文档说明，All Upfront 要求在期限开始时全额付款，在剩余期限内不会产生其他费用，**无论使用了多少小时**，并且预付费用会被计费而不考虑资源使用情况。这无法利用在夜间和周末停止数据库所带来的优势。[Reserved DB instances for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithReservedDBInstances.html)

en.question: A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
options.B: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
options.C: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
options.D: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D.**

The application currently uses locally attached storage and the company wants a lift-and-shift migration without changing the application architecture. Amazon EBS is the closest fit among the options because an EBS volume is a **block-level storage device that you attach to an EC2 instance** and can use “as you would use a physical hard drive” ([Amazon EBS volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes.html)). For cost-effectiveness, **gp3** is the best EBS choice: AWS documents gp3 as the **lowest cost SSD volume offered by Amazon EBS**, with a balance of price/performance, single-digit millisecond latency, independently provisionable performance, and **20% lower price per GiB than gp2** ([Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. FSx for Lustre with an Auto Scaling group** — FSx for Lustre is a high-performance **file system** intended for workloads such as HPC, machine learning, video processing, and financial modeling; it is not the most direct replacement for locally attached block storage in a lift-and-shift scenario ([What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)). An Auto Scaling group is also unnecessary when the requirement is simply to host the existing application without changing architecture.
- **B. EC2 with EBS gp2** — EBS is appropriate, but gp2 is less cost-effective than gp3. AWS states that gp3 provides more predictable performance scaling and can be up to 20% lower priced than gp2 ([Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html)).
- **C. FSx for OpenZFS with an Auto Scaling group** — FSx for OpenZFS is a fully managed **file storage** service accessed through NFS and is designed to replace file servers, not to act as directly attached block storage for a simple lift-and-shift EC2 deployment ([What is Amazon FSx for OpenZFS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/OpenZFSGuide/what-is-fsx.html)). The Auto Scaling group also adds complexity not required by the question.

zh.question: 一家公司在本地使用本地附加存储来运行一个对延迟敏感的应用程序。该公司正在使用直接迁移（lift and shift）方法将该应用程序迁移到 AWS Cloud。该公司不想更改应用程序架构。哪种解决方案能够以最高成本效益满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置一个包含 Amazon EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组。使用 Amazon FSx for Lustre 文件系统来运行该应用程序。
options.B: 在 Amazon EC2 实例上托管该应用程序。使用 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 卷来运行该应用程序。
options.C: 配置一个包含 Amazon EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组。使用 Amazon FSx for OpenZFS 文件系统来运行该应用程序。
options.D: 在 Amazon EC2 实例上托管该应用程序。使用 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 卷来运行该应用程序。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D.**

该应用程序当前使用本地附加存储，并且公司希望在不更改应用程序架构的情况下进行直接迁移。Amazon EBS 是这些选项中最接近的匹配项，因为 EBS 卷是一个**可附加到 EC2 实例的块级存储设备**，并且可以“像使用物理硬盘一样”使用它（[Amazon EBS volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes.html)）。从成本效益角度来看，**gp3** 是最佳 EBS 选择：AWS 文档将 gp3 描述为 **Amazon EBS 提供的最低成本 SSD 卷**，在价格/性能方面取得平衡，具有个位数毫秒延迟、可独立预置的性能，并且**每 GiB 价格比 gp2 低 20%**（[Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. FSx for Lustre with an Auto Scaling group** — FSx for Lustre 是一种高性能**文件系统**，面向 HPC、机器学习、视频处理和金融建模等工作负载；在直接迁移场景中，它并不是本地附加块存储最直接的替代方案（[What is Amazon FSx for Lustre?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html)）。当要求只是托管现有应用程序且不更改架构时，Auto Scaling 组也并非必要。
- **B. EC2 with EBS gp2** — EBS 是合适的，但 gp2 不如 gp3 具有成本效益。AWS 表示，gp3 提供更可预测的性能扩展，并且价格最多可比 gp2 低 20%（[Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html)）。
- **C. FSx for OpenZFS with an Auto Scaling group** — FSx for OpenZFS 是一种完全托管的**文件存储**服务，通过 NFS 访问，设计用于替代文件服务器，而不是在简单的直接迁移 EC2 部署中充当直接附加的块存储（[What is Amazon FSx for OpenZFS?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/OpenZFSGuide/what-is-fsx.html)）。Auto Scaling 组也增加了题目并不需要的复杂性。

en.question: A company runs a stateful production application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires at least two EC2 instances to always be running. A solutions architect needs to design a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture for the application. The solutions architect creates an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances. Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

options.A: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.
options.B: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.
options.C: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.
options.D: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.**

The application requires **at least two EC2 instances to always be running**, even during an Availability Zone failure. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling distributes desired capacity across specified Availability Zones and maintains balance across them when multiple AZs are configured ([Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)). AWS also describes AZ distribution strategies for applications that need Availability Zone redundancy and notes that a group can tolerate the loss of an AZ only when it has sufficient capacity in the remaining AZs ([Auto Scaling group Availability Zone distribution](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-availability-zone-balanced.html)). With **four On-Demand Instances split as two in each of two AZs**, the loss of one AZ still leaves two running instances in the other AZ, meeting the requirement.

- **A is wrong:** A minimum of two with one instance in each of two AZs provides AZ redundancy, but if one AZ fails, only one instance remains running immediately. That does not satisfy the requirement for at least two instances to always be running.
- **C is wrong:** All instances are in one Availability Zone, so the design is not highly available or fault tolerant to an AZ failure. It also uses Spot Instances, which Amazon EC2 can terminate as capacity or price changes ([Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)).
- **D is wrong:** Although the group has four instances across two AZs, two of them are Spot Instances. Spot Instances can be terminated by Amazon EC2, so they are not appropriate for guaranteeing the required minimum capacity for this stateful production application ([Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司在 Amazon EC2 实例上运行一个有状态的生产应用程序。该应用程序要求始终至少有两个 EC2 实例处于运行状态。解决方案架构师需要为该应用程序设计一个高可用且容错的架构。解决方案架构师创建了一个 EC2 实例的 Auto Scaling 组。解决方案架构师还应采取哪一组额外步骤来满足这些要求？

options.A: 将 Auto Scaling 组的最小容量设置为两个。在一个 Availability Zone 中部署一个 On-Demand Instance，并在第二个 Availability Zone 中部署一个 On-Demand Instance。
options.B: 将 Auto Scaling 组的最小容量设置为四个。在一个 Availability Zone 中部署两个 On-Demand Instances，并在第二个 Availability Zone 中部署两个 On-Demand Instances。
options.C: 将 Auto Scaling 组的最小容量设置为两个。在一个 Availability Zone 中部署四个 Spot Instances。
options.D: 将 Auto Scaling 组的最小容量设置为四个。在一个 Availability Zone 中部署两个 On-Demand Instances，并在第二个 Availability Zone 中部署两个 Spot Instances。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。**

该应用程序要求**始终至少有两个 EC2 实例处于运行状态**，即使在发生 Availability Zone 故障期间也是如此。Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 会在指定的 Availability Zones 中分配所需容量，并在配置多个 AZ 时维持它们之间的平衡（[Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)）。AWS 还描述了适用于需要 Availability Zone 冗余的应用程序的 AZ 分布策略，并指出只有当组在其余 AZ 中具有足够容量时，才能容忍一个 AZ 的丢失（[Auto Scaling group Availability Zone distribution](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-availability-zone-balanced.html)）。使用**四个 On-Demand Instances，并在两个 AZ 中各分配两个**，即使一个 AZ 丢失，另一个 AZ 中仍有两个正在运行的实例，从而满足要求。

- **A 错误：** 最小容量为两个，并在两个 AZ 中各有一个实例，可以提供 AZ 冗余，但如果一个 AZ 发生故障，立即只会剩下一个实例在运行。这不满足始终至少有两个实例运行的要求。
- **C 错误：** 所有实例都位于一个 Availability Zone 中，因此该设计对于 AZ 故障而言并不是高可用或容错的。它还使用 Spot Instances，而 Amazon EC2 可在容量或价格变化时终止这些实例（[Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)）。
- **D 错误：** 尽管该组在两个 AZ 中共有四个实例，但其中两个是 Spot Instances。Spot Instances 可能会被 Amazon EC2 终止，因此不适合为这个有状态生产应用程序保证所需的最小容量（[Auto Scaling groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html)）。

en.question: An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud. The company's on-premises data center is near the us-west-1 Region. The company uses the eu-central-1 Region to host the website. The company wants to minimize load time for the website as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the traffic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center. Send the traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1.
options.B: Set up a simple routing policy that routes all traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all traffic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.
options.C: Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.
options.D: Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the traffic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** Route 53 **geolocation routing** lets you choose the resources that serve traffic based on the geographic location of the users/DNS queries. AWS gives the example of routing all queries from Europe to a load balancer in the Frankfurt Region, and notes that geolocation routing can be used so that each user location is consistently routed to the same endpoint ([Route 53 geolocation routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html)). Therefore, routing users near the on-premises data center to that data center and users near `eu-central-1` to the AWS-hosted site best matches the requirement to minimize website load time based on user proximity.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B:** Simple routing is only standard DNS routing with no special Route 53 routing such as weighted or latency; it typically routes traffic to a single resource, and if multiple values are specified Route 53 returns them in random order ([Route 53 simple routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-simple.html)). It cannot implement location-aware routing.
- **C:** Latency-based routing is intended to serve requests from the **AWS Region** that provides the lowest latency, using Route 53 latency data between users and AWS data centers. AWS specifically warns that if resources are not in an AWS Region, actual latency to those resources can vary significantly from AWS latency data ([Route 53 latency-based routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html)). Also, associating only with `us-west-1` would not route between both the on-premises endpoint and `eu-central-1` as required.
- **D:** Weighted routing distributes traffic according to assigned weights/proportions, which is useful for load balancing or testing, not for sending each user to the nearest/lowest-load-time location ([Route 53 weighted routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-weighted.html)). Splitting traffic evenly could send European users to the on-premises data center or western US users to Europe, increasing load time.

zh.question: 一家电子商务公司使用 Amazon Route 53 作为其 DNS 提供商。该公司在本地和 AWS Cloud 中托管其网站。该公司的本地数据中心靠近 us-west-1 Region。该公司使用 eu-central-1 Region 来托管网站。该公司希望尽可能缩短网站的加载时间。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 设置地理位置路由策略。将靠近 us-west-1 的流量发送到本地数据中心。将靠近 eu-central-1 的流量发送到 eu-central-1。
options.B: 设置简单路由策略，将所有靠近 eu-central-1 的流量路由到 eu-central-1，并将所有靠近本地数据中心的流量路由到本地数据中心。
options.C: 设置延迟路由策略。将该策略与 us-west-1 关联。
options.D: 设置加权路由策略。在 eu-central-1 和本地数据中心之间平均分配流量。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.** Route 53 **geolocation routing** 允许你根据用户/DNS 查询的地理位置选择为流量提供服务的资源。AWS 给出的示例是将来自欧洲的所有查询路由到 Frankfurt Region 中的负载均衡器，并指出可以使用地理位置路由，使每个用户位置始终路由到相同的端点（[Route 53 geolocation routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html)）。因此，将靠近本地数据中心的用户路由到该数据中心，并将靠近 `eu-central-1` 的用户路由到 AWS 托管的网站，最符合根据用户接近程度来最小化网站加载时间的要求。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B:** 简单路由只是标准 DNS 路由，没有加权或延迟等特殊 Route 53 路由；它通常将流量路由到单个资源，并且如果指定了多个值，Route 53 会以随机顺序返回它们（[Route 53 simple routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-simple.html)）。它无法实现位置感知路由。
- **C:** 基于延迟的路由旨在从提供最低延迟的 **AWS Region** 为请求提供服务，使用 Route 53 在用户和 AWS 数据中心之间的延迟数据。AWS 特别警告，如果资源不在 AWS Region 中，到这些资源的实际延迟可能会与 AWS 延迟数据有显著差异（[Route 53 latency-based routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html)）。此外，仅与 `us-west-1` 关联无法按要求在本地端点和 `eu-central-1` 之间进行路由。
- **D:** 加权路由根据分配的权重/比例分配流量，这对于负载均衡或测试很有用，但不适合将每个用户发送到最近/最低加载时间的位置（[Route 53 weighted routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-weighted.html)）。平均拆分流量可能会将欧洲用户发送到本地数据中心，或将美国西部用户发送到欧洲，从而增加加载时间。

en.question: A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
options.B: Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.C: Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball. Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.D: Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud. Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.

en.explanation:
**Answer: C.**

For this exam scenario, the most cost-effective way to migrate **5 PB** within **6 months** over only a **1 Gbps** uplink is to avoid sending the bulk data across the internet. AWS Snowball Edge is designed for physical data transfer: AWS documentation states that each Snowball Edge device can transport data “at speeds faster than the internet” by shipping the device, and that Snowball Edge can import data between local environments and Amazon S3 without using the internet ([Snowball Edge overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)). Snowball Edge storage-optimized devices provide large local capacity—210 TB usable per device—so multiple devices can handle petabyte-scale migration ([Snowball Edge device configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/device-differences.html)). AWS documentation also identifies a Snowball Edge configuration for the Storage Gateway **Tape Gateway** type ([TGWOnDeviceServiceConfiguration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/api-reference/API_TGWOnDeviceServiceConfiguration.html)). After ingestion to S3, S3 Lifecycle can transition objects to **S3 Glacier Deep Archive** for long-term archival, and AWS explicitly supports Lifecycle transitions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive ([S3 Lifecycle transitions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)).

Why the other options are not best:

- **A**: DataSync over a 1 Gbps internet link for 5 PB is unlikely to meet the 6-month migration requirement, and it targets **S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval**, which is not the lowest-cost archival class for 10-year retention compared with Deep Archive.
- **B**: Writing directly to S3 Glacier Deep Archive over the 1 Gbps uplink still depends on the constrained internet connection for the full 5 PB transfer.
- **D**: An on-premises Tape Gateway is appropriate for ongoing tape-style backup, but Tape Gateway uploads virtual tape data asynchronously to AWS; it still relies on the 1 Gbps uplink for the full dataset. Tape Gateway itself is a cost-effective cloud-backed virtual tape solution and can archive to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, but the network bottleneck makes it unsuitable for this one-time 5 PB migration within 6 months ([Tape Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html), [How Tape Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)).

*Note: Current AWS documentation notes that Snowball Edge and Tape Gateway on Snow Family devices are no longer available to new customers; however, among the options as framed in this SAA-C03-style question, option C is the architecture AWS documentation supports for bypassing the internet bottleneck and landing long-term archival data in Deep Archive.*

zh.question: 一家公司在物理磁带上有 5 PB 的归档数据。出于合规目的，公司需要将这些磁带上的数据再保留 10 年。公司希望在未来 6 个月内迁移到 AWS。存放这些磁带的数据中心具有 1 Gbps 的上行互联网连接。哪种解决方案能够以最低成本满足这些要求？

options.A: 在本地读取磁带中的数据。将数据暂存到本地 NFS 存储中。使用 AWS DataSync 将数据迁移到 Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval。
options.B: 使用本地备份应用程序读取磁带中的数据，并直接写入 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive。
options.C: 订购多台带有 Tape Gateway 的 AWS Snowball 设备。将物理磁带复制到 Snowball 中的虚拟磁带。将 Snowball 设备运送到 AWS。创建生命周期策略，将磁带移动到 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive。
options.D: 配置本地 Tape Gateway。在 AWS Cloud 中创建虚拟磁带。使用备份软件将物理磁带复制到虚拟磁带。

zh.explanation:
**答案：C.**

对于此考试场景，要在仅有 **1 Gbps** uplink 的情况下于 **6 个月** 内迁移 **5 PB** 数据，最具成本效益的方法是避免通过互联网发送大部分数据。AWS Snowball Edge 专为物理数据传输而设计：AWS 文档说明，每台 Snowball Edge 设备都可以通过运输设备以“快于互联网的速度”传输数据，并且 Snowball Edge 可以在本地环境和 Amazon S3 之间导入数据而无需使用互联网（[Snowball Edge overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)）。Snowball Edge storage-optimized 设备提供较大的本地容量——每台设备可用容量为 210 TB——因此多台设备可以处理 PB 级迁移（[Snowball Edge device configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/device-differences.html)）。AWS 文档还指出了适用于 Storage Gateway **Tape Gateway** 类型的 Snowball Edge 配置（[TGWOnDeviceServiceConfiguration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/api-reference/API_TGWOnDeviceServiceConfiguration.html)）。摄取到 S3 后，S3 Lifecycle 可以将对象转换到 **S3 Glacier Deep Archive** 用于长期归档，并且 AWS 明确支持到 S3 Glacier Deep Archive 的 Lifecycle 转换（[S3 Lifecycle transitions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)）。为什么其他选项不是最佳选择：

- **A**：通过 1 Gbps 互联网链路使用 DataSync 传输 5 PB 数据不太可能满足 6 个月的迁移要求，并且它的目标是 **S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval**，与 Deep Archive 相比，这并不是用于 10 年保留的最低成本归档存储类。
- **B**：通过 1 Gbps uplink 直接写入 S3 Glacier Deep Archive，仍然依赖受限的互联网连接来完成全部 5 PB 传输。
- **D**：本地 Tape Gateway 适合持续的磁带式备份，但 Tape Gateway 会将虚拟磁带数据异步上传到 AWS；它仍然依赖 1 Gbps uplink 来传输完整数据集。Tape Gateway 本身是一种经济高效、由云支持的虚拟磁带解决方案，并且可以归档到 S3 Glacier Deep Archive，但网络瓶颈使其不适合在 6 个月内完成这次一次性的 5 PB 迁移（[Tape Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/WhatIsStorageGateway.html), [How Tape Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/tgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html)）。

*注意：当前 AWS 文档指出，Snowball Edge 以及 Snow Family 设备上的 Tape Gateway 不再向新客户提供；但是，在此 SAA-C03 风格问题所给出的选项框架下，选项 C 是 AWS 文档支持的架构，可绕过互联网瓶颈，并将长期归档数据落地到 Deep Archive。*

en.question: A company is deploying an application that processes large quantities of data in parallel. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to prevent groups of nodes from sharing the same underlying hardware. Which networking solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Run the EC2 instances in a spread placement group.
options.B: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
options.C: Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy.
options.D: Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Run the EC2 instances in a spread placement group.**

A spread placement group is specifically designed to place instances on distinct underlying hardware: AWS states that “a spread placement group is a group of instances that are each placed on distinct hardware,” and that it reduces simultaneous failures that can occur when instances share the same equipment ([AWS EC2 placement strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)). This matches the requirement to configure the architecture so groups of nodes do not share the same underlying hardware.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts** — Separate accounts do not guarantee hardware separation. With default shared tenancy, AWS says multiple AWS accounts might share the same physical hardware ([AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)).
- **C. Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy** — Dedicated Instances isolate instances from instances that belong to *other* AWS accounts, but AWS notes they might share hardware with other instances from the same AWS account and provide no visibility or control over instance placement ([AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)). Therefore, this does not meet the requirement to prevent groups of the company’s nodes from sharing underlying hardware.
- **D. Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy** — Shared tenancy is the default, and AWS states that multiple AWS accounts might share the same physical hardware ([AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)), so it does not provide the required hardware separation.

zh.question: 一家公司正在部署一个并行处理大量数据的应用程序。该公司计划使用 Amazon EC2 实例来运行该工作负载。网络架构必须可配置，以防止节点组共享相同的底层硬件。哪种网络解决方案满足这些要求？

options.A: 在分散置放群组中运行 EC2 实例。
options.B: 将 EC2 实例分组到单独的账户中。
options.C: 为 EC2 实例配置专用租用。
options.D: 为 EC2 实例配置共享租用。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 在分散置放群组中运行 EC2 实例。**

分散置放群组专门用于将实例放置在不同的底层硬件上：AWS 表示，“分散置放群组是一组分别放置在不同硬件上的实例”，并且它可以减少实例共享相同设备时可能发生的同时故障（[AWS EC2 placement strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)）。这与配置架构以使节点组不共享相同底层硬件的要求相匹配。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. 将 EC2 实例分组到单独的账户中** — 单独的账户并不能保证硬件隔离。在默认共享租用下，AWS 表示多个 AWS 账户可能共享相同的物理硬件（[AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)）。
- **C. 为 EC2 实例配置专用租用** — Dedicated Instances 会将实例与属于*其他* AWS 账户的实例隔离开来，但 AWS 指出，它们可能会与来自同一 AWS 账户的其他实例共享硬件，并且不提供对实例放置的可见性或控制权（[AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)）。因此，这不满足防止公司节点组共享底层硬件的要求。
- **D. 为 EC2 实例配置共享租用** — 共享租用是默认设置，并且 AWS 表示多个 AWS 账户可能共享相同的物理硬件（[AWS EC2 Dedicated Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/dedicated-instance.html)），因此它无法提供所需的硬件隔离。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.
options.B: Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.
options.C: Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.
options.D: Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.

en.explanation:
The correct answer is **D. Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.**

AWS states that Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone, and explicitly lists **disaster recovery** as a common use case: use On-Demand Capacity Reservations to reserve capacity in a different Availability Zone or **Region** for DR. AWS also says to use On-Demand Capacity Reservations when workloads have strict capacity requirements and need capacity assurance, because they ensure access to the EC2 capacity that has been reserved ([AWS EC2 Capacity Reservations overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-reservation-overview.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A. On-Demand Instances**: On-Demand is a consumption/pricing model; purchasing or planning to launch On-Demand Instances does not reserve capacity in advance. It does not satisfy the requirement to meet capacity in the failover Region.
- **B. EC2 Savings Plan**: AWS describes Savings Plans as a way to save on compute costs by committing to a consistent USD/hour usage amount; it is a pricing discount model, not a capacity guarantee ([AWS cost optimization reservation models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/cost-optimization-reservation-models/regional-and-zonal-reserved-instances.html)).
- **C. Regional Reserved Instances**: AWS documentation says Reserved Instances are not physical instances but billing discounts applied to matching On-Demand Instance usage. More specifically, a **regional** Reserved Instance **does not reserve capacity**; only a zonal Reserved Instance reserves capacity in a specified Availability Zone ([Regional and zonal Reserved Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/reserved-instances-scope.html)). Therefore, the regional RI option does not meet the stated capacity requirement.

Therefore, the only option that directly provides EC2 capacity assurance for DR in the failover Region is **D**.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在设计一种灾难恢复 (DR) 策略，以便在故障转移 AWS Region 中提供 Amazon EC2 容量。业务需求规定，DR 策略必须在故障转移 Region 中满足容量要求。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在故障转移 Region 中购买 On-Demand Instances。
options.B: 在故障转移 Region 中购买 EC2 Savings Plan。
options.C: 在故障转移 Region 中购买 regional Reserved Instances。
options.D: 在故障转移 Region 中购买 Capacity Reservation。

zh.explanation:
正确答案是 **D. Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.**

AWS 说明，Capacity Reservations 会在特定 Availability Zone 中预留 EC2 计算容量，并明确将 **disaster recovery** 列为常见用例：使用 On-Demand Capacity Reservations 在不同 Availability Zone 或 **Region** 中为 DR 预留容量。AWS 还表示，当工作负载具有严格的容量要求并需要容量保证时，应使用 On-Demand Capacity Reservations，因为它们可确保访问已预留的 EC2 容量（[AWS EC2 Capacity Reservations overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-reservation-overview.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A. On-Demand Instances**：On-Demand 是一种消费/定价模型；购买或计划启动 On-Demand Instances 不会提前预留容量。它不满足在故障转移 Region 中满足容量的要求。
- **B. EC2 Savings Plan**：AWS 将 Savings Plans 描述为一种通过承诺一致的 USD/hour 使用量来节省计算成本的方式；它是一种定价折扣模型，而不是容量保证（[AWS cost optimization reservation models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/cost-optimization-reservation-models/regional-and-zonal-reserved-instances.html)）。
- **C. Regional Reserved Instances**：AWS 文档说明，Reserved Instances 不是物理实例，而是应用于匹配 On-Demand Instance 使用量的账单折扣。更具体地说，**regional** Reserved Instance **does not reserve capacity**；只有 zonal Reserved Instance 会在指定 Availability Zone 中预留容量（[Regional and zonal Reserved Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/reserved-instances-scope.html)）。因此，regional RI 选项不满足所述容量要求。因此，唯一能为故障转移 Region 中的 DR 直接提供 EC2 容量保证的选项是 **D**。

en.question: A company has five organizational units (OUs) as part of its organization in AWS Organizations. Each OU correlates to the five businesses that the company owns. The company's research and development (R&D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose. What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?

options.A: Have the R&D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.
options.B: Invite the R&D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&D AWS account has left the prior organization.
options.C: Create a new R&D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&D AWS account to the new R&D AWS account.
options.D: Have the R&D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.**

AWS Organizations supports migrating an existing AWS account from one organization to another. The documented migration process is for the **new organization’s management account to send an invitation to the migrating account**, and for the migrating account to accept it; AWS also lists the needed permissions to **leave** the old organization and to **invite** the account to the new organization in the migration prerequisites ([Migrate an account to another organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html)). AWS Organizations also states that **an account can only join one organization** ([Managing account invitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_invites.html)). Therefore, the R&D account must first leave the prior organization, then be invited to join the new organization.

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A** is incorrect because an AWS account cannot be a member of two organizations at the same time; AWS says an account can only join one organization ([Managing account invitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_invites.html)).
- **C** is incorrect because creating a new account and migrating resources is unnecessary. AWS provides a direct account migration process: send an invitation from the new organization and accept it from the migrating account ([Migrate an account to another organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html)).
- **D** is incorrect because it implies joining the new organization without first leaving the prior one, which conflicts with the one-organization limit. Also, making the new management account a member of the prior organization would not create an independent organization for the separating R&D business.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Organizations 中的组织包含五个组织部门（OU）。每个 OU 对应公司拥有的五个业务之一。该公司的研究与开发（R&D）业务正在从公司拆分出来，并且需要自己的组织。一名解决方案架构师为此创建了一个单独的新管理账户。接下来，解决方案架构师应在新的管理账户中做什么？

options.A: 让 R&D AWS 账户在过渡期间同时属于两个组织。
options.B: 在 R&D AWS 账户离开之前的组织后，邀请该 R&D AWS 账户加入新组织。
options.C: 在新组织中创建一个新的 R&D AWS 账户。将资源从之前的 R&D AWS 账户迁移到新的 R&D AWS 账户。
options.D: 让 R&D AWS 账户加入新组织。将新的管理账户设为之前组织的成员。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。**

AWS Organizations 支持将现有 AWS 账户从一个组织迁移到另一个组织。文档化的迁移流程是由**新组织的管理账户向要迁移的账户发送邀请**，并由要迁移的账户接受该邀请；AWS 还在迁移先决条件中列出了**离开**旧组织以及**邀请**该账户加入新组织所需的权限（[Migrate an account to another organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html)）。AWS Organizations 还说明，**一个账户只能加入一个组织**（[Managing account invitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_invites.html)）。因此，R&D 账户必须先离开之前的组织，然后再被邀请加入新组织。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A** 不正确，因为一个 AWS 账户不能同时成为两个组织的成员；AWS 说明一个账户只能加入一个组织（[Managing account invitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_invites.html)）。
- **C** 不正确，因为创建新账户并迁移资源是不必要的。AWS 提供了直接的账户迁移流程：由新组织发送邀请，并由要迁移的账户接受该邀请（[Migrate an account to another organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html)）。
- **D** 不正确，因为它暗示在未先离开之前组织的情况下加入新组织，这与单组织限制相冲突。此外，将新的管理账户设为之前组织的成员，并不能为正在拆分的 R&D 业务创建一个独立组织。

en.question: A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity in different web applications to process analytics and make predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can increase suddenly. The company requires a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must include an authorization step for security purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.
options.B: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.
options.C: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.
options.D: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.**

API Gateway is appropriate as the integration front end for web applications because AWS describes it as a service for creating, publishing, maintaining, monitoring, and securing REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs “at any scale,” including APIs that access AWS services and other web services ([API Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html)). Amazon Data Firehose is a fully managed service for delivering real-time streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3, and AWS states that producers send data to Firehose and it automatically delivers the data to the configured destination ([Amazon Data Firehose overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html)). For an S3 destination, Firehose delivers streaming data to the S3 bucket, and the S3 destination settings explicitly require choosing the S3 bucket where streaming data should be delivered ([Firehose S3 destination settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html)). Finally, API Gateway Lambda authorizers are designed for this authorization step: API Gateway invokes the Lambda authorizer “to determine if a caller can invoke your method” ([Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** Gateway Load Balancer is for deploying, scaling, and managing virtual appliances such as firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention systems, and deep packet inspection systems, not for exposing web APIs or performing application authorization ([Gateway Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)). Also, storing event streams on EFS behind ECS is not the managed streaming-ingestion-to-S3 analytics pattern.
- **B:** API Gateway can integrate with Kinesis and invoke Kinesis actions such as `PutRecord`/`PutRecords` ([API Gateway Kinesis proxy tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/integrating-api-with-aws-services-kinesis.html)), but a Kinesis data stream is not the component that automatically delivers records to S3. Firehose is the managed service that automatically delivers streaming data to S3 ([Amazon Data Firehose overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html)).
- **D:** This has the same GWLB/ECS/EFS mismatch as option A. A separate generic Lambda function is not the right front-door authorization mechanism; API Gateway Lambda authorizers are the documented feature for deciding whether a caller may invoke an API method ([Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司正在设计一个解决方案，用于捕获不同 Web 应用程序中的客户活动，以处理分析并进行预测。Web 应用程序中的客户活动不可预测，并且可能突然增加。公司需要一个能够与其他 Web 应用程序集成的解决方案。出于安全目的，该解决方案必须包含一个授权步骤。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 容器实例前配置 Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)，该容器实例将公司接收到的信息存储在 Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) 文件系统中。授权在 GWLB 处解析。
options.B: 在 Amazon Kinesis data stream 前配置 Amazon API Gateway 端点，该数据流将公司接收到的信息存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。使用 AWS Lambda 函数来解析授权。
options.C: 在 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 前配置 Amazon API Gateway 端点，该服务将公司接收到的信息存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。使用 API Gateway Lambda authorizer 来解析授权。
options.D: 在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 容器实例前配置 Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)，该容器实例将公司接收到的信息存储在 Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) 文件系统上。使用 AWS Lambda 函数来解析授权。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C。**

API Gateway 适合作为 Web 应用程序的集成前端，因为 AWS 将其描述为一项用于“以任意规模”创建、发布、维护、监控和保护 REST、HTTP 和 WebSocket API 的服务，包括访问 AWS 服务和其他 Web 服务的 API（[API Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html)）。Amazon Data Firehose 是一项完全托管的服务，用于将实时流式数据传输到 Amazon S3 等目标，AWS 表示生产者将数据发送到 Firehose，Firehose 会自动将数据传输到配置的目标（[Amazon Data Firehose overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html)）。对于 S3 目标，Firehose 会将流式数据传输到 S3 存储桶，并且 S3 目标设置明确要求选择应将流式数据传输到的 S3 存储桶（[Firehose S3 destination settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html)）。最后，API Gateway Lambda authorizers 正是为此授权步骤而设计的：API Gateway 调用 Lambda authorizer “以确定调用方是否可以调用你的方法”（[Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A:** Gateway Load Balancer 用于部署、扩展和管理防火墙、入侵检测/防御系统以及深度数据包检查系统等虚拟设备，而不是用于公开 Web API 或执行应用程序授权（[Gateway Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)）。此外，将事件流存储在 ECS 后面的 EFS 上并不是托管的流式摄取到 S3 的分析模式。
- **B:** API Gateway 可以与 Kinesis 集成，并调用 `PutRecord`/`PutRecords` 等 Kinesis 操作（[API Gateway Kinesis proxy tutorial](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/integrating-api-with-aws-services-kinesis.html)），但 Kinesis data stream 并不是会自动将记录传输到 S3 的组件。Firehose 才是自动将流式数据传输到 S3 的托管服务（[Amazon Data Firehose overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html)）。
- **D:** 这与选项 A 存在相同的 GWLB/ECS/EFS 不匹配问题。单独的通用 Lambda 函数并不是正确的入口授权机制；API Gateway Lambda authorizers 才是用于决定调用方是否可以调用 API 方法的文档化功能（[Configure an API Gateway Lambda authorizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/configure-api-gateway-lambda-authorization.html)）。

en.question: An ecommerce company wants a disaster recovery solution for its Amazon RDS DB instances that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition. The company's current recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create a cross-Region read replica and promote the read replica to the primary instance.
options.B: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create RDS cross-Region replication.
options.C: Use cross-Region replication every 24 hours to copy native backups to an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.D: Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **D. Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.**

A 24-hour RPO/RTO does not require a continuously running standby database or continuous replication. Amazon RDS supports copying a DB snapshot to another AWS Region; the copy becomes a manual DB snapshot in that Region, and automated backups can be copied to manual snapshots. AWS also notes that after the first cross-Region copy, subsequent copies of the same DB instance can be incremental, which is faster and has lower storage impact than repeatedly copying full data sets. This meets a 24-hour RPO by scheduling the copy every 24 hours, and avoids paying for a constantly running replica instance. AWS documentation also states that RDS supports DB snapshots, point-in-time restores, and automated or manual backups for RDS for SQL Server, and that RDS manages backups for you ([RDS for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html), [copying DB snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html)).

Why the other options are wrong:

- **A**: A cross-Region read replica can be used for DR, but read replicas are billed as standard DB instances, so this is more expensive than keeping only copied snapshots for a 24-hour RPO/RTO. AWS specifically says read replicas are billed as standard DB instances ([RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)).
- **B**: AWS DMS replication would provide ongoing replication infrastructure, which is unnecessary for a 24-hour RPO/RTO and is not the most cost-effective RDS-native backup approach.
- **C**: Native SQL Server backup and restore to S3 is supported and can add protection for DR, but it is a database-level native backup workflow rather than the simplest RDS-managed instance-level DR mechanism. Snapshot copy is the RDS-native solution and can use incremental cross-Region copies ([native backup and restore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.Procedural.Importing.html), [copying DB snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html)).

zh.question: 一家电子商务公司希望为其运行 Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition 的 Amazon RDS DB 实例提供灾难恢复解决方案。该公司当前的恢复点目标 (RPO) 和恢复时间目标 (RTO) 均为 24 小时。哪种解决方案将以最高成本效益满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建跨区域只读副本，并将该只读副本提升为主实例。
options.B: 使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 创建 RDS 跨区域复制。
options.C: 每 24 小时使用跨区域复制将原生备份复制到 Amazon S3 存储桶。
options.D: 每 24 小时将自动快照复制到另一个区域。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **D. 每 24 小时将自动快照复制到另一个区域。**

24 小时的 RPO/RTO 不需要持续运行的备用数据库或持续复制。Amazon RDS 支持将 DB 快照复制到另一个 AWS Region；该副本会成为该区域中的手动 DB 快照，并且自动备份可以复制为手动快照。AWS 还指出，在第一次跨区域复制之后，同一 DB 实例的后续副本可以是增量的，这比反复复制完整数据集更快，并且对存储的影响更低。通过每 24 小时计划一次复制，这满足了 24 小时 RPO，并避免为持续运行的副本实例付费。AWS 文档还说明，RDS for SQL Server 支持 DB 快照、时间点还原以及自动或手动备份，并且 RDS 会为你管理备份（[RDS for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_SQLServer.html), [copying DB snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html)）。其他选项错误的原因：

- **A**：跨区域只读副本可用于 DR，但只读副本按标准 DB 实例计费，因此对于 24 小时 RPO/RTO 来说，这比仅保留已复制的快照更昂贵。AWS 明确说明只读副本按标准 DB 实例计费（[RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。
- **B**：AWS DMS 复制会提供持续的复制基础设施，这对于 24 小时 RPO/RTO 来说并不必要，也不是最具成本效益的 RDS 原生备份方法。
- **C**：支持将原生 SQL Server 备份和还原到 S3，并且可以为 DR 增加保护，但它是数据库级别的原生备份工作流，而不是最简单的由 RDS 管理的实例级 DR 机制。快照复制是 RDS 原生解决方案，并且可以使用增量跨区域副本（[native backup and restore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.Procedural.Importing.html), [copying DB snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html)）。

en.question: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that has sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently hosts the user session state. The company wants to ensure high availability and avoid user session state loss in the event of a web server outage. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.
options.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.
options.C: Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.
options.D: Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.**

The problem is that session state is stored on individual web servers. AWS guidance notes that sticky sessions preserve state only while the same EC2 instance is available; if the instance fails, the sticky session is broken and the user’s session state is lost. AWS recommends using a **shared backing store** so session state is decoupled from individual EC2 instances and persists independently if an instance fails or during scaling events. The same guidance specifically describes configuring **ElastiCache (Redis OSS)** as a shared backing store for session storage and states that this provides high availability, scalability, and fault tolerance ([AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-asp-net-web-forms/ha-scaling.html)).

ElastiCache for Redis also has the availability features needed for this use case: AWS documents that Redis OSS replication groups can include replicas so that if a node fails, data is replicated in other nodes, and with Multi-AZ enabled, the primary fails over to a read replica ([High availability using replication groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)). AWS also states that Multi-AZ for Valkey/Redis OSS improves fault tolerance and automatically fails over the primary to a replica, minimizing downtime ([Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. ElastiCache for Memcached** — Memcached is an in-memory cache, but AWS’s engine comparison shows **Memcached has no high availability replication and no automatic failover**, while Redis OSS supports both ([ElastiCache engine comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/SelectEngine.html)). Therefore it does not best meet the high availability/session-loss requirement.
- **C. AWS Storage Gateway cached volume** — Storage Gateway cached volumes are not the appropriate service for low-latency, per-user web session state. AWS guidance for this session-state problem recommends a shared backing store such as DynamoDB, RDS, or **ElastiCache Redis**, and provides Redis session-store configuration—not Storage Gateway ([AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-asp-net-web-forms/ha-scaling.html)).
- **D. Amazon RDS** — RDS can be a shared backing store in some application designs, but this option does not specify Multi-AZ or failover configuration, and a relational database is not the best fit for high-speed ephemeral session state. ElastiCache Redis is the purpose-built in-memory key-value option with documented replication and Multi-AZ failover for this requirement ([Replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html), [Multi-AZ failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司在 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行 Web 应用程序，并且该负载均衡器启用了粘性会话。当前，Web 服务器托管用户会话状态。该公司希望确保高可用性，并在 Web 服务器中断时避免用户会话状态丢失。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached 实例来存储会话数据。更新应用程序以使用 ElastiCache for Memcached 存储会话状态。
options.B: 使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis 来存储会话状态。更新应用程序以使用 ElastiCache for Redis 存储会话状态。
options.C: 使用 AWS Storage Gateway 缓存卷来存储会话数据。更新应用程序以使用 AWS Storage Gateway 缓存卷存储会话状态。
options.D: 使用 Amazon RDS 来存储会话状态。更新应用程序以使用 Amazon RDS 存储会话状态。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.**

问题在于会话状态存储在各个 Web 服务器上。AWS 指南指出，粘性会话只有在同一个 EC2 实例可用时才能保留状态；如果该实例发生故障，粘性会话会中断，用户的会话状态会丢失。AWS 建议使用一个 **shared backing store**，以便将会话状态与各个 EC2 实例解耦，并在实例故障或扩缩容事件期间独立持久保留。同一指南还专门描述了将 **ElastiCache (Redis OSS)** 配置为用于会话存储的共享后端存储，并说明这可提供高可用性、可扩展性和容错能力（[AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-asp-net-web-forms/ha-scaling.html)）。

ElastiCache for Redis 还具备此用例所需的可用性功能：AWS 文档说明，Redis OSS replication groups 可以包含副本，因此如果某个节点发生故障，数据会复制到其他节点；并且在启用 Multi-AZ 后，主节点会故障转移到只读副本（[High availability using replication groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)）。AWS 还说明，Valkey/Redis OSS 的 Multi-AZ 可提高容错能力，并自动将主节点故障转移到副本，从而最大限度地减少停机时间（[Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. ElastiCache for Memcached** — Memcached 是内存缓存，但 AWS 的引擎比较显示 **Memcached 没有高可用性复制，也没有自动故障转移**，而 Redis OSS 同时支持这两者（[ElastiCache engine comparison](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/SelectEngine.html)）。因此，它并不能最好地满足高可用性/会话丢失方面的要求。
- **C. AWS Storage Gateway cached volume** — Storage Gateway cached volumes 并不是用于低延迟、按用户划分的 Web 会话状态的合适服务。AWS 针对此会话状态问题的指南建议使用共享后端存储，例如 DynamoDB、RDS 或 **ElastiCache Redis**，并提供 Redis 会话存储配置，而不是 Storage Gateway（[AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-asp-net-web-forms/ha-scaling.html)）。
- **D. Amazon RDS** — RDS 在某些应用程序设计中可以作为共享后端存储，但此选项未指定 Multi-AZ 或故障转移配置，并且关系数据库并不是高速临时会话状态的最佳选择。ElastiCache Redis 是专为此要求而构建的内存键值选项，并有文档记录其复制和 Multi-AZ 故障转移能力（[Replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html), [Multi-AZ failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)）。

en.question: A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to meet the company's average daily workload. Once a month, the database performs slowly when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants to have the ability to run reports and maintain the performance of the daily workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.
options.B: Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance. Direct the queries to the new database.
options.C: Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.
options.D: Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** Amazon RDS read replicas are intended for scaling read-heavy workloads: AWS says you can direct excess read traffic to read replicas, and specifically lists **business reporting** queries as a use case where reports run against a read replica instead of the production DB instance. A read replica is created from the source DB instance and then updated asynchronously, and applications can connect to it like any other DB instance, so monthly report queries can be directed there without overloading the primary workload database ([Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**
- **B:** Restoring a backup/snapshot to another DB instance creates another DB instance, but it is a point-in-time copy and is operationally heavier for a recurring monthly reporting need. A read replica is the native RDS feature for keeping a separate read-only instance updated from the primary ([Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)).
- **C:** Athena can query data in Amazon S3, but the question is about offloading report queries from an RDS for MySQL database while maintaining daily workload performance. Exporting to S3 and querying with Athena adds an ETL/export workflow and is not the most direct RDS solution ([Create tables in Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/creating-tables.html)).
- **D:** Resizing the primary DB instance might handle the monthly spike, but the report queries would still compete with the daily workload on the same production instance. AWS explicitly recommends directing excess read traffic and business reporting queries to read replicas instead ([Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司将一个 MySQL 数据库从公司的本地数据中心迁移到 Amazon RDS for MySQL DB 实例。该公司根据公司的日均工作负载来确定 RDS DB 实例的规格。每月一次，当公司运行报表查询时，数据库性能会变慢。公司希望能够运行报表并保持日常工作负载的性能。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建该数据库的只读副本。将查询定向到该只读副本。
options.B: 创建该数据库的备份。将该备份还原到另一个 DB 实例。将查询定向到新数据库。
options.C: 将数据导出到 Amazon S3。使用 Amazon Athena 查询 S3 存储桶。
options.D: 调整 DB 实例大小以容纳额外的工作负载。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A。** Amazon RDS 只读副本旨在扩展读取密集型工作负载：AWS 表示你可以将多余的读取流量定向到只读副本，并特别将 **business reporting** 查询列为一个用例，即报表在只读副本上运行，而不是在生产 DB 实例上运行。只读副本从源 DB 实例创建，然后异步更新，并且应用程序可以像连接任何其他 DB 实例一样连接到它，因此每月报表查询可以被定向到那里，而不会使主工作负载数据库过载（[Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**
- **B:** 将备份/快照还原到另一个 DB 实例会创建另一个 DB 实例，但它是一个时间点副本，并且对于每月定期报表需求来说运维负担更重。只读副本是 RDS 原生功能，用于保持一个单独的只读实例从主实例更新（[Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。
- **C:** Athena 可以查询 Amazon S3 中的数据，但本题关注的是在保持日常工作负载性能的同时，将报表查询从 RDS for MySQL 数据库卸载出去。导出到 S3 并使用 Athena 查询会增加 ETL/导出工作流，并不是最直接的 RDS 解决方案（[Create tables in Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/creating-tables.html)）。
- **D:** 调整主 DB 实例大小可能可以处理每月峰值，但报表查询仍会在同一个生产实例上与日常工作负载竞争。AWS 明确建议将多余的读取流量和业务报表查询定向到只读副本（[Amazon RDS read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。

en.question: A company runs a container application by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application includes microservices that manage customers and place orders. The company needs to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservices. Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision a Network Load Balancer.
options.B: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.
options.C: Use an AWS Lambda function to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
options.D: Use Amazon API Gateway to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.**

Amazon EKS documentation states that when you create a Kubernetes `Ingress`, the AWS Load Balancer Controller provisions an **Application Load Balancer (ALB)**, and that ALB load balances **application traffic**. The same page notes that application traffic is balanced at **Layer 7** ([Route application and HTTP traffic with Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/alb-ingress.html)). EKS best practices also state that an ALB, controlled by an Ingress resource, **routes HTTP or HTTPS traffic to different Pods within the cluster** ([Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)). This is the native, cost-effective way to route incoming HTTP/HTTPS requests to customer and order microservices in EKS.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Network Load Balancer**: An NLB is provisioned for a Kubernetes Service of type `LoadBalancer` and operates at **Layer 4**. AWS guidance says to choose an NLB for TCP/UDP workloads or source IP preservation, not for Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS request routing between microservices ([Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)).
- **C. Lambda function**: Lambda is not the native EKS traffic-routing mechanism. The AWS Load Balancer Controller is specifically documented to expose EKS cluster applications by provisioning AWS load balancers that point to Kubernetes Service or Ingress resources ([Route internet traffic with AWS Load Balancer Controller](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/aws-load-balancer-controller.html)). Adding Lambda would add an unnecessary component.
- **D. API Gateway**: API Gateway can be useful for API management, but the requirement is simply to route requests to EKS microservices. EKS documentation recommends the AWS Load Balancer Controller for reconciling Kubernetes Service and Ingress resources, and ALB Ingress provides the needed Layer 7 routing directly in the cluster ([Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)). API Gateway would add another managed service and is not the most cost-effective solution for this stated requirement.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 运行一个容器应用程序。该应用程序包含用于管理客户和下订单的微服务。公司需要将传入请求路由到相应的微服务。哪种解决方案能以最低成本满足此要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS Load Balancer Controller 预置 Network Load Balancer。
options.B: 使用 AWS Load Balancer Controller 预置 Application Load Balancer。
options.C: 使用 AWS Lambda 函数将请求连接到 Amazon EKS。
options.D: 使用 Amazon API Gateway 将请求连接到 Amazon EKS。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B. 使用 AWS Load Balancer Controller 预置 Application Load Balancer。**

Amazon EKS 文档指出，当你创建 Kubernetes `Ingress` 时，AWS Load Balancer Controller 会预置一个 **Application Load Balancer (ALB)**，并且该 ALB 对**应用程序流量**进行负载均衡。同一页面还指出，应用程序流量在 **Layer 7** 进行均衡（[Route application and HTTP traffic with Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/alb-ingress.html)）。EKS 最佳实践还指出，由 Ingress 资源控制的 ALB 会**将 HTTP 或 HTTPS 流量路由到集群内的不同 Pods**（[Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)）。这是在 EKS 中将传入 HTTP/HTTPS 请求路由到客户和订单微服务的原生且具有成本效益的方式。

**其他选项错误的原因：**

- **A. Network Load Balancer**：NLB 是为类型为 `LoadBalancer` 的 Kubernetes Service 预置的，并在 **Layer 4** 运行。AWS 指南指出，应为 TCP/UDP 工作负载或保留源 IP 选择 NLB，而不是用于微服务之间的 Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS 请求路由（[Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)）。
- **C. Lambda function**：Lambda 不是原生的 EKS 流量路由机制。AWS Load Balancer Controller 被明确记录为通过预置指向 Kubernetes Service 或 Ingress 资源的 AWS 负载均衡器来暴露 EKS 集群应用程序（[Route internet traffic with AWS Load Balancer Controller](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/aws-load-balancer-controller.html)）。添加 Lambda 会增加不必要的组件。
- **D. API Gateway**：API Gateway 可用于 API 管理，但此要求只是将请求路由到 EKS 微服务。EKS 文档建议使用 AWS Load Balancer Controller 来协调 Kubernetes Service 和 Ingress 资源，而 ALB Ingress 可直接在集群中提供所需的 Layer 7 路由（[Load Balancing - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/load-balancing.html)）。API Gateway 会增加另一项托管服务，并且对于此处所述要求而言不是最具成本效益的解决方案。

en.question: A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company’s global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly. The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
options.B: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.
options.C: Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
options.D: Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D.**

Amazon S3 is an appropriate low-cost origin for storing image objects, and CloudFront can use an S3 bucket as an origin with origin access control so that CloudFront is the controlled access path to the bucket ([Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)). CloudFront geographic restrictions directly meet the country-blocking requirement: AWS documentation states that you can prevent users from accessing content if they are in banned countries on a denylist ([Restrict the geographic distribution of your content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/georestrictions.html)). For paid/copyrighted content, CloudFront signed URLs are also appropriate because the application can verify that a user is entitled to access the content, create a signed URL, and the signed URL lets the user download or stream the content from the CloudFront edge cache ([Use signed URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** Making an S3 bucket public and giving users a bucket link does not restrict access by country and does not provide per-customer paid access control. MFA on an AWS account is not a content-distribution authorization mechanism for customers.
- **B:** Creating an IAM user for each customer is operationally inefficient and not intended for broad customer access to web content. It also does not provide global edge caching or geographic restrictions.
- **C:** EC2 instances behind ALBs would be more expensive and operationally complex than S3 plus CloudFront. Deploying instances only in serviced countries does not reliably deny users from other countries, and it lacks CloudFront’s built-in geographic restriction capability.

Therefore, **D** is the solution that satisfies fast global access, country-based denial, paid-content access control, and cost minimization.

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS 并销售受版权保护图像的访问权限。该公司的全球客户群需要能够快速访问这些图像。公司必须拒绝来自特定国家/地区的用户访问。公司希望尽可能降低成本。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon S3 存储图像。开启多重身份验证 (MFA) 和公有存储桶访问。向客户提供指向 S3 存储桶的链接。
options.B: 使用 Amazon S3 存储图像。为每个客户创建一个 IAM 用户。将这些用户添加到一个具有访问 S3 存储桶权限的组中。
options.C: 使用位于 Application Load Balancers (ALBs) 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例来存储图像。仅在公司提供服务的国家/地区部署实例。向客户提供指向其特定国家/地区实例的 ALBs 的链接。
options.D: 使用 Amazon S3 存储图像。使用 Amazon CloudFront 通过地理限制分发图像。为每个客户提供一个签名 URL，以访问 CloudFront 中的数据。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D.**

Amazon S3 是用于存储图像对象的合适低成本源站，CloudFront 可以将 S3 存储桶用作源站，并结合源访问控制，使 CloudFront 成为通向该存储桶的受控访问路径（[Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html)）。CloudFront 地理限制直接满足按国家/地区阻止访问的要求：AWS 文档指出，如果用户位于拒绝列表中的被禁止国家/地区，你可以阻止他们访问内容（[Restrict the geographic distribution of your content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/georestrictions.html)）。对于付费/受版权保护的内容，CloudFront 签名 URLs 也很合适，因为应用程序可以验证用户是否有权访问该内容，创建签名 URL，而签名 URL 允许用户从 CloudFront 边缘缓存下载或流式传输内容（[Use signed URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-signed-urls.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A:** 将 S3 存储桶设为公有并向用户提供存储桶链接，无法按国家/地区限制访问，也无法提供按客户的付费访问控制。AWS 账户上的 MFA 不是面向客户的内容分发授权机制。
- **B:** 为每个客户创建 IAM 用户在运营上效率低下，并且并非用于向大量客户提供 Web 内容访问。它也不提供全球边缘缓存或地理限制。
- **C:** 与 S3 加 CloudFront 相比，位于 ALBs 后面的 EC2 实例成本更高且运营复杂度更高。仅在提供服务的国家/地区部署实例并不能可靠地拒绝来自其他国家/地区的用户访问，并且缺少 CloudFront 内置的地理限制功能。因此，**D** 是满足快速全球访问、基于国家/地区的拒绝、付费内容访问控制以及成本最小化的解决方案。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region. The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.
options.B: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.
options.C: Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.
options.D: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.**

A Redis OSS/Valkey shard in ElastiCache can contain one primary and 1–5 replica nodes; AWS states that a multiple-node shard implements replication with a read/write primary and replica nodes, and that read replicas improve fault tolerance by maintaining multiple copies of data. AWS also recommends placing replicas in different Availability Zones for greater reliability and faster recovery within the Region ([ElastiCache components and features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.Components.html)). With Multi-AZ enabled, if the primary node fails, ElastiCache promotes the replica with the least replication lag, typically allowing writes to resume in a few seconds ([Multi-AZ failure scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)). Therefore, Multi-AZ replication groups with multiple-node shards provide the required node-level and in-Region/AZ-level high availability.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B:** AOF is not the right HA design. AWS describes single-node clusters as having only limited data protection services such as AOF, and if the cluster fails, all cluster data is lost ([High availability using replication groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)). Also, ElastiCache for Redis OSS Multi-AZ and AOF are mutually exclusive, so AOF does not meet the Multi-AZ HA requirement ([Multi-AZ limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)).
- **C:** Having more than one read replica can improve fault tolerance, but this option is less complete than A because it does not specify that **each shard** contains multiple nodes. AWS notes that if any primary has no replicas and the primary fails, that primary’s data is lost ([ElastiCache replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.Components.html)).
- **D:** Auto Scaling addresses capacity/scalability, not automatic failover or data protection. The documented HA mechanism is replication plus Multi-AZ failover, where replicas are promoted after primary failure ([Multi-AZ failure scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)).

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在设计一个基于 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis 的高可用解决方案。解决方案架构师需要确保故障不会导致本地以及 AWS Region 内的性能下降或数据丢失。该解决方案需要在节点级别和 Region 级别提供高可用性。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Multi-AZ Redis 复制组，并使用包含多个节点的分片。
options.B: 使用包含多个节点的 Redis 分片，并开启 Redis append only files (AOF)。
options.C: 使用一个 Multi-AZ Redis 集群，并在复制组中配置多个读取副本。
options.D: 使用包含多个节点的 Redis 分片，并开启 Auto Scaling。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 使用 Multi-AZ Redis 复制组，并使用包含多个节点的分片。**

ElastiCache 中的 Redis OSS/Valkey shard 可以包含一个主节点和 1–5 个副本节点；AWS 说明，多节点 shard 通过读/写主节点和副本节点实现复制，并且读取副本通过维护多份数据副本来提高容错能力。AWS 还建议将副本放置在不同的 Availability Zones 中，以便在 Region 内实现更高的可靠性和更快的恢复（[ElastiCache components and features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.Components.html)）。启用 Multi-AZ 后，如果主节点发生故障，ElastiCache 会提升复制延迟最小的副本，通常可在几秒钟内恢复写入（[Multi-AZ failure scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)）。因此，带有多节点分片的 Multi-AZ 复制组可提供所需的节点级别以及 Region 内/AZ 级别的高可用性。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B:** AOF 不是合适的 HA 设计。AWS 将单节点集群描述为仅具有有限的数据保护服务，例如 AOF；如果集群发生故障，所有集群数据都会丢失（[High availability using replication groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Replication.html)）。此外，ElastiCache for Redis OSS Multi-AZ 与 AOF 互斥，因此 AOF 不满足 Multi-AZ HA 要求（[Multi-AZ limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)）。
- **C:** 拥有多个读取副本可以提高容错能力，但此选项不如 A 完整，因为它没有指定 **each shard** 包含多个节点。AWS 指出，如果任何主节点没有副本且该主节点发生故障，则该主节点的数据会丢失（[ElastiCache replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.Components.html)）。
- **D:** Auto Scaling 解决的是容量/可扩展性问题，而不是自动故障转移或数据保护。文档中说明的 HA 机制是复制加 Multi-AZ 故障转移，即在主节点故障后提升副本（[Multi-AZ failure scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)）。

en.question: A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive. Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?

options.A: Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
options.B: Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
options.C: Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
options.D: Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **C**.

Amazon EC2 hibernation directly addresses the described problem: AWS states that if an instance or application takes a long time to bootstrap and build a memory footprint, you can use hibernation to pre-warm it by launching it with hibernation enabled, bringing it to the desired state, and hibernating it so it can later resume from that state. When resumed, RAM contents are reloaded and previously running processes continue ([EC2 hibernation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Hibernate.html)). EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools also reduce latency for applications with long boot times by keeping pre-initialized instances that an Auto Scaling group can draw from during scale-out; warm pool instances can be kept in a `Hibernated` state so RAM is preserved and reloaded when started ([warm pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A**: Launching more On-Demand Instances and enabling Auto Scaling can add capacity, but it does not solve the slow bootstrap/memory-loading problem. The warm pools documentation specifically notes warm pools avoid needing to over-provision Auto Scaling groups to manage latency ([warm pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html)).
- **B**: Spot Instances provide spare EC2 capacity and can help with cost/scaling, but changing the purchase option to Spot does not reduce application initialization or memory warm-up time. The question also specifies using On-Demand Instances.
- **D**: Capacity Reservations reserve On-Demand compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone, but they do not pre-initialize the application or preserve RAM state; therefore they address capacity availability, not launch-time latency ([EC2 Capacity Reservations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司计划迁移到 AWS，并为其应用程序使用 Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances。在迁移测试阶段，技术团队观察到该应用程序需要很长时间才能启动并加载内存，从而达到完全可用状态。哪种解决方案将在下一次测试阶段减少该应用程序的启动时间？

options.A: 启动两个或更多 EC2 On-Demand Instances。开启自动扩缩功能，并使这些 EC2 On-Demand Instances 在下一次测试阶段可用。
options.B: 启动 EC2 Spot Instances 以支持该应用程序，并扩展该应用程序，使其在下一次测试阶段可用。
options.C: 在开启休眠的情况下启动 EC2 On-Demand Instances。在下一次测试阶段配置 EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools。
options.D: 使用 Capacity Reservations 启动 EC2 On-Demand Instances。在下一次测试阶段启动额外的 EC2 实例。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **C**。

Amazon EC2 hibernation 直接解决了题目中描述的问题：AWS 表示，如果某个实例或应用程序需要很长时间来引导并构建内存占用，你可以使用 hibernation 对其进行预热，方法是在启用 hibernation 的情况下启动它，将其置于所需状态，然后将其休眠，以便之后可以从该状态恢复。恢复时，RAM 内容会被重新加载，之前运行的进程会继续运行（[EC2 hibernation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Hibernate.html)）。EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools 也通过保留预初始化的实例来降低启动时间较长应用程序的延迟，Auto Scaling 组可以在横向扩展时从中取用这些实例；warm pool 实例可以保持在 `Hibernated` 状态，以便保留 RAM，并在启动时重新加载（[warm pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html)）。为什么其他选项不正确：

- **A**：启动更多 On-Demand Instances 并启用 Auto Scaling 可以增加容量，但不能解决缓慢的引导/内存加载问题。warm pools 文档特别指出，warm pools 可避免为了管理延迟而需要过度预置 Auto Scaling 组（[warm pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html)）。
- **B**：Spot Instances 提供备用 EC2 容量，并可帮助降低成本/实现扩展，但将购买选项更改为 Spot 并不能减少应用程序初始化或内存预热时间。题目也明确指定使用 On-Demand Instances。
- **D**：Capacity Reservations 会在特定 Availability Zone 中预留 On-Demand 计算容量，但它们不会预初始化应用程序或保留 RAM 状态；因此它们解决的是容量可用性，而不是启动时间延迟（[EC2 Capacity Reservations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html)）。

en.question: A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden traffic increases on random days of the week. The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden traffic increases. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
options.B: Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
options.D: Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C. Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.**

Dynamic scaling is the best fit because the traffic increases are **sudden** and occur on **random days**, so the company does not know in advance when capacity will be needed. AWS states that dynamic scaling resizes an Auto Scaling group to meet changes in demand and is useful “when you don't know when the traffic will change” ([Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)). This maintains performance while remaining cost-effective because instances are added in response to demand rather than being kept running unnecessarily.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Manual scaling** is not appropriate because it requires someone to manually update desired capacity; it will not automatically respond to sudden, random spikes ([Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)).
- **B. Predictive scaling** is intended for traffic with historical daily or weekly patterns, cyclical traffic, or recurring workload patterns. The scenario says traffic increases happen on random days, so there is no predictable pattern to forecast ([Predictive scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-scaling.html)).
- **D. Scheduled scaling** is useful when you know exactly when to increase or decrease capacity because demand follows a predictable schedule. Random traffic increases do not meet that condition ([Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司的应用程序在 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行。该公司注意到，其应用程序在一周中的随机日期会遇到突发流量增加。该公司希望在突发流量增加期间保持应用程序性能。哪种解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用手动扩缩来更改 Auto Scaling 组的大小。
options.B: 使用预测性扩缩来更改 Auto Scaling 组的大小。
options.C: 使用动态扩缩来更改 Auto Scaling 组的大小。
options.D: 使用计划扩缩来更改 Auto Scaling 组的大小。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C. 使用动态扩缩来更改 Auto Scaling 组的大小。**

动态扩缩最适合此场景，因为流量增加是**突发的**，并且发生在**随机日期**，因此公司无法提前知道何时需要容量。AWS 表示，动态扩缩会调整 Auto Scaling 组的大小以满足需求变化，并且在“你不知道流量何时会变化”时非常有用（[Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)）。这可以在保持性能的同时保持成本效益，因为实例是响应需求而添加的，而不是不必要地一直运行。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. Manual scaling** 不合适，因为它需要有人手动更新所需容量；它不会自动响应突发的随机流量峰值（[Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)）。
- **B. Predictive scaling** 适用于具有历史每日或每周模式的流量、周期性流量或重复出现的工作负载模式。该场景说明流量增加发生在随机日期，因此没有可预测的模式可用于预测（[Predictive scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-predictive-scaling.html)）。
- **D. Scheduled scaling** 在你确切知道何时增加或减少容量时很有用，因为需求遵循可预测的计划。随机流量增加不满足这一条件（[Choose your scaling method](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/scaling-overview.html)）。

en.question: An ecommerce application uses a PostgreSQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. During a monthly sales event, database usage increases and causes database connection issues for the application. The traffic is unpredictable for subsequent monthly sales events, which impacts the sales forecast. The company needs to maintain performance when there is an unpredictable increase in traffic. Which solution resolves this issue in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.A: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.
options.B: Enable auto scaling for the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to accommodate increased usage.
options.C: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a larger instance type.
options.D: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Redshift to accommodate increased usage.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.**

Aurora Serverless is designed for **highly variable and unpredictable workloads**, including retail/ecommerce sites with periodic promotional events. AWS states that for variable workloads with sudden unpredictable increases, Aurora Serverless automatically scales capacity to meet peak load and scales back down after the surge; you do not need to provision for peak or average capacity. It is also cost-effective because it avoids overprovisioning and you pay only for the database resources consumed, measured per second ([Using Aurora serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)). Aurora Serverless scaling is automatic, granular, and nondisruptive, and AWS notes that Aurora manages connections automatically without requiring application connection string changes ([How Aurora serverless works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html)). This directly matches unpredictable monthly sales spikes and the need for cost-effective performance.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B.
