That does not meet the requirement for generated images, especially premium users who can download anytime ([S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)).
- **C**: S3 One Zone-IA provides millisecond access, but the uploaded images are needed only for rare, planned training. Archival storage is more cost-effective for rarely accessed data, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost AWS storage option. Also, One Zone-IA is not resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone ([S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)).
- **D**: It has the same problem as B for generated images: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is archival and not real-time. It also uses S3 One Zone-IA for the uploaded images instead of the lower-cost archival option for rare access ([S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司有一个拥有数千名用户的 Web 应用程序。该应用程序使用 8-10 张用户上传的图像来生成 AI 图像。用户每 6 小时可以下载一次生成的 AI 图像。该公司还有一个高级用户选项，使用户能够随时下载生成的 AI 图像。该公司使用用户上传的图像每年运行两次 AI 模型训练。该公司需要一个存储解决方案来存储这些图像。哪种存储解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 将上传的图像移至 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive。将高级用户生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Standard。将非高级用户生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)。
options.B: 将上传的图像移至 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive 将所有生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval。
options.C: 将上传的图像移至 Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)。将高级用户生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Standard。将非高级用户生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)。
options.D: 将上传的图像移至 Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)。将所有生成的 AI 图像移至 S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval。

zh.explanation:
**答案：A**

A 是这些选项中最具成本效益的选择，因为它将每个图像类别映射到仍符合访问模式的最低成本 S3 类：

- **用户上传的源图像**每年仅需要用于 AI 模型训练两次。它们是归档数据，而不是面向用户的数据。AWS 表示，S3 Glacier 存储类用于低成本、长期存储，并且访问频率较低、检索时间较长的存储类可提供较低的存储成本。S3 Glacier Deep Archive 被描述为 **AWS 中成本最低的存储选项**，适用于可以等待数小时进行检索的数据，并且具有 180 天的最短存储期限——如果提前规划恢复，对于每年两次的训练周期是合理的（[S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)，[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。
- **高级用户生成的 AI 图像**必须能够随时下载，因此需要即时、低延迟访问。S3 Standard 专为频繁访问的数据设计，并提供毫秒级访问（[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。
- **非高级用户生成的 AI 图像**不需要不受限制地随时下载。S3 Standard-IA 专为长期存在、不频繁访问的数据设计，同时仍提供毫秒级访问，使其对于这种访问模式比 S3 Standard 更具成本效益（[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B**：S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 是归档存储，对象**不能用于实时访问**；必须先恢复才能访问。这不满足生成图像的要求，尤其是可以随时下载的高级用户（[S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。
- **C**：S3 One Zone-IA 提供毫秒级访问，但上传的图像仅用于罕见且有计划的训练。对于很少访问的数据，归档存储更具成本效益，而 S3 Glacier Deep Archive 是成本最低的 AWS 存储选项。此外，One Zone-IA 无法抵御 Availability Zone 丢失（[S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。
- **D**：它对于生成图像存在与 B 相同的问题：S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 是归档存储，并非实时访问。它还对上传的图像使用 S3 One Zone-IA，而不是针对罕见访问使用成本更低的归档选项（[S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。

en.question: A company is developing machine learning (ML) models on AWS. The company is developing the ML models as independent microservices. The microservices fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory. Users access the ML models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests. The company provides the ML models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular. Some models are not used for days or weeks. Other models receive batches of thousands of requests at a time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that the NLB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the Lambda functions based on the traffic that the NLB receives.
options.B: Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that the ALB will invoke. Use auto scaling to scale the ECS cluster instances based on the traffic that the ALB receives.
options.C: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as AWS Lambda functions that SQS events will invoke. Use auto scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the size of the SQS queue.
options.D: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the ML models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Use auto scaling for Amazon ECS to scale both the cluster capacity and number of the services based on the size of the SQS queue.

en.explanation:
**Answer: D.**

The workload is asynchronous, bursty, and queue-oriented: users may submit single requests or batches, some models are idle for days/weeks, and other models receive thousands of requests. Amazon SQS is appropriate because it uses distributed queues with producers and consumers, stores messages redundantly, and can scale transparently for load spikes; consumers process and delete messages when ready ([Amazon SQS overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)).

Running the ML model microservices as ECS services that read from SQS is the best fit. ECS Service Auto Scaling can automatically increase or decrease the desired number of tasks, using CloudWatch metrics, to handle peak demand and reduce cost during low utilization ([ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)). AWS also notes that an appropriate scaling metric should correlate with demand and include utilization signals such as I/O queue depth; for an SQS-backed worker service, queue depth/backlog is such a demand signal ([optimizing ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-autoscaling-best-practice.html)). If ECS is using EC2 capacity, ECS cluster auto scaling can manage the EC2 instances registered to the cluster by using capacity providers and CloudWatch alarms to scale the Auto Scaling group in and out ([ECS cluster auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/cluster-auto-scaling.html)).

Why the other options are not best:

* **A**: A load balancer is for request routing, not durable asynchronous buffering. It also does not address irregular batches or queue-based back-pressure. Lambda is additionally a poor fit for heavy ML model initialization because each new execution environment would need to load the ~1 GB model, and Lambda has a hard 15-minute function timeout ([Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)).
* **B**: ECS behind an ALB can scale web services, but this solution does not use a queue. It therefore does not naturally buffer asynchronous batches or let workers drain requests at a controlled rate when thousands of requests arrive.
* **C**: SQS + Lambda is a valid asynchronous pattern, and Lambda can scale SQS event processing based on message volume ([Lambda SQS scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)). However, the option says to “increase the number of vCPUs” for Lambda based on queue size, which is not how Lambda scaling works. Lambda CPU is allocated in proportion to configured memory, and the timeout is 900 seconds/15 minutes ([Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)). For independent ML microservices that load large model data and process potentially large batches, ECS workers are the safer and more flexible compute choice.

Therefore, **SQS + ECS services with both service and cluster capacity auto scaling based on queue backlog** best meets the requirements.

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS 上开发机器学习 (ML) 模型。该公司将这些 ML 模型开发为独立的微服务。微服务在启动时从 Amazon S3 获取约 1 GB 的模型数据，并将数据加载到内存中。用户通过异步 API 访问这些 ML 模型。用户可以发送单个请求或一批请求。该公司向数百名用户提供这些 ML 模型。模型的使用模式不规律。有些模型数天或数周都不会被使用。其他模型则会一次收到数千个请求批次。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 将来自 API 的请求定向到 Network Load Balancer (NLB)。将 ML 模型部署为由 NLB 调用的 AWS Lambda 函数。使用 auto scaling，根据 NLB 接收的流量扩展 Lambda 函数。
options.B: 将来自 API 的请求定向到 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。将 ML 模型部署为由 ALB 调用的 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 服务。使用 auto scaling，根据 ALB 接收的流量扩展 ECS 集群实例。
options.C: 将来自 API 的请求定向到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。将 ML 模型部署为由 SQS 事件调用的 AWS Lambda 函数。使用 auto scaling，根据 SQS 队列的大小增加 Lambda 函数的 vCPU 数量。
options.D: 将来自 API 的请求定向到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。将 ML 模型部署为从队列读取消息的 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 服务。对 Amazon ECS 使用 auto scaling，根据 SQS 队列的大小同时扩展集群容量和服务数量。

zh.explanation:
**答案：D.**

该工作负载是异步的、突发性的，并且以队列为导向：用户可能提交单个请求或批量请求，有些模型会闲置数天/数周，而其他模型会收到数千个请求。Amazon SQS 是合适的，因为它使用具有生产者和消费者的分布式队列，冗余存储消息，并且可以针对负载峰值透明扩展；消费者在准备好时处理并删除消息（[Amazon SQS overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html)）。将 ML 模型微服务作为从 SQS 读取消息的 ECS 服务运行是最佳匹配。ECS Service Auto Scaling 可以使用 CloudWatch 指标自动增加或减少所需任务数，以处理峰值需求并在低利用率期间降低成本（[ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)）。AWS 还指出，合适的扩展指标应与需求相关，并包含利用率信号，例如 I/O 队列深度；对于由 SQS 支持的工作服务，队列深度/积压就是这样的需求信号（[optimizing ECS service auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/capacity-autoscaling-best-practice.html)）。如果 ECS 使用 EC2 容量，ECS cluster auto scaling 可以通过使用容量提供程序和 CloudWatch 警报来扩展 Auto Scaling group 的容量，从而管理注册到集群的 EC2 实例（[ECS cluster auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/cluster-auto-scaling.html)）。为什么其他选项不是最佳选择：

* **A**：负载均衡器用于请求路由，而不是持久的异步缓冲。它也无法解决不规律批次或基于队列的反压问题。此外，Lambda 不太适合繁重的 ML 模型初始化，因为每个新的执行环境都需要加载约 1 GB 的模型，并且 Lambda 有严格的 15 分钟函数超时限制（[Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)）。
* **B**：位于 ALB 后面的 ECS 可以扩展 Web 服务，但此解决方案没有使用队列。因此，当数千个请求到达时，它无法自然地缓冲异步批次，也无法让工作节点以受控速率排空请求。
* **C**：SQS + Lambda 是一种有效的异步模式，并且 Lambda 可以根据消息量扩展 SQS 事件处理（[Lambda SQS scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)）。但是，该选项说要根据队列大小“增加 Lambda 的 vCPU 数量”，这并不是 Lambda 扩展的工作方式。Lambda CPU 按配置的内存比例分配，超时时间为 900 秒/15 分钟（[Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html)）。对于需要加载大型模型数据并处理潜在大型批次的独立 ML 微服务，ECS 工作节点是更安全且更灵活的计算选择。因此，**SQS + ECS 服务，并基于队列积压同时进行服务和集群容量 auto scaling** 最能满足这些要求。

en.question: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The company needs to create a disaster recovery (DR) solution. The acceptable recovery time for the DR solution is up to 30 minutes. The DR solution does not need to support customer usage when the primary infrastructure is healthy. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB and an Auto Scaling group. Set the desired capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to a minimum value. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database. Configure Amazon Route 53 for an active- passive failover with ALB endpoints.
options.B: Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALUpdate the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.
options.C: Back up the Aurora MySQL DB cluster data by using AWS Backup. Deploy the DR infrastructure in a second AWS Region with an ALB. Update the Auto Scaling group to include EC2 instances from the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora MySQL DB cluster in the second Region Restore the data from the backup.
options.D: Back up the infrastructure configuration by using AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Set the Auto Scaling group desired capacity to zero. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Convert the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to an Aurora global database.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.**

The requirement is an active/passive DR solution with an RTO up to 30 minutes and no need to serve customers from the DR Region while the primary Region is healthy. AWS describes active/passive DR as a primary site serving traffic and a passive site used for recovery only. A scaled-down DR environment with data replication is consistent with pilot light/warm standby patterns; warm standby is a “scaled down, but fully functional” copy in another Region and decreases recovery time because it is always on, while traffic management uses active/passive routing to switch to the recovery endpoint when needed ([AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)).

Option A deploys the web tier in a second Region with an ALB and a minimally sized Auto Scaling group, uses Aurora Global Database for cross-Region database replication, and configures Route 53 active-passive failover. Aurora Global Database replicates to secondary Regions with latency typically under a second and is designed to make a database available in a new primary Region with lower RTO/RPO than traditional replication ([Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html)). Route 53 active-passive failover is specifically for a primary resource that is normally used and a secondary resource that remains on standby until primary resources become unavailable ([Route 53 failover types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)). Route 53 can route to ELB/ALB endpoints using alias records ([Route 53 to ELB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-elb-load-balancer.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **B** is incorrect because it proposes active-active failover, but the DR solution does not need to support customer usage during normal operation. Also, an EC2 Auto Scaling group spans Availability Zones in the Region you are working in, not multiple Regions ([EC2 Auto Scaling Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)).
* **C** is incorrect for the same cross-Region Auto Scaling group issue and because restoring the Aurora cluster from backup at failover time is a backup-and-restore approach. AWS notes that backup data in the DR Region must be restored at failover time, increasing recovery time and potentially exceeding the RTO ([AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)).
* **D** is incorrect because relying on AWS Backup to recreate the infrastructure in the second Region is not the best fit for a 30-minute RTO. AWS states that for backup/restore, infrastructure and configuration must be redeployed in the recovery Region and that without proper IaC this can increase recovery times and exceed the RTO; it also notes EC2 backup metadata is only used when restoring to the same Region ([AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司在 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行一个 Web 应用程序。该应用程序将数据存储在 Amazon Aurora MySQL DB 集群中。公司需要创建灾难恢复 (DR) 解决方案。该 DR 解决方案可接受的恢复时间最长为 30 分钟。当主基础设施运行正常时，DR 解决方案不需要支持客户使用。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 在第二个 AWS Region 中部署 DR 基础设施，包括一个 ALB 和一个 Auto Scaling 组。将 Auto Scaling 组的所需容量和最大容量设置为最小值。将 Aurora MySQL DB 集群转换为 Aurora global database。配置 Amazon Route 53，以 ALB 端点进行主动-被动故障转移。
options.B: 在第二个 AWS Region 中使用 ALUpdate 部署 DR 基础设施，将 Auto Scaling 组更新为包含来自第二个 Region 的 EC2 实例。使用 Amazon Route 53 配置主动-主动故障转移。将 Aurora MySQL DB 集群转换为 Aurora global database。
options.C: 使用 AWS Backup 备份 Aurora MySQL DB 集群数据。在第二个 AWS Region 中部署带有 ALB 的 DR 基础设施。将 Auto Scaling 组更新为包含来自第二个 Region 的 EC2 实例。使用 Amazon Route 53 配置主动-主动故障转移。在第二个 Region 中创建 Aurora MySQL DB 集群。从备份中还原数据。
options.D: 使用 AWS Backup 备份基础设施配置。使用该备份在第二个 AWS Region 中创建所需的基础设施。将 Auto Scaling 组的所需容量设置为零。使用 Amazon Route 53 配置主动-被动故障转移。将 Aurora MySQL DB 集群转换为 Aurora global database。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A。**

要求是一个主动/被动 DR 解决方案，RTO 最长为 30 分钟，并且在主 Region 健康时不需要从 DR Region 为客户提供服务。AWS 将主动/被动 DR 描述为主站点提供流量服务，被动站点仅用于恢复。带有数据复制的缩减规模 DR 环境符合 pilot light/warm standby 模式；warm standby 是另一个 Region 中“缩减规模但功能完整”的副本，并且由于它始终开启而缩短恢复时间，同时流量管理使用主动/被动路由在需要时切换到恢复端点（[AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)）。选项 A 在第二个 Region 中部署 Web 层，包括一个 ALB 和一个最小规模的 Auto Scaling 组，使用 Aurora Global Database 进行跨 Region 数据库复制，并配置 Route 53 主动-被动故障转移。Aurora Global Database 复制到辅助 Regions 的延迟通常低于一秒，并且旨在以比传统复制更低的 RTO/RPO 使数据库在新的主 Region 中可用（[Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html)）。Route 53 主动-被动故障转移专门用于通常使用的主资源，以及在主资源不可用之前保持备用状态的辅助资源（[Route 53 failover types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)）。Route 53 可以使用别名记录将流量路由到 ELB/ALB 端点（[Route 53 to ELB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-elb-load-balancer.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **B** 不正确，因为它提出主动-主动故障转移，但 DR 解决方案在正常运行期间不需要支持客户使用。此外，EC2 Auto Scaling 组跨越的是你正在使用的 Region 中的 Availability Zones，而不是多个 Regions（[EC2 Auto Scaling Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)）。
* **C** 不正确，原因同样包括跨 Region Auto Scaling 组的问题，并且因为在故障转移时从备份还原 Aurora 集群是一种备份和还原方法。AWS 指出，DR Region 中的备份数据必须在故障转移时还原，这会增加恢复时间并可能超过 RTO（[AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)）。
* **D** 不正确，因为依赖 AWS Backup 在第二个 Region 中重新创建基础设施并不最适合 30 分钟 RTO。AWS 表示，对于备份/还原，必须在恢复 Region 中重新部署基础设施和配置，并且如果没有适当的 IaC，这可能会增加恢复时间并超过 RTO；它还指出 EC2 备份元数据仅在还原到同一 Region 时使用（[AWS DR options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)）。

en.question: A company is migrating its data processing application to the AWS Cloud. The application processes several short-lived batch jobs that cannot be disrupted. Data is generated after each batch job is completed. The data is accessed for 30 days and retained for 2 years. The company wants to keep the cost of running the application in the AWS Cloud as low as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Instant. Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
options.B: Migrate the data processing application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Move the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
options.C: Deploy Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.
options.D: Deploy Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to run the batch jobs. Store the data in Amazon S3 Standard. Move the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days. Set an expiration to delete the data after 2 years.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: D.**

The batch jobs **cannot be disrupted**, so Spot Instances are not appropriate: AWS states that Spot Instances are cost-effective only when applications are flexible about when they run and **can be interrupted**. On-Demand Instances are therefore the suitable EC2 choice for uninterrupted jobs, and they are billed for the instances you launch without requiring a long-term commitment ([Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html)).

For the output data, it is accessed for the first 30 days, so S3 Standard is appropriate for frequently accessed data with millisecond access and no minimum storage duration ([Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)). After 30 days, the data only needs to be retained for 2 years. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is AWS's **lowest-cost storage option** for archive data accessed less than once a year, with a 180-day minimum storage duration, which fits a 2-year retention period ([S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)). S3 Lifecycle rules can transition objects to less-expensive storage classes and then expire/delete them, matching the 30-day transition and 2-year deletion requirement ([Managing the lifecycle of objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lifecycle-mgmt.html)).

Why the other options are wrong:

* **A**: Uses Spot Instances, which can be interrupted, violating the requirement that jobs cannot be disrupted. It also uses S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 30 days instead of the lower-cost Deep Archive for long-term retention.
* **B**: Uses On-Demand Instances, but stores newly generated, 30-day-accessed data directly in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. That class is recommended for long-term data accessed once per quarter and has a 90-day minimum storage duration, so transitioning it after only 30 days is not cost-optimal.
* **C**: Uses Spot Instances, which can be interrupted. It also uses S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval rather than Deep Archive, while Deep Archive is the lowest-cost AWS storage option for long-term archive data when immediate retrieval is not required.

zh.question: 一家公司正在将其数据处理应用程序迁移到 AWS Cloud。该应用程序处理多个生命周期较短且不能被中断的批处理作业。每个批处理作业完成后会生成数据。这些数据会被访问 30 天，并保留 2 年。该公司希望尽可能降低在 AWS Cloud 中运行该应用程序的成本。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 将数据处理应用程序迁移到 Amazon EC2 Spot Instances。将数据存储在 Amazon S3 Standard 中。30 天后将数据移动到 Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval。设置过期规则，在 2 年后删除数据。
options.B: 将数据处理应用程序迁移到 Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances。将数据存储在 Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval 中。30 天后将数据移动到 S3 Glacier Deep Archive。设置过期规则，在 2 年后删除数据。
options.C: 部署 Amazon EC2 Spot Instances 来运行批处理作业。将数据存储在 Amazon S3 Standard 中。30 天后将数据移动到 Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval。设置过期规则，在 2 年后删除数据。
options.D: 部署 Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances 来运行批处理作业。将数据存储在 Amazon S3 Standard 中。30 天后将数据移动到 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive。设置过期规则，在 2 年后删除数据。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：D。**

批处理作业**不能被中断**，因此 Spot Instances 不合适：AWS 表示，只有当应用程序对运行时间具有灵活性并且**可以被中断**时，Spot Instances 才具有成本效益。因此，On-Demand Instances 是适合不中断作业的 EC2 选择，并且它们按你启动的实例计费，无需长期承诺（[Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html)）。对于输出数据，前 30 天会被访问，因此 S3 Standard 适合需要毫秒级访问且没有最低存储期限的频繁访问数据（[Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。30 天后，数据只需要保留 2 年。S3 Glacier Deep Archive 是 AWS 针对每年访问少于一次的归档数据的**最低成本存储选项**，最低存储期限为 180 天，符合 2 年保留期（[S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)）。S3 Lifecycle 规则可以将对象转换到成本更低的存储类，然后使其过期/删除，符合 30 天转换和 2 年删除的要求（[Managing the lifecycle of objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lifecycle-mgmt.html)）。其他选项错误的原因：

* **A**：使用 Spot Instances，它们可能被中断，违反了作业不能被中断的要求。它还在 30 天后使用 S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval，而不是用于长期保留且成本更低的 Deep Archive。
* **B**：使用 On-Demand Instances，但将新生成且会被访问 30 天的数据直接存储在 S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval 中。该存储类建议用于每季度访问一次的长期数据，并且有 90 天的最低存储期限，因此仅 30 天后就转换并非成本最优。
* **C**：使用 Spot Instances，它们可能被中断。它还使用 S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 而不是 Deep Archive，而当不需要立即检索时，Deep Archive 是用于长期归档数据的最低成本 AWS 存储选项。

en.question: A company needs to design a hybrid network architecture. The company's workloads are currently stored in the AWS Cloud and in on-premises data centers. The workloads require single-digit latencies to communicate. The company uses an AWS Transit Gateway transit gateway to connect multiple VPCs. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

options.A: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to each VPC.
options.B: Associate an AWS Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.
options.C: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to an AWS Direct Connect gateway.
options.D: Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection. Create a transit virtual interface (VIF) to a Direct Connect gateway.
options.E: Associate AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections with the transit gateway that is attached to the VPCs.

en.explanation:
The best choices are **B and D**.

- **B is correct** because AWS documents the intended architecture for this case: use a **Direct Connect gateway** to connect a Direct Connect connection, over a transit virtual interface, to the **VPCs or VPNs attached to a transit gateway**, and **associate the Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway** ([Direct Connect gateways and transit gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)). This lets the existing transit gateway provide hub connectivity to multiple VPCs instead of building separate connections to each VPC.
- **D is correct** because to connect Direct Connect to a transit gateway, AWS says you must create a **transit virtual interface** for the Direct Connect connection and specify the Direct Connect gateway ([Create a transit virtual interface to the Direct Connect gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-transit-vif-for-gateway.html)). Direct Connect links the on-premises network to an AWS Direct Connect location and can create virtual interfaces to Amazon VPC while **bypassing internet service providers in the network path**, which is the appropriate choice for low, consistent latency requirements ([What is Direct Connect?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A is incorrect** because creating a Site-to-Site VPN connection to each VPC does not use the existing transit gateway hub and is not the most cost-effective scalable design for multiple VPCs. A virtual private gateway is attached to a **single VPC**, whereas a transit gateway is the hub for multiple VPCs and on-premises networks ([What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)).
- **C is incorrect** because Site-to-Site VPN uses target gateways such as a virtual private gateway or transit gateway; a Direct Connect gateway is not the VPN endpoint described for Site-to-Site VPN ([What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)).
- **E is incorrect** because Site-to-Site VPN can attach to a transit gateway, but VPN is an IPsec VPN connection rather than the dedicated Direct Connect path needed for single-digit latency-sensitive hybrid workloads. Direct Connect with a transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway is the documented architecture for connecting Direct Connect to transit gateway-attached VPCs ([Direct Connect gateways and transit gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司需要设计混合网络架构。该公司的工作负载目前存储在 AWS Cloud 和本地数据中心中。这些工作负载需要个位数延迟来进行通信。该公司使用 AWS Transit Gateway transit gateway 来连接多个 VPC。哪组步骤组合能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 为每个 VPC 建立 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 连接。
options.B: 将 AWS Direct Connect gateway 与已连接到 VPC 的 transit gateway 关联。
options.C: 建立到 AWS Direct Connect gateway 的 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 连接。
options.D: 建立 AWS Direct Connect 连接。创建到 Direct Connect gateway 的 transit virtual interface (VIF)。
options.E: 将 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 连接与已连接到 VPC 的 transit gateway 关联。

zh.explanation:
最佳选择是 **B 和 D**。

- **B 正确**，因为 AWS 文档说明了此场景的预期架构：使用 **Direct Connect gateway** 将 Direct Connect 连接通过 transit virtual interface 连接到**附加到 transit gateway 的 VPCs 或 VPNs**，并**将 Direct Connect gateway 与 transit gateway 关联**（[Direct Connect gateways and transit gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)）。这样可以让现有的 transit gateway 为多个 VPC 提供中心辐射式连接，而无需为每个 VPC 构建单独连接。
- **D 正确**，因为要将 Direct Connect 连接到 transit gateway，AWS 表示必须为 Direct Connect 连接创建 **transit virtual interface**，并指定 Direct Connect gateway（[Create a transit virtual interface to the Direct Connect gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-transit-vif-for-gateway.html)）。Direct Connect 将本地网络连接到 AWS Direct Connect 位置，并且可以创建到 Amazon VPC 的虚拟接口，同时**绕过网络路径中的互联网服务提供商**，这对于低且稳定延迟的要求是合适的选择（[What is Direct Connect?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A 不正确**，因为为每个 VPC 创建 Site-to-Site VPN 连接没有使用现有的 transit gateway hub，并且对于多个 VPC 来说并不是最具成本效益的可扩展设计。virtual private gateway 附加到**单个 VPC**，而 transit gateway 是多个 VPC 和本地网络的中心 hub（[What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)）。
- **C 不正确**，因为 Site-to-Site VPN 使用的目标网关包括 virtual private gateway 或 transit gateway；Direct Connect gateway 并不是 Site-to-Site VPN 所描述的 VPN 端点（[What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)）。
- **E 不正确**，因为 Site-to-Site VPN 可以附加到 transit gateway，但 VPN 是 IPsec VPN 连接，而不是个位数延迟敏感型混合工作负载所需的专用 Direct Connect 路径。使用带有 transit VIF 的 Direct Connect 连接到 Direct Connect gateway，是将 Direct Connect 连接到附加了 transit gateway 的 VPCs 的文档化架构（[Direct Connect gateways and transit gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)）。

en.question: A global ecommerce company runs its critical workloads on AWS. The workloads use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance that is configured for a Multi-AZ deployment. Customers have reported application timeouts when the company undergoes database failovers. The company needs a resilient solution to reduce failover time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon RDS Proxy. Assign the proxy to the DB instance.
options.B: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Move the read traffic to the read replica.
options.C: Enable Performance Insights. Monitor the CPU load to identify the timeouts.
options.D: Take regular automatic snapshots. Copy the automatic snapshots to multiple AWS Regions.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Create an Amazon RDS Proxy. Assign the proxy to the DB instance.**

Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance failover is automatic, but AWS states that failover typically takes **60–120 seconds** and existing connections must be re-established after DNS changes to the standby instance ([Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html)). RDS Proxy is designed for this scenario: it pools and shares database connections and makes applications more resilient by **automatically connecting to a standby DB instance while preserving application connections** ([Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)). Therefore, placing RDS Proxy in front of the PostgreSQL DB instance reduces application disruption and timeout impact during failover.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Read replica:** Read replicas are for read scaling; AWS describes them as read-only copies used to reduce load by routing read queries to replicas ([Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)). This does not reduce Multi-AZ writer failover time for the application.
- **C. Performance Insights:** Performance Insights helps visualize and analyze DB load and troubleshoot performance ([Monitoring DB load with Performance Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html)). It is diagnostic, not a failover-acceleration or connection-preservation solution.
- **D. Automated snapshots copied to Regions:** Automated backups and snapshots are for backup and point-in-time recovery; AWS notes that backups let you recover a DB instance within the retention period ([Introduction to backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html)). They do not reduce failover time for an active Multi-AZ database.

zh.question: 一家全球电子商务公司在 AWS 上运行其关键工作负载。这些工作负载使用一个 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB 实例，该实例配置为 Multi-AZ 部署。客户报告称，当公司发生数据库故障转移时，应用程序会出现超时。公司需要一种具有弹性的解决方案来减少故障转移时间。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon RDS Proxy。将该代理分配给该 DB 实例。
options.B: 为该 DB 实例创建一个只读副本。将读取流量转移到该只读副本。
options.C: 启用 Performance Insights。监控 CPU 负载以识别超时。
options.D: 定期创建自动快照。将自动快照复制到多个 AWS Regions。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 创建一个 Amazon RDS Proxy。将该代理分配给该 DB 实例。**

Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB 实例故障转移是自动的，但 AWS 声明故障转移通常需要 **60–120 秒**，并且在 DNS 更改到备用实例后，现有连接必须重新建立（[Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html)）。RDS Proxy 正是为这种场景而设计的：它会池化并共享数据库连接，并通过**在保留应用程序连接的同时自动连接到备用 DB 实例**来提高应用程序的弹性（[Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)）。因此，将 RDS Proxy 放在 PostgreSQL DB 实例前面，可以减少故障转移期间的应用程序中断和超时影响。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. Read replica：** 只读副本用于读取扩展；AWS 将其描述为只读副本，通过将读取查询路由到副本来减少负载（[Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。这不会减少应用程序的 Multi-AZ 写入器故障转移时间。
- **C. Performance Insights：** Performance Insights 帮助可视化和分析 DB 负载并排查性能问题（[Monitoring DB load with Performance Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PerfInsights.html)）。它是一种诊断工具，而不是加速故障转移或保留连接的解决方案。
- **D. Automated snapshots copied to Regions：** 自动备份和快照用于备份和时间点恢复；AWS 指出，备份可让你在保留期内恢复 DB 实例（[Introduction to backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.html)）。它们不会减少活动 Multi-AZ 数据库的故障转移时间。

en.question: A company has multiple Amazon RDS DB instances that run in a development AWS account. All the instances have tags to identify them as development resources. The company needs the development DB instances to run on a schedule only during business hours. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to identify RDS instances that need to be stopped. Create an AWS Lambda function to start and stop the RDS instances.
options.B: Create an AWS Trusted Advisor report to identify RDS instances to be started and stopped. Create an AWS Lambda function to start and stop the RDS instances.
options.C: Create AWS Systems Manager State Manager associations to start and stop the RDS instances.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the RDS instances.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.**

AWS Systems Manager State Manager is the lowest-overhead fit because AWS documents this exact pattern: you can create a State Manager association with an Automation runbook, target resources by **tags**, run it **on a schedule** with cron or rate expressions, and use it to **start, restart, or stop Amazon RDS instances**. The Systems Manager Automation runbook reference also lists predefined RDS runbooks, including **AWS-StartRdsInstance** and **AWS-StopRdsInstance**, so no custom code is required. ([Scheduling automations with State Manager associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/scheduling-automations-state-manager-associations.html), [Amazon RDS Automation runbooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-ref-rds.html))

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** CloudWatch alarms are for monitoring metrics and taking actions on alarm state changes; they are not the simplest way to implement a tag-based business-hours schedule for RDS. This option also requires custom Lambda code. ([Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html))
- **B:** Trusted Advisor inspects the AWS environment and makes recommendations for cost, performance, availability, and security; it is not a scheduling/automation service for starting and stopping RDS instances. This option also requires custom Lambda code. ([AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html))
- **D:** EventBridge can schedule Lambda invocations, but this requires creating and maintaining Lambda functions to identify tagged RDS instances and call start/stop APIs. AWS also notes that EventBridge scheduled rules are a legacy feature. Compared with State Manager associations plus predefined RDS Automation runbooks, this has more operational overhead. ([Schedule a Lambda function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html))

zh.question: 一家公司在一个开发 AWS 账户中运行多个 Amazon RDS DB 实例。所有实例都有标签，用于将它们标识为开发资源。公司需要让这些开发 DB 实例仅在工作时间按计划运行。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon CloudWatch 警报来识别需要停止的 RDS 实例。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来启动和停止 RDS 实例。
options.B: 创建一个 AWS Trusted Advisor 报告来识别需要启动和停止的 RDS 实例。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来启动和停止 RDS 实例。
options.C: 创建 AWS Systems Manager State Manager 关联来启动和停止 RDS 实例。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，用于调用 AWS Lambda 函数来启动和停止 RDS 实例。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C.**

AWS Systems Manager State Manager 是运营开销最低的合适选择，因为 AWS 文档记录了这种精确模式：你可以创建一个带有 Automation runbook 的 State Manager 关联，通过 **tags** 定位资源，使用 cron 或 rate 表达式 **on a schedule** 运行，并用它来 **start, restart, or stop Amazon RDS instances**。Systems Manager Automation runbook 参考还列出了预定义的 RDS runbooks，包括 **AWS-StartRdsInstance** 和 **AWS-StopRdsInstance**，因此不需要自定义代码。([Scheduling automations with State Manager associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/scheduling-automations-state-manager-associations.html), [Amazon RDS Automation runbooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-ref-rds.html))

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A:** CloudWatch 警报用于监控指标并在警报状态变化时采取操作；它们不是为 RDS 实现基于标签的工作时间计划的最简单方式。此选项还需要自定义 Lambda 代码。([Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Alarms.html))
- **B:** Trusted Advisor 会检查 AWS 环境，并针对成本、性能、可用性和安全性提出建议；它不是用于启动和停止 RDS 实例的调度/自动化服务。此选项还需要自定义 Lambda 代码。([AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html))
- **D:** EventBridge 可以调度 Lambda 调用，但这需要创建和维护 Lambda 函数，以识别带标签的 RDS 实例并调用启动/停止 API。AWS 还指出 EventBridge 计划规则是一项旧版功能。与 State Manager 关联加预定义 RDS Automation runbooks 相比，这具有更多运营开销。([Schedule a Lambda function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html))

en.question: A consumer survey company has gathered data for several years from a specific geographic region. The company stores this data in an Amazon S3 bucket in an AWS Region. The company has started to share this data with a marketing firm in a new geographic region. The company has granted the firm's AWS account access to the S3 bucket. The company wants to minimize the data transfer costs when the marketing firm requests data from the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company’s S3 bucket.
options.B: Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the company’s S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.
options.C: Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share the S3 bucket with the marketing firm AWS account.
options.D: Configure the company’s S3 bucket to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering Sync the S3 bucket to one of the marketing firm’s S3 buckets.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A. Configure the Requester Pays feature on the company’s S3 bucket.**

Requester Pays is designed for this exact pattern: an S3 bucket owner shares data with another AWS account and wants the requester to bear the request and data-transfer-out charges. AWS states that for successful Requester Pays requests, “the requester pays for the data transfer and the request, and the bucket owner pays for the data storage” ([Amazon S3 Requester Pays](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html)). Therefore, when the marketing firm requests data, the consumer survey company minimizes its own data transfer costs for those requests.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)** – CRR copies objects to a bucket in another Region, but it introduces replication requirements and costs. AWS notes that CRR copies objects across buckets in different Regions and that inter-Region data transfer charges vary by Region ([S3 replication considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-requirements.html)). This does not directly make the marketing firm pay for requests from the company’s bucket; it can add replication and storage overhead.
- **C. AWS Resource Access Manager** – AWS RAM is for sharing supported resources across accounts. The RAM shareable resources list for Amazon S3 includes **S3 Access Grants**, not a general-purpose S3 bucket itself ([AWS RAM shareable resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html)). Also, RAM pricing documentation says resource usage charges vary by the owning service, so RAM itself does not solve S3 data-transfer cost allocation ([AWS RAM pricing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)).
- **D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering** – Intelligent-Tiering optimizes **storage** costs by moving objects among access tiers based on access patterns; it does not shift or minimize data-transfer-out charges for another account’s requests ([S3 Intelligent-Tiering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html)).

zh.question: 一家消费者调查公司多年来从某个特定地理区域收集了数据。该公司将这些数据存储在一个 AWS Region 中的 Amazon S3 bucket 中。该公司已开始与位于新地理区域的一家营销公司共享这些数据。该公司已授予该营销公司的 AWS 账户访问该 S3 bucket 的权限。当营销公司从该 S3 bucket 请求数据时，该公司希望最大限度降低数据传输成本。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在公司的 S3 bucket 上配置 Requester Pays 功能。
options.B: 配置 S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)，将公司的 S3 bucket 复制到营销公司的某个 S3 bucket。
options.C: 配置 AWS Resource Access Manager，以便与营销公司 AWS 账户共享该 S3 bucket。
options.D: 将公司的 S3 bucket 配置为使用 S3 Intelligent-Tiering，并将该 S3 bucket 同步到营销公司的某个 S3 bucket。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A. 在公司的 S3 bucket 上配置 Requester Pays 功能。**

Requester Pays 正是为这种模式设计的：S3 bucket 所有者与另一个 AWS 账户共享数据，并希望由请求者承担请求费用和数据传出费用。AWS 表示，对于成功的 Requester Pays 请求，“请求者支付数据传输和请求费用，bucket 所有者支付数据存储费用”([Amazon S3 Requester Pays](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/RequesterPaysBuckets.html))。因此，当营销公司请求数据时，消费者调查公司可以最大限度降低这些请求产生的自身数据传输成本。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)** – CRR 会将对象复制到另一个 Region 中的 bucket，但它会引入复制要求和成本。AWS 指出，CRR 会在不同 Regions 中的 bucket 之间复制对象，并且跨 Region 数据传输费用因 Region 而异（[S3 replication considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-requirements.html)）。这并不会直接让营销公司为从公司 bucket 发起的请求付费；它可能增加复制和存储开销。
- **C. AWS Resource Access Manager** – AWS RAM 用于在账户之间共享受支持的资源。Amazon S3 的 RAM 可共享资源列表包括 **S3 Access Grants**，而不是通用的 S3 bucket 本身（[AWS RAM shareable resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html)）。此外，RAM 定价文档说明资源使用费用因拥有该资源的服务而异，因此 RAM 本身不能解决 S3 数据传输成本分摊问题（[AWS RAM pricing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)）。
- **D. S3 Intelligent-Tiering** – Intelligent-Tiering 通过根据访问模式在访问层之间移动对象来优化**存储**成本；它不会为另一个账户的请求转移或降低数据传出费用（[S3 Intelligent-Tiering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html)）。

en.question: A company uses AWS to host its public ecommerce website. The website uses an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator for traffic from the internet. The Global Accelerator accelerator forwards the traffic to an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is the entry point for an Auto Scaling group. The company recently identified a DDoS attack on the website. The company needs a solution to mitigate future attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

options.A: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL for the Global Accelerator accelerator to block traffic by using rate-based rules
options.B: Configure an AWS Lambda function to read the ALB metrics to block attacks by updating a VPC network ACL
options.C: Configure an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB to block traffic by using rate-based rules
options.D: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the Global Accelerator accelerator

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.** AWS WAF web ACLs can be associated with an **Application Load Balancer** as a regional protected resource; the AWS WAF supported association list includes Application Load Balancer but does **not** include AWS Global Accelerator ([AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)). A rate-based rule is appropriate for this DDoS mitigation use case because AWS WAF can rate limit requests whose aggregation count is over the configured limit, and with the **Block** action AWS WAF blocks those requests ([AWS WAF rate limiting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-request-limiting.html)). This requires only adding/associating a web ACL to the existing ALB, so it is the least-effort option.

**Why the other options are wrong:**

- **A:** AWS WAF web ACL associations list ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify, and CloudFront—not Global Accelerator—so configuring WAF directly on the accelerator is not supported by the documented association options ([AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)).
- **B:** Building a Lambda function to inspect ALB metrics and update network ACLs is a custom automation approach and is not the least implementation effort. AWS WAF already provides native request rate limiting and blocking for an ALB ([AWS WAF rate limiting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-request-limiting.html)).
- **D:** Adding CloudFront in front of the existing Global Accelerator changes the architecture and adds more implementation work. Also, CloudFront would need its own WAF association to provide the requested rate-based blocking; simply placing CloudFront in front is not the least-effort mitigation. AWS WAF can instead be associated directly with the existing ALB ([AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 AWS 托管其公共电子商务网站。该网站使用 AWS Global Accelerator accelerator 来处理来自互联网的流量。Global Accelerator accelerator 将流量转发到 Application Load Balancer (ALB)，该 ALB 是 Auto Scaling group 的入口点。该公司最近发现网站遭受了 DDoS 攻击。公司需要一种解决方案来缓解未来的攻击。哪种解决方案能够以最少的实施工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 为 Global Accelerator accelerator 配置 AWS WAF web ACL，通过使用基于速率的规则来阻止流量
options.B: 配置 AWS Lambda 函数读取 ALB 指标，并通过更新 VPC network ACL 来阻止攻击
options.C: 在 ALB 上配置 AWS WAF web ACL，通过使用基于速率的规则来阻止流量
options.D: 在 Global Accelerator accelerator 前面配置 Amazon CloudFront distribution

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C。** AWS WAF web ACL 可以与 **Application Load Balancer** 关联，作为区域性受保护资源；AWS WAF 支持的关联列表包括 Application Load Balancer，但**不**包括 AWS Global Accelerator（[AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)）。基于速率的规则适用于此 DDoS 缓解用例，因为 AWS WAF 可以对聚合计数超过配置限制的请求进行速率限制，并且通过 **Block** 操作，AWS WAF 会阻止这些请求（[AWS WAF rate limiting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-request-limiting.html)）。这只需要向现有 ALB 添加/关联 web ACL，因此是工作量最少的选项。

**为什么其他选项是错误的：**

- **A:** AWS WAF web ACL 关联列表包含 ALB、API Gateway、AppSync、Cognito、App Runner、Verified Access、Amplify 和 CloudFront，而不包含 Global Accelerator，因此根据记录的关联选项，不支持直接在 accelerator 上配置 WAF（[AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)）。
- **B:** 构建 Lambda 函数来检查 ALB 指标并更新 network ACL 是一种自定义自动化方法，并不是实施工作量最少的方案。AWS WAF 已经为 ALB 提供原生的请求速率限制和阻止功能（[AWS WAF rate limiting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-request-limiting.html)）。
- **D:** 在现有 Global Accelerator 前面添加 CloudFront 会改变架构并增加更多实施工作。此外，CloudFront 需要自己的 WAF 关联才能提供所请求的基于速率的阻止；仅将 CloudFront 放在前面并不是工作量最少的缓解措施。AWS WAF 可以改为直接与现有 ALB 关联（[AWS WAF resource associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html)）。

en.question: A company uses an Amazon DynamoDB table to store data that the company receives from devices. The DynamoDB table supports a customer-facing website to display recent activity on customer devices. The company configured the table with provisioned throughput for writes and reads. The company wants to calculate performance metrics for customer device data on a daily basis. The solution must have minimal effect on the table's provisioned read and write capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an Amazon Athena SQL query with the Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
options.B: Use an AWS Glue job with the AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
options.C: Use an Amazon Redshift COPY command to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.
options.D: Use an Amazon EMR job with an Apache Hive external table to calculate performance metrics on a recurring schedule.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.**

The requirement is to run daily analytics with **minimal effect on the DynamoDB table’s provisioned read and write capacity**. DynamoDB export to S3 is designed for this: AWS states that exports are asynchronous, **do not consume read capacity units (RCUs)**, and have **no impact on table performance and availability**. The feature is also intended for analytics using services such as **AWS Glue**. The AWS Glue DynamoDB **export connector** invokes `ExportTableToPointInTime` and reads the exported data from Amazon S3; AWS Glue notes that, with this connector, you do not configure DynamoDB throughput read percentage, unlike the standard ETL connector. Therefore, a recurring AWS Glue job using the DynamoDB export connector best meets the requirement.

Why the other options are not best:

* **A. Athena DynamoDB connector** — This queries DynamoDB directly. The connector requires DynamoDB read access and uses `Query` and `Scan` operations; AWS also warns that scans can consume a large number of RCUs. That does not minimize impact on a provisioned-capacity table.
* **C. Amazon Redshift COPY** — COPY can load from sources such as S3 or DynamoDB, but it is a data-loading mechanism, not the best minimal-impact analytics pattern here. Loading directly from DynamoDB would still involve accessing the table, whereas exporting to S3 avoids RCU consumption.
* **D. EMR with Hive external table** — Amazon EMR Hive integration can import, export, query, and join DynamoDB data, but this interaction with DynamoDB is not the minimal-impact approach compared with DynamoDB export to S3, which explicitly avoids RCU consumption and table-performance impact.

Sources: [DynamoDB export to S3: how it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/S3DataExport.HowItWorks.html), [AWS Glue DynamoDB connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-dynamodb-home.html), [Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/connectors-dynamodb.html), [Import DynamoDB data into Hive with Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-input-dynamodb.html), [Amazon Redshift COPY](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_COPY.html).

zh.question: 一家公司使用 Amazon DynamoDB 表来存储公司从设备接收的数据。该 DynamoDB 表支持面向客户的网站，用于显示客户设备上的近期活动。公司为该表配置了预置吞吐量以支持写入和读取。公司希望每天计算客户设备数据的性能指标。该解决方案必须对表的预置读写容量产生最小影响。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon Athena SQL 查询，并通过 Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector 按重复计划计算性能指标。
options.B: 使用 AWS Glue 作业，并通过 AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector 按重复计划计算性能指标。
options.C: 使用 Amazon Redshift COPY 命令按重复计划计算性能指标。
options.D: 使用带有 Apache Hive 外部表的 Amazon EMR 作业按重复计划计算性能指标。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B。**

要求是运行每日分析，并且对 **DynamoDB 表的预置读写容量** 产生最小影响。DynamoDB export to S3 正是为此而设计的：AWS 声明导出是异步的，**不消耗读取容量单位 (RCUs)**，并且对**表性能和可用性没有影响**。该功能也适用于使用 **AWS Glue** 等服务进行分析。AWS Glue DynamoDB **export connector** 会调用 `ExportTableToPointInTime`，并从 Amazon S3 读取导出的数据；AWS Glue 指出，使用此 connector 时，与标准 ETL connector 不同，你无需配置 DynamoDB 吞吐量读取百分比。因此，使用 DynamoDB export connector 的重复执行 AWS Glue 作业最符合该要求。为什么其他选项不是最佳选择：

* **A. Athena DynamoDB connector** — 这会直接查询 DynamoDB。该 connector 需要 DynamoDB 读取访问权限，并使用 `Query` 和 `Scan` 操作；AWS 还警告说，扫描可能会消耗大量 RCUs。这并不能最小化对预置容量表的影响。
* **C. Amazon Redshift COPY** — COPY 可以从 S3 或 DynamoDB 等来源加载数据，但它是一种数据加载机制，并不是这里影响最小的最佳分析模式。直接从 DynamoDB 加载仍然会涉及访问该表，而导出到 S3 可避免 RCU 消耗。
* **D. EMR with Hive external table** — Amazon EMR Hive 集成可以导入、导出、查询和联接 DynamoDB 数据，但与 DynamoDB export to S3 相比，这种与 DynamoDB 的交互并不是影响最小的方法；后者明确避免 RCU 消耗和对表性能的影响。来源：[DynamoDB export to S3: how it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/S3DataExport.HowItWorks.html), [AWS Glue DynamoDB connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-dynamodb-home.html), [Amazon Athena DynamoDB connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/connectors-dynamodb.html), [Import DynamoDB data into Hive with Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-plan-input-dynamodb.html), [Amazon Redshift COPY](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_COPY.html).

en.question: A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new stateless application that will be deployed on AWS. The solutions architect created an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) and launch template for the application. Based on the number of jobs that need to be processed, the processing must run in parallel while adding and removing application Amazon EC2 instances as needed. The application must be loosely coupled. The job items must be durably stored. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on CPU usage.
options.B: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on network usage.
options.C: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on the number of items in the SQS queue.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Auto Scaling group by using the launch template with the scaling policy set to add and remove EC2 instances based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: C.**

The workload is stateless, parallel, and queue-driven. Amazon SQS is the right service to loosely couple producers from worker EC2 instances: AWS lists SQS standard queues as suitable for “decoupling live user requests from intensive background work” and for “allocating tasks to multiple worker nodes.” SQS also durably stores messages by redundantly storing them in multiple Availability Zones before acknowledging them, which addresses the durable job storage requirement ([Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)).

For scaling, AWS specifically documents an Auto Scaling group that processes messages from an SQS queue and uses a scaling policy based on queue backlog/queue length per instance. The documentation describes calculating backlog from the `ApproximateNumberOfMessages` queue attribute and configuring a target tracking policy so the Auto Scaling group scales out when backlog exceeds the target ([Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html)). Therefore, using an SQS queue and scaling EC2 workers based on the number of queued items best matches the requirements.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** SNS is publish/subscribe notification, not the best fit for durably holding a backlog of jobs for worker instances. CPU usage also may not correlate with the number of jobs waiting to be processed.
- **B:** SQS is appropriate, but scaling on network usage does not directly reflect queue backlog or job demand. AWS’s documented pattern is to scale based on SQS backlog/queue messages per instance, not network usage.
- **D:** SNS does not provide the same durable work queue/backlog semantics for EC2 workers. Scaling based on messages published to a topic also does not represent the current amount of unprocessed work waiting in a queue.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在为一个将部署在 AWS 上的新无状态应用程序设计云架构。该解决方案架构师为该应用程序创建了一个 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) 和启动模板。根据需要处理的作业数量，处理必须并行运行，并根据需要添加和移除应用程序的 Amazon EC2 实例。应用程序必须松耦合。作业项必须持久存储。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题来发送需要处理的作业。使用启动模板创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，并将扩展策略设置为根据 CPU 使用率添加和移除 EC2 实例。
options.B: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列来保存需要处理的作业。使用启动模板创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，并将扩展策略设置为根据网络使用率添加和移除 EC2 实例。
options.C: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列来保存需要处理的作业。使用启动模板创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，并将扩展策略设置为根据 SQS 队列中的项目数量添加和移除 EC2 实例。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题来发送需要处理的作业。使用启动模板创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，并将扩展策略设置为根据发布到 SNS 主题的消息数量添加和移除 EC2 实例。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：C。**

该工作负载是无状态、并行且由队列驱动的。Amazon SQS 是将生产者与工作进程 EC2 实例松耦合的正确服务：AWS 将 SQS 标准队列列为适用于“将实时用户请求与密集型后台工作解耦”以及“将任务分配给多个工作节点”的场景。SQS 还会在确认消息之前，将消息冗余存储在多个 Availability Zones 中，从而持久存储消息，这满足了作业持久存储的要求（[Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)）。对于扩展，AWS 专门记录了一种 Auto Scaling 组处理来自 SQS 队列的消息，并使用基于每个实例的队列积压/队列长度的扩展策略的模式。文档描述了如何根据 `ApproximateNumberOfMessages` 队列属性计算积压，并配置目标跟踪策略，以便当积压超过目标时 Auto Scaling 组向外扩展（[Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html)）。因此，使用 SQS 队列并根据排队项目数量扩展 EC2 工作节点，最符合这些要求。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A:** SNS 是发布/订阅通知，不是为工作实例持久保存作业积压的最佳选择。CPU 使用率也可能无法与等待处理的作业数量相关联。
- **B:** SQS 是合适的，但基于网络使用率进行扩展并不能直接反映队列积压或作业需求。AWS 文档化的模式是基于 SQS 积压/每个实例的队列消息数进行扩展，而不是基于网络使用率。
- **D:** SNS 不为 EC2 工作节点提供相同的持久工作队列/积压语义。基于发布到主题的消息进行扩展，也不能表示队列中当前等待处理的未完成工作量。

en.question: A global ecommerce company uses a monolithic architecture. The company needs a solution to manage the increasing volume of product data. The solution must be scalable and have a modular service architecture. The company needs to maintain its structured database schemas. The company also needs a storage solution to store product data and product images. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group to deploy a containerized application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute web traffic. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance to store product data and product images.
options.B: Use AWS Lambda functions to manage the existing monolithic application. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store product data and product images. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for event-driven communication between the Lambda functions.
options.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with an Amazon EC2 deployment to deploy a containerized application. Use an Amazon Aurora cluster to store the product data. Use AWS Step Functions to manage workflows. Store the product images in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to deploy a containerized application. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store the product data. Store the product images in an Amazon S3 bucket.

en.explanation:
The best answer is **D**.

**Why D is correct:** Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate fits the requirement for a scalable, modular container-based architecture with low operational overhead. AWS states that Fargate lets you run containers with Amazon ECS “without having to manage servers or clusters of Amazon EC2 instances” and removes the need to provision, configure, or scale VM clusters ([AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)). Amazon RDS preserves structured relational schemas and is managed by AWS; RDS supports familiar relational engines and manages backups, patching, failure detection, and recovery ([Amazon RDS advantages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)). A Multi-AZ RDS deployment provides standby DB instances for failover support ([Amazon RDS Multi-AZ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)). Amazon S3 is the right storage service for product images because files uploaded to S3 are stored as objects, and AWS explicitly says you can upload “any file type—images, backups, data, movies, and so on” into an S3 bucket ([Uploading objects to S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/upload-objects.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A** uses EC2 instances and Auto Scaling, which requires more infrastructure management than Fargate. It also stores product images in RDS, which is not the appropriate object/file storage pattern when S3 is designed for image objects.
* **B** uses DynamoDB, but the question says the company must maintain structured database schemas. AWS contrasts relational database design with DynamoDB NoSQL design and notes that DynamoDB schemas are tailored to specific access patterns, unlike RDBMS schema design ([DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)). DynamoDB is also not the appropriate place to store product images compared with S3.
* **C** uses Amazon EKS on EC2, which adds Kubernetes and EC2 management overhead compared with ECS on Fargate. It also stores product images in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which AWS describes as archive storage for data that rarely needs access and not available for real-time access, making it unsuitable for ecommerce product images ([S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)).

zh.question: 一家全球电子商务公司使用单体架构。该公司需要一种解决方案来管理不断增加的产品数据量。该解决方案必须具备可扩展性，并具有模块化服务架构。该公司需要维护其结构化数据库架构。该公司还需要一种存储解决方案来存储产品数据和产品图片。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例来部署容器化应用程序。使用 Application Load Balancer 分发 Web 流量。使用 Amazon RDS 数据库实例存储产品数据和产品图片。
options.B: 使用 AWS Lambda 函数来管理现有的单体应用程序。使用 Amazon DynamoDB 存储产品数据和产品图片。使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 在 Lambda 函数之间进行事件驱动通信。
options.C: 使用 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 搭配 Amazon EC2 部署来部署容器化应用程序。使用 Amazon Aurora 集群存储产品数据。使用 AWS Step Functions 管理工作流。将产品图片存储在 Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive 中。
options.D: 使用 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 搭配 AWS Fargate 来部署容器化应用程序。使用具有 Multi-AZ 部署的 Amazon RDS 存储产品数据。将产品图片存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。

zh.explanation:
最佳答案是 **D**。

**为什么 D 正确：** Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate 符合对可扩展、模块化、基于容器的架构以及低运营开销的要求。AWS 表示，Fargate 使你能够使用 Amazon ECS 运行容器，“无需管理服务器或 Amazon EC2 实例集群”，并且无需预置、配置或扩展 VM 集群（[AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html)）。Amazon RDS 保留结构化关系型架构，并由 AWS 托管；RDS 支持常见的关系型引擎，并管理备份、修补、故障检测和恢复（[Amazon RDS advantages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)）。Multi-AZ RDS 部署提供备用数据库实例以支持故障转移（[Amazon RDS Multi-AZ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)）。Amazon S3 是产品图片的合适存储服务，因为上传到 S3 的文件会作为对象存储，并且 AWS 明确说明你可以将“任何文件类型——图像、备份、数据、电影等等”上传到 S3 存储桶中（[Uploading objects to S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/upload-objects.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A** 使用 EC2 实例和 Auto Scaling，与 Fargate 相比需要更多基础设施管理。它还将产品图片存储在 RDS 中，而在 S3 专为图像对象而设计的情况下，这不是合适的对象/文件存储模式。
* **B** 使用 DynamoDB，但题目说明公司必须维护结构化数据库架构。AWS 将关系型数据库设计与 DynamoDB NoSQL 设计进行对比，并指出 DynamoDB 架构是针对特定访问模式定制的，不同于 RDBMS 架构设计（[DynamoDB NoSQL design](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/bp-general-nosql-design.html)）。与 S3 相比，DynamoDB 也不是存储产品图片的合适位置。
* **C** 使用 Amazon EKS on EC2，与 ECS on Fargate 相比，会增加 Kubernetes 和 EC2 管理开销。它还将产品图片存储在 S3 Glacier Deep Archive 中，AWS 将其描述为用于很少需要访问的数据的归档存储，并且不适用于实时访问，因此不适合电子商务产品图片（[S3 Glacier storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。

en.question: A company is migrating an application from an on-premises environment to AWS. The application will store sensitive data in Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data before storing the data in Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with customer managed keys.
options.B: Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
options.C: Encrypt the data by using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
options.D: Encrypt the data by using client-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** The requirement says the company must encrypt the data **before storing the data in Amazon S3**. AWS describes client-side encryption as encrypting data locally; to encrypt objects before sending them to S3, use the Amazon S3 Encryption Client. In that model, “Amazon S3 receives your objects already encrypted” and “does not play a role in encrypting or decrypting” them ([AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html)). The S3 Encryption Client also protects data keys with a wrapping key that you define and pass to the client ([AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/what-is-s3-encryption-client.html)). Therefore, client-side encryption with customer-managed keys best meets the requirement.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. SSE-KMS** is server-side encryption. AWS defines server-side encryption as encryption “at its destination by the application or service that receives it,” and S3 encrypts the data as it writes it to disks in AWS data centers ([AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/serv-side-encryption.html)). That does not encrypt the data before S3 receives/stores it.
- **C. SSE-C** is also server-side encryption, even though the customer provides the key. It still relies on S3 to perform encryption at the destination, so it does not satisfy the “encrypt before storing in S3” requirement ([AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/serv-side-encryption.html)).
- **D. Client-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys** is not the appropriate S3 client-side model. Amazon S3 managed keys are a server-side encryption option (SSE-S3), while the S3 Encryption Client uses client-side data keys and wrapping keys supplied/defined for the client ([AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/what-is-s3-encryption-client.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司正在将一个应用程序从本地环境迁移到 AWS。该应用程序将在 Amazon S3 中存储敏感数据。公司必须在将数据存储到 Amazon S3 之前对数据进行加密。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用带有客户托管密钥的客户端加密来加密数据。
options.B: 使用带有 AWS KMS keys 的服务器端加密 (SSE-KMS) 来加密数据。
options.C: 使用带有客户提供密钥的服务器端加密 (SSE-C) 来加密数据。
options.D: 使用带有 Amazon S3 托管密钥的客户端加密来加密数据。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A。** 要求说明公司必须在**将数据存储到 Amazon S3 之前**对数据进行加密。AWS 将客户端加密描述为在本地加密数据；要在将对象发送到 S3 之前对其进行加密，请使用 Amazon S3 Encryption Client。在该模型中，“Amazon S3 receives your objects already encrypted” 并且 “does not play a role in encrypting or decrypting” 它们（[AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html)）。S3 Encryption Client 还会使用你定义并传递给客户端的包装密钥来保护数据密钥（[AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/what-is-s3-encryption-client.html)）。因此，使用客户托管密钥的客户端加密最能满足该要求。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **B. SSE-KMS** 是服务器端加密。AWS 将服务器端加密定义为“at its destination by the application or service that receives it”进行的加密，并且 S3 在将数据写入 AWS 数据中心的磁盘时对数据进行加密（[AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/serv-side-encryption.html)）。这并不会在 S3 接收/存储数据之前对数据进行加密。
- **C. SSE-C** 也是服务器端加密，即使密钥由客户提供。它仍然依赖 S3 在目标端执行加密，因此不满足“在存储到 S3 之前加密”的要求（[AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/serv-side-encryption.html)）。
- **D. Client-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys** 不是合适的 S3 客户端加密模型。Amazon S3 托管密钥是服务器端加密选项 (SSE-S3)，而 S3 Encryption Client 使用为客户端提供/定义的客户端数据密钥和包装密钥（[AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-s3-encryption-client/latest/developerguide/what-is-s3-encryption-client.html)）。

en.question: A company wants to create an Amazon EMR cluster that multiple teams will use. The company wants to ensure that each team’s big data workloads can access only the AWS services that each team needs to interact with. The company does not want the workloads to have access to Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) on the cluster’s underlying EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure interface VPC endpoints for each AWS service that the teams need. Use the required interface VPC endpoints to submit the big data workloads.
options.B: Create EMR runtime roles. Configure the cluster to use the runtime roles. Use the runtime roles to submit the big data workloads.
options.C: Create an EC2 IAM instance profile that has the required permissions for each team. Use the instance profile to submit the big data workloads.
options.D: Create an EMR security configuration that has the EnableApplicationScopedIAMRole option set to false. Use the security configuration to submit the big data workloads.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: B.**

Amazon EMR **runtime roles** are designed for per-job/per-query access control. AWS states that a runtime role is an IAM role specified when submitting a job or query to an EMR cluster, and that the job uses that role to access AWS resources. AWS also explains that runtime roles let you manage access control for each job or query individually instead of sharing the cluster’s EC2 instance profile. Most importantly for this question, AWS notes that when a runtime role is specified for an EMR step, the submitted jobs or queries **can only access resources allowed by the runtime role policies** and **can't access the Instance Metadata Service on the EC2 instances or use the EC2 instance profile** ([Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)).

Why the other options are incorrect:

- **A:** Interface VPC endpoints can provide private network connectivity to AWS services, but they do not provide per-team workload IAM isolation, and they do not by themselves prevent EMR workloads from using the EC2 instance profile or IMDS.
- **C:** An EC2 IAM instance profile is associated with the cluster’s EC2 instances. AWS specifically says that before runtime roles, EMR jobs used permissions from the instance profile, requiring the profile policies to contain the **union of all permissions** for all jobs on the cluster. That does not meet the per-team least-privilege requirement ([Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)).
- **D:** This is the opposite of what is needed. AWS documentation says that to use EMR runtime roles, the security configuration must set `EnableApplicationScopedIAMRole` to **`true`**, not `false` ([Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司希望创建一个供多个团队使用的 Amazon EMR 集群。公司希望确保每个团队的大数据工作负载只能访问该团队需要交互的 AWS 服务。公司不希望这些工作负载能够访问集群底层 EC2 实例上的 Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2)。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 为各团队需要的每个 AWS 服务配置 interface VPC endpoints。使用所需的 interface VPC endpoints 提交大数据工作负载。
options.B: 创建 EMR runtime roles。配置集群使用这些 runtime roles。使用这些 runtime roles 提交大数据工作负载。
options.C: 创建一个具有每个团队所需权限的 EC2 IAM instance profile。使用该 instance profile 提交大数据工作负载。
options.D: 创建一个 EMR security configuration，并将 EnableApplicationScopedIAMRole 选项设置为 false。使用该 security configuration 提交大数据工作负载。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：B.**

Amazon EMR **runtime roles** 专为按作业/按查询进行访问控制而设计。AWS 说明，runtime role 是在向 EMR 集群提交作业或查询时指定的 IAM role，并且该作业会使用该 role 访问 AWS 资源。AWS 还解释说，runtime roles 允许你为每个作业或查询单独管理访问控制，而不是共享集群的 EC2 instance profile。对于本题最重要的是，AWS 指出，当为 EMR step 指定 runtime role 时，提交的作业或查询**只能访问 runtime role 策略允许的资源**，并且**无法访问 EC2 实例上的 Instance Metadata Service，也无法使用 EC2 instance profile**（[Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)）。其他选项不正确的原因：

- **A:** Interface VPC endpoints 可以为 AWS 服务提供私有网络连接，但它们不提供按团队划分的工作负载 IAM 隔离，并且其本身不会阻止 EMR 工作负载使用 EC2 instance profile 或 IMDS。
- **C:** EC2 IAM instance profile 与集群的 EC2 实例相关联。AWS 明确表示，在 runtime roles 之前，EMR 作业使用来自 instance profile 的权限，这要求该 profile 策略包含集群上所有作业的**所有权限的并集**。这不满足按团队最小权限的要求（[Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)）。
- **D:** 这与所需配置相反。AWS 文档说明，要使用 EMR runtime roles，security configuration 必须将 `EnableApplicationScopedIAMRole` 设置为 **`true`**，而不是 `false`（[Runtime roles for Amazon EMR steps](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-steps-runtime-roles.html)）。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing an application that helps users fill out and submit registration forms. The solutions architect plans to use a two-tier architecture that includes a web application server tier and a worker tier. The application needs to process submitted forms quickly. The application needs to process each form exactly once. The solution must ensure that no data is lost. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
options.B: Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
options.C: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue between the web application server tier and the worker tier to store and forward form data.
options.D: Use an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create a synchronous workflow between the web application server tier and the worker tier that stores and forwards form data.

en.explanation:
**Correct answer: A.** Amazon SQS FIFO queues are specifically designed for workloads where duplicates cannot be tolerated. AWS states that FIFO queues provide **exactly-once processing**, that a message is delivered once and remains unavailable until a consumer processes and deletes it, and that duplicates are not introduced into the queue ([Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html)). SQS also stores messages redundantly across multiple Availability Zones before acknowledging them, which supports the requirement that no submitted form data is lost ([Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. API Gateway HTTP API**: HTTP API integrations connect API routes to backend resources such as Lambda, AWS service, HTTP proxy, or private integrations; they are not a durable queue for storing and forwarding work between tiers ([Create integrations for HTTP APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations.html)).
- **C. SQS standard queue**: Standard queues are highly scalable, but they provide **at-least-once** delivery. AWS notes that more than one copy of a message might be delivered, so applications must be idempotent ([Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html), [Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)). This does not meet the “process each form exactly once” requirement.
- **D. Step Functions synchronous workflow**: Synchronous Express Workflows have **at-most-once** execution and do not automatically manage idempotency; workflows do not restart if an exception occurs ([Choosing workflow type in Step Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/choosing-workflow-type.html)). This does not fit the durable store-and-forward queue requirement between a web tier and worker tier.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在设计一个应用程序，帮助用户填写并提交注册表单。解决方案架构师计划使用包含 Web 应用程序服务器层和工作线程层的双层架构。该应用程序需要快速处理提交的表单。该应用程序需要对每个表单仅处理一次。该解决方案必须确保不会丢失任何数据。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Web 应用程序服务器层和工作线程层之间使用 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO 队列来存储和转发表单数据。
options.B: 在 Web 应用程序服务器层和工作线程层之间使用 Amazon API Gateway HTTP API 来存储和转发表单数据。
options.C: 在 Web 应用程序服务器层和工作线程层之间使用 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 标准队列来存储和转发表单数据。
options.D: 使用 AWS Step Functions 工作流。在 Web 应用程序服务器层和工作线程层之间创建一个同步工作流，用于存储和转发表单数据。

zh.explanation:
**正确答案：A.** Amazon SQS FIFO 队列专为无法容忍重复项的工作负载而设计。AWS 表示，FIFO 队列提供 **exactly-once processing**，即消息会被传递一次，并在消费者处理并删除该消息之前保持不可用状态，而且不会向队列引入重复项（[Amazon SQS FIFO queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html)）。SQS 还会在确认消息之前，将消息跨多个 Availability Zones 冗余存储，这支持“不丢失已提交表单数据”的要求（[Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)）。

**其他选项错误的原因：**

- **B. API Gateway HTTP API**：HTTP API 集成将 API 路由连接到后端资源，例如 Lambda、AWS service、HTTP proxy 或 private integrations；它们不是用于在层之间存储和转发工作的持久队列（[Create integrations for HTTP APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations.html)）。
- **C.
